S2wu8zXYWH.one_liner: Likelihood-free doubly robust estimator of Best-of-N policy value using score-rank probabilities, with budget selection rules.
S2wu8zXYWH.problem: Evaluating Best-of-N policies from logged data needs density ratios that depend on unavailable response likelihoods, and larger N can amplify reward errors and cause overoptimization.
S2wu8zXYWH.method: They express the BoN density ratios through score-rank probabilities estimable from samples alone, and build a doubly robust estimator (BoN-DR) that reuses a shared auxiliary sample pool across candidate budgets. They derive two selection rules: maximize the estimated policy value, or maximize a lower confidence bound on improvement over the reference policy.
S2wu8zXYWH.key_idea: Use the order-statistic structure of Best-of-N to replace sequence likelihood ratios with score-rank U-statistic weights computed from a shared auxiliary sample pool.
S2wu8zXYWH.evidence: Asymptotic inference and efficiency proofs, plus synthetic experiments and GSM8K with multiple reference and reward models.
S2wu8zXYWH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is real and that the likelihood-free doubly robust estimator, with theoretical guarantees and clear presentation, is a strong technical contribution.
S2wu8zXYWH.main_concern: Guarantees are asymptotic only, and at large budgets (N=256) the effective sample size collapses and nominal 95% confidence intervals undercover (75%-88% on GSM8K), while the real-LLM experiments rely mainly on GSM8K.

l8cRwOCaUt.one_liner: Closes a predictive coding network into a loop so energy relaxation acts as an implicit layer trained with equilibrium propagation.
l8cRwOCaUt.problem: Predictive coding and equilibrium propagation can train arbitrary topologies but have mostly been used for feedforward networks matching backprop, not for iterative algorithmic reasoning with computation that scales at test time.
l8cRwOCaUt.method: They close a feedforward model into a loop by identifying its first and last hidden layers, so recurrent computation emerges from continuous relaxation of the energy landscape. They prove that in these circular predictive coding networks the bi-level framework of equilibrium propagation approximates the gradient update of an implicit layer.
l8cRwOCaUt.key_idea: Identify the first and last hidden layers to form a loop, so the zero-energy fixed point equals a DEQ equilibrium and EP approximates the implicit-function-theorem gradient.
l8cRwOCaUt.evidence: Theory (a theorem on equivalence with the DEQ fixed point and gradient approximation) plus experiments on image classification, medium-scale NLP tasks, Sudoku, and prefix-sum.
l8cRwOCaUt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the link between looped predictive coding, DEQs, and equilibrium propagation is well presented, relevant to physical hardware, and backed by a sound theoretical derivation.
l8cRwOCaUt.main_concern: The paper overclaims and under-cites (the circular model is an architecture, not a predictive coding credit-assignment algorithm), the Lipschitz premise of the theory is not verified for trained models, and novelty beyond combining PC, EP, and DEQ-style recurrence is limited.

U3XQbRi1eq.one_liner: Benchmark testing MLLMs on 28 spatial relations, from understanding to constrained spatial editing, over real-city GeoJSON and map images.
U3XQbRi1eq.problem: Existing MLLM spatial reasoning evaluations rely on static QA over small-scale or synthetic scenes and rarely test whether models can modify spatial configurations under explicit geometric constraints.
U3XQbRi1eq.method: GeoSpatialBench covers a taxonomy of 28 topological, directional, metric, and ordering relations over structured GeoJSON and map image inputs from six geographically diverse cities, with ground truth and constraints verified via GIS operations. Tasks escalate from relation understanding and geometric reasoning to constrained spatial editing.
U3XQbRi1eq.key_idea: Check editing outputs against explicit relation constraints via GIS operations, accepting any edit that satisfies them rather than only one reference edit.
U3XQbRi1eq.evidence: Frontier MLLMs evaluated on GeoJSON, map images, and multimodal combinations across six cities.
U3XQbRi1eq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well organized and that adding constrained spatial editing to spatial QA is a useful extension that exposes weaknesses in metric reasoning and editing.
U3XQbRi1eq.main_concern: Several findings (GeoJSON beating map images, weak metric reasoning) are expected or already reported, and the paper offers no analysis of causes or a remedy.

6mobCb4hQ7.one_liner: Semi-autoregressive continuous diffusion language models using position-dependent noise schedules, enabling variable-length generation and KV caching
6mobCb4hQ7.problem: Continuous diffusion language models lack variable-length generation and key-value cache support and still lag autoregressive and discrete diffusion quality.
6mobCb4hQ7.method: A parameterization with position-dependent noise schedules (local clocks) defines semi-autoregressive continuous DLMs, with block and sliding-window special cases and efficient training and sampling. ClockDLMs are Gaussian DLMs built on the sliding window, and Cache Grab samplers adapt accelerated-inference techniques from discrete diffusion.
6mobCb4hQ7.key_idea: Give each token position its own noise level through position-dependent schedules, so finished tokens can be cached while a sliding window denoises semi-autoregressively.
6mobCb4hQ7.evidence: ClockDLMs are evaluated on OpenWebText diffusion likelihood bounds and, trained on TinyGSM, on GSM8K against continuous baselines and semi-autoregressive discrete diffusion models; the paper reports better likelihood bounds than block SAR discrete diffusion.
6mobCb4hQ7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework comprehensive and clearly written, covering formulation, training and sampling, with strong benchmark results and practical benefits from bringing sliding-window diffusion to continuous DLMs.
6mobCb4hQ7.main_concern: The core mechanism is adapted from prior work (Diffusion Forcing, Rolling Diffusion, block discrete diffusion), and evaluation is limited to small models with efficiency measured mainly by NFE rather than wall-clock time.

hweb3jGXCJ.one_liner: Proposes normalized fraction-of-oracle (NFoO) to evaluate RL representation proxies by the downstream performance of what they select.
hweb3jGXCJ.problem: Rank correlation validates representation proxies over the whole candidate pool, but practical model selection depends only on the top choices.
hweb3jGXCJ.method: Defines NFoO, the downstream performance of the representation a proxy selects relative to the best available, and compares seven proxies (probing of reward, return, behavioral cloning, episode structure, dynamics and temporal structure, plus effective rank) under both NFoO and rank correlation in two Atari selection scenarios and for early stopping.
hweb3jGXCJ.key_idea: Score a proxy by the normalized downstream return of the representation it picks (fraction of oracle) rather than by rank correlation over the full pool.
hweb3jGXCJ.evidence: Seven proxies in two model-selection scenarios (across pretraining methods and within a single game) on Atari, plus early stopping; reviews cite 16 pretraining methods, 15 games, 2 downstream learners and over 20,000 finetuning runs.
hweb3jGXCJ.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is cut off before its results.
hweb3jGXCJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between ranking and selection is well motivated and practically relevant, and that the empirical study is extensive and clearly reported.
hweb3jGXCJ.main_concern: Novelty and generality are limited: NFoO equals one minus top-k normalized regret from offline policy selection, and the findings are confined to Atari with frozen encoders and are sensitive to the candidate pool.

RsR9OqpcE9.one_liner: Adds a lightweight pointer-network-style copy head to language models to improve in-context copying and training efficiency.
RsR9OqpcE9.problem: Transformers are assumed to copy from their inputs efficiently, yet in-context copying can be improved through explicit modeling.
RsR9OqpcE9.method: CPLMs add a lightweight Copy-Paste head, similar to pointer networks, on top of language models and are pretrained at scales from 135M to 1.7B parameters across backbones.
RsR9OqpcE9.key_idea: Mix a pointer-style copy distribution over context tokens into the LM output, which also opens an alternative gradient path past the LM-head bottleneck.
RsR9OqpcE9.evidence: Pretraining from 135M to 1.7B parameters across backbones, with window-size sweeps, sliding-window and document-memory setups, long-context and retrieval tests, zero-shot downstream evaluations and gradient-path ablations per reviews.
RsR9OqpcE9.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overhead, with no numbers.
RsR9OqpcE9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the empirical study broad and well controlled, with perplexity gains across scales and backbones, including full-attention models, at low overhead.
RsR9OqpcE9.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the design closely follows existing pointer mixtures, and the gradient-bottleneck explanation is not cleanly isolated from backbone and copy-head co-adaptation.

naRYgKObRP.one_liner: Two-temperature variational principle that jointly compresses two noisy views to maximize shared synoptic information, with closed-form Gaussian solutions.
naRYgKObRP.problem: It is unclear how to jointly compress two noisy high-dimensional views so representations keep shared structure while discarding view-specific detail, without an external teacher.
naRYgKObRP.method: Formalizes synoptic information, the bits shared between two compressed views that maximally retain what each predicts about the other, and derives exact coupled self-consistent equations for both encoders solved by an iterative algorithm. For Gaussian inputs it decomposes over canonical correlation modes with closed-form solutions.
naRYgKObRP.key_idea: Trade off compression of each view against mutual prediction via two temperatures, yielding coupled encoder equations that interpolate between canonical correlation analysis and the information bottleneck.
naRYgKObRP.evidence: Analytical derivations and phase diagrams over the two temperatures for Gaussian inputs, with visualizations of analytical results and no experiments per reviews.
naRYgKObRP.claimed_gains: not stated; this is a theory paper with no empirical numbers.
naRYgKObRP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework an elegant, unifying generalization of the Gaussian information bottleneck to two encoders, with a tractable closed-form solution and an interesting phase-transition analysis.
naRYgKObRP.main_concern: There are no experiments beyond visualizations of analytical results, optimality of CCA-aligned encoders is not established, and related work (DVSIB, Dikshtein et al.) is missed or misreported.

qLuXowoPJt.one_liner: Verification-based algorithm gives provable upper and lower bounds on exact Shapley interactions of neural networks by finding additive structure.
qLuXowoPJt.problem: Exact Shapley interactions require reasoning over exponentially many feature subsets, so they are typically estimated without provable guarantees.
qLuXowoPJt.method: A verification-based algorithm discovers additive structures in a network to bound game-theoretic explanations of any order, including sparse Fourier explanations, plus a robustness-based training scheme that encourages additive structure, and a proof that computing Shapley interactions is #P-hard even for two ReLU neurons or a single attention layer.
qLuXowoPJt.key_idea: Discover additive structure in the network by verification to bound exact interaction values, and train for robustness so that such structure is easier to find.
qLuXowoPJt.evidence: Experiments on larger models and search spaces than before, including certified interactions for a small certified-trained ViT, with an estimator benchmark and a #P-hardness proof.
qLuXowoPJt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending neural-network verification to Shapley interactions is a timely and meaningful problem and that the framework gives useful bounds before exact termination.
qLuXowoPJt.main_concern: Scalability relies on certified training, which changes the model being explained, and empirical support for broad applicability is limited (small ViT, two images, few inputs per network).

8vm8TVPHjv.one_liner: Exponentially weighted signature extends SSMs with a learnable generator, learnable clock, and higher-order iterated integrals in a single layer.
8vm8TVPHjv.problem: Standard SSMs use a restricted generator and step size and are linear in the input path within one layer, limiting the functionals a single layer can compute.
8vm8TVPHjv.method: EWS computes iterated integrals of a path with each increment weighted by the matrix exponential of a learnable generator over elapsed clock time; it solves a linear controlled differential equation, keeps signature universality and a modified Chen identity enabling parallel scan, and maps LTI SSMs, Mamba channels and Mamba-2 heads to it in closed form.
8vm8TVPHjv.key_idea: Weight signature increments by the matrix exponential of a learnable generator over a learnable clock, so SSMs are the depth-one case and higher truncation depths add non-linear path functionals.
8vm8TVPHjv.evidence: Six long time-series classification datasets, formal-language state-tracking tasks, and regression and forecasting comparisons with competing SSMs, plus synthetic validation and ablations.
8vm8TVPHjv.claimed_gains: EWS achieves the highest average accuracy and rank on six long time-series classification datasets, and at depth one matches or exceeds competing SSMs on regression and forecasting with far fewer parameters.
8vm8TVPHjv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the exponentially weighted signature is a clean, mathematically consistent generalization of SSMs with strong empirical results, notably on state tracking and with far fewer parameters.
8vm8TVPHjv.main_concern: The paper is hard to read for non-experts (dense signature and controlled-differential-equation background), and the memory cost of deeper models is deferred to the appendix.

BEwseckHht.one_liner: Adds a lateral circuit to predictive coding that learns activity correlations and implicitly inverts the Fisher matrix locally.
BEwseckHht.problem: Predictive coding's inference dynamics cost more than the learning benefit they yield, so it is not yet competitive with backpropagation.
BEwseckHht.method: Natural PC augments standard predictive coding with a lateral circuit that learns the activity correlations determining the Fisher information matrix and implicitly computes its inverse, giving exact natural-gradient learning that is local in space and time without explicit matrix inversion.
BEwseckHht.key_idea: A lateral weight matrix learns the activity Gram (Fisher) correlations and implicitly applies their inverse, so natural-gradient updates use only local signals.
BEwseckHht.evidence: Image reconstruction benchmarks and scaling to ImageNet, compared with existing PC approaches and with BP trained with AdamW and second-order optimizers, plus theory linking the method to Newton and Gauss-Newton optimization.
BEwseckHht.claimed_gains: Best sample and compute efficiency among PC approaches on all tested reconstruction benchmarks; on ImageNet it matches BP with AdamW and second-order optimizers at an order of magnitude lower computational cost and two orders of magnitude fewer training samples.
BEwseckHht.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the lateral-circuit implementation of natural gradient is elegant, biologically motivated and easy to follow, and that it addresses an important predictive coding bottleneck with substantial speedups.
BEwseckHht.main_concern: Claims outrun the evidence: results are limited to generative reconstruction with small models and mostly PC baselines, the ImageNet comparison uses different inference procedures, and lateral-weight alignment is checked only on a three-layer network.

ZOHaSrepMQ.one_liner: NEIN-TSF regulates historical irregularities in forecasting by learning teacher-derived forecast-damage ranking and support-bounded residual corrections.
ZOHaSrepMQ.problem: Forecasting models capture fine-grained history, but irregular changes may be transient noise or real regime shifts, and apparently stable patterns may lose predictive relevance beyond the input window.
ZOHaSrepMQ.method: Forecast-Damage Ranking Pretraining learns relative teacher-derived damage from matched local counterfactuals, and Supported Predictive Evidence combines retrieval, periodicity, local trends and persistence into bounded residual corrections. Horizon-Adaptive Evidence Utility calibrates correction strength by prediction position, and Chronological Forward Utility Selection picks model states on later validation data.
ZOHaSrepMQ.key_idea: Learn which historical deviations damage forecasts via counterfactual damage ranking against a teacher, then apply only bounded, evidence-supported residual corrections scaled by horizon.
ZOHaSrepMQ.evidence: Fifteen real-world benchmarks across multiple horizons, plus mechanism analyses of damage alignment and support-benefit association.
ZOHaSrepMQ.claimed_gains: Consistent MSE and MAE improvements over strong recent baselines across fifteen benchmarks; no numbers are stated.
ZOHaSrepMQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework well motivated and coherent, with cautious bounded corrections and extensive evaluation across fifteen datasets.
ZOHaSrepMQ.main_concern: Several component gains are modest and close to seed variation relative to the added multi-stage complexity, and the results do not show the gains come from regulating irregularities.

ifBcYWjpbX.one_liner: Bayesian optimization in high-dimensional latent spaces with an affine surrogate, scheduled exploration, and compressed posterior updates.
ifBcYWjpbX.problem: Generative-model latent spaces can have thousands to tens of thousands of dimensions, exceeding the evaluation budget, which breaks standard Bayesian optimization.
ifBcYWjpbX.method: SABLE uses a Bayesian affine surrogate and splits each query into an in-span component optimized by expected improvement in at most N dimensions and an off-span component whose norm follows an exploration schedule. A recompression scheme reduces information to O(M) pseudo-observations.
ifBcYWjpbX.key_idea: Prescribe the off-span norm of each query with an exploration schedule, since affine expected improvement underexplores, and compress history into pseudo-observations to bound refitting cost.
ifBcYWjpbX.evidence: Mathematical analysis of the affine-EI failure mode, ablations, a ZonalFunctionBench toy suite, and sensitivity experiments; reviewers note limited benchmark diversity.
ifBcYWjpbX.claimed_gains: Per-step time complexity of O(M^2 D + M^3 + D log D); sample-efficiency numbers are not stated in the available abstract.
ifBcYWjpbX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method carefully derived, the diagnosis of affine EI underexploration clear, and the ablations comprehensive.
ifBcYWjpbX.main_concern: Benchmarks never remove the affine signal the surrogate prefers and omit established tests of competing methods, so robustness beyond affine-friendly objectives is unproven; the schedule is also precomputed rather than adaptive.

Uad5ZyZbzM.one_liner: Measures how often LLMs replace impossible computed quantities in word problems with unjustified plausible answers.
Uad5ZyZbzM.problem: LLMs often identify an impossible intermediate value but still output a plausible answer through a modification the problem does not license.
Uad5ZyZbzM.method: Builds an English-Chinese corpus of word problems with implicit constraint violations, separating problems that license a repair from those admitting no consistent answer, with two controls per violating problem. Evaluates 17 models with an LLM judge checked against three annotators and a rule-based scorer.
Uad5ZyZbzM.key_idea: Distinguish recognizing a violated implicit constraint from responding to it appropriately, using paired controls that either make the value legal or change what it represents.
Uad5ZyZbzM.evidence: 129,600 model-prompt pairs over 17 models, with an LLM judge validated against three independent annotators and a rule-based scorer.
Uad5ZyZbzM.claimed_gains: No method gains claimed; the pooled accuracy gap to the first control is 63.2 percentage points when no repair is licensed versus 11.8 when one is.
Uad5ZyZbzM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the focus on implicit commonsense constraints, the distinction between recognizing a conflict and repairing it appropriately, and the extensive 17-model evaluation.
Uad5ZyZbzM.main_concern: Constraint types and answer formats differ between conditions, so the gap cannot be cleanly attributed to whether repair is licensed, and human versus LLM grading disagree (68.3% versus 87.8%).

lgh2yE8SLn.one_liner: Controlled component analysis of PEFT class-incremental learning: fixed experts, varied heads, routing signals, and inference rules across eight settings.
lgh2yE8SLn.problem: Existing PEFT-based class-incremental methods change several components at once (backbone, classification head, routing signal, inference rule), so it is unclear whether gains come from expert training or from the surrounding inference system.
lgh2yE8SLn.method: Holding expert training fixed, the authors vary the classification head, routing signal, and inference rule across four benchmarks and two task granularities, then apply the best readout and combination choices to experts from established methods.
lgh2yE8SLn.key_idea: Trains LoRA experts once and freezes them, then evaluates heads, routing signals, and expert-combination rules on that identical expert set, attributing performance changes to inference design.
lgh2yE8SLn.evidence: Four benchmarks and two task granularities (eight settings), twelve baselines, three seeds, a factorial grid with variance decomposition, and a transfer experiment to established methods such as InfLoRA (per reviews).
lgh2yE8SLn.claimed_gains: Reports the highest mean across eight settings for a mechanism-free learner (regularized least-squares readout, Mahalanobis-weighted expert ensembling); no numeric values are visible in the abstract.
lgh2yE8SLn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important and the design is clean and controlled (identical experts, same backbone and splits, multiple seeds), showing that inference choices substantially affect accuracy.
lgh2yE8SLn.main_concern: The mechanism-free learner is not compute-matched (one ViT pass per expert) and has hyperparameters tuned on test data, and it is unclear that conclusions transfer beyond frozen, independent experts.

BUZoqCgWXn.one_liner: Binary-choice protocol measuring how often an LLM's sycophantic judgment switches under repeated unsupported rebuttal persist at reevaluation.
BUZoqCgWXn.problem: Sycophancy evaluations typically need a reference answer and check a flip at a single stage, which misses decision-support tasks without correct answers and whether changed judgments persist.
BUZoqCgWXn.method: SOLIPS is a binary-choice protocol evaluating five models on eight benchmarks under explicit judgment criteria. It records switches toward the user's requested alternative under repeated, unsupported pressure and computes the share of switches retained at reevaluation, keeping the full conversation history and adding no new pressure.
BUZoqCgWXn.key_idea: Measure flip retention: the proportion of pressure-induced switches that remain when the model is asked again with the conversation history kept and no further pressure.
BUZoqCgWXn.evidence: Five models on eight benchmarks, including medical and legal tasks with and without reference answers (e.g., MedQA-USMLE and PrinciplismQA), under standardized rebuttal conditions.
BUZoqCgWXn.claimed_gains: Under Bare rebuttal with Medium or High reasoning, flip retention was numerically higher on the no-reference benchmark in nine of ten medical and legal comparisons; for Claude Opus 5 with High reasoning, switches were less frequent on PrinciplismQA than MedQA-USMLE (79.3% vs. 87.2%) but retention was higher (91.6% vs. 28.5%).
BUZoqCgWXn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reevaluation step and no-reference-answer tasks fill a real gap, with a carefully controlled design (shared initial responses, neutral and verification conditions) across five models and eight domains.
BUZoqCgWXn.main_concern: Without a correct answer, sycophancy cannot be separated from legitimate uncertainty on close calls, and the retained conversation history means persistence is not isolated from continued conditioning on it.

idsZMKDPIx.one_liner: Head-tail sampled softmax sums frequent tokens exactly and importance-samples the rare tail, scoring a third of the vocabulary
idsZMKDPIx.problem: Softmax cross-entropy scores every vocabulary token at every position, so the output layer takes close to a third of a step's FLOPs (28.9% in Qwen3.5-0.8B), and earlier in-batch-negative language models omitted the inverse-draw-frequency weight.
idsZMKDPIx.method: HTSS sums the K most frequent tokens exactly and weights the sampled tail by inverse draw frequency, so the normalizer estimate stays unbiased at every K. It changes only the training loss; the model and inference are unchanged.
idsZMKDPIx.key_idea: Compute the softmax normalizer exactly over the K most frequent tokens and estimate the tail with inverse-probability-weighted samples, giving an unbiased estimate of the full-softmax sum.
idsZMKDPIx.evidence: Pretraining on GPT-2 (124M) and a 304M multilingual backbone plus fine-tuning of pretrained models, supported by a theoretical analysis of unbiasedness; reviewers cite pretraining up to 828M parameters.
idsZMKDPIx.claimed_gains: On GPT-2 (124M), HTSS is 1.6% behind cross-entropy in perplexity at matched steps; at equal training compute it reaches 1.9-2.6% lower perplexity than cross-entropy and overtakes it on a 304M multilingual backbone from V = 128K.
idsZMKDPIx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a clear diagnosis (the missing log q correction) backed by theory, with matched-compute and memory gains over sampled-softmax baselines.
idsZMKDPIx.main_concern: The advantage appears at matched compute rather than matched steps and is shown only at modest scale, without multi-seed error bars, so benefit at larger scale is extrapolated.

5T8G04HDYa.one_liner: SPLICE adapts a neural-operator library to unlabeled mixed-mechanism trajectories via convex contribution inference and calibrated mechanism assignment
5T8G04HDYa.problem: Neural operator splitting needs physical mechanisms and their labels specified in advance, although real trajectories have several mechanisms acting simultaneously.
5T8G04HDYa.method: SPLICE infers each candidate operator's contribution to each trajectory by solving a convex optimization problem, alternating with a non-convex adjustment of the operators' latent representations. A calibrated test then assigns each discovered operator the mechanism it implements, and the operators compose into zero-shot simulators of unseen equations.
5T8G04HDYa.key_idea: Alternate a convex problem estimating each operator's contribution to mixed trajectories with latent-representation adaptation, then identify mechanisms with a calibrated test against reference solvers.
5T8G04HDYa.evidence: One- and two-dimensional systems and Navier-Stokes zero-shot composition compared with supervised libraries, plus an ablation against amortized assignment and analysis of detectable failure cases.
5T8G04HDYa.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that discovered operators compose close to their supervised counterparts on Navier-Stokes)
5T8G04HDYa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value identifying simultaneously acting mechanisms from unlabeled mixtures, with falsifiable identification and concrete Navier-Stokes evidence.
5T8G04HDYa.main_concern: Mechanisms must be sufficiently distinct to be identified, correct identification does not guarantee precise composition, and growth recovers only mechanisms the pretrained network already represents.

mYDDvIglKc.one_liner: Continuous Variational Synthesis trains synthesis-control models by gradient descent in continuous space, then discretizes by post-training quantization
mYDDvIglKc.problem: Chemical synthesis constraints force many parameters of variational synthesis models into a discrete space, limiting pre-training and fine-tuning.
mYDDvIglKc.method: Trains "free" variational synthesis models with stochastic gradient descent in continuous space (via a continuous relaxation), then discretizes them with post-training quantization. Reviewers note reward fine-tuning, mixtures of independent categorical distributions, and variance-reduction techniques.
mYDDvIglKc.key_idea: Relax the discrete synthesis parameters to continuous values for reward-driven gradient training, then quantize to synthesizable discrete values after training.
mYDDvIglKc.evidence: In silico experiments on peptides, antibody CDRH3s, regulatory DNA elements, and enzymes against EM VS and PGLD baselines, plus in vitro DNA synthesis and sequencing.
mYDDvIglKc.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract claims a strictly dominating quality-diversity Pareto frontier and in silico performance maintained in vitro, without figures)
mYDDvIglKc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit improved quality-diversity trade-offs over EM VS and PGLD across four design tasks and in vitro validation of the quantized, synthesized library.
mYDDvIglKc.main_concern: Reviewers question the restricted independent-categorical model family, possible reward hacking, and the unclear individual contributions of relaxation, quantization, and variance reduction.

Ty1kT3NAss.one_liner: Multi-token prediction and alternative tokenizations let transformers learn shortest-path search on graphs at scales beyond prior limits
Ty1kT3NAss.problem: Language models fail to learn shortest-path generation on unseen graphs as graphs scale, a failure the paper traces to the supervision signal and the tokenization.
Ty1kT3NAss.method: Uses multi-token prediction (MTP), backed by a choice-node and sub-path coverage analysis, to change the supervision signal, and introduces alternative tokenizations (STAN and a node-list augmentation +N) to change how graphs are encoded.
Ty1kT3NAss.key_idea: Predict multiple future tokens so supervision covers sub-paths through choice nodes, and separately re-tokenize the graph (STAN, +N); the two fixes are orthogonal.
Ty1kT3NAss.evidence: Theory plus experiments on Erdos-Renyi, Euclidean, and path-star graphs with small language models on synthetic graphs, including ablations of the motivating hypotheses.
Ty1kT3NAss.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that models consistently and stably learn the task at scales far beyond previous limits)
Ty1kT3NAss.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the choice-node formalism and sub-path coverage proof explaining why MTP helps, falsifiable ablations, and the scale and rigor of the experiments.
Ty1kT3NAss.main_concern: The mechanism behind the tokenization gains is not isolated, since the paper's own ablations contradict the motivating hypotheses for STAN and the node list.

3sHJQANwy7.one_liner: Gauge Matching makes marginal-preserving gauge freedom explicit in Gaussian flow dynamics for simulation-free latent SDE learning
3sHJQANwy7.problem: Simulation-free latent SDE training relies on posteriors with tractable one-time marginals, but marginals do not fix temporal structure, and existing parameterizations fix it implicitly, restricting the posterior family and biasing the model.
3sHJQANwy7.method: Gaussian flow dynamics build stochastic processes from smoothly evolving Gaussian marginals with explicit, parameterizable gauge degrees of freedom, admitting state-dependent diffusion and recovering every linear additive-noise SDE with a non-degenerate Gaussian initial distribution. Gauge Matching combines this with the SDE Matching objective at cost at most quadratic in the latent dimension.
3sHJQANwy7.key_idea: Parameterize the skew-symmetric gauge generator that leaves Gaussian marginals unchanged, and learn it with the SDE Matching objective rather than computing it from the prior drift.
3sHJQANwy7.evidence: A linear benchmark with a known exact posterior, nonlinear systems, and settings where Helmholtz-SDE does not apply, plus theory showing optimizing square-root factors and gauge suffices for linear SDEs.
3sHJQANwy7.claimed_gains: Comes within a nat of Helmholtz-SDE on the linear benchmark and matches it on nonlinear systems, at cost at most quadratic in latent dimension versus cubic for Helmholtz-SDE.
3sHJQANwy7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the clear theoretical framing of gauge freedom, the elegant formulation building on Helmholtz-SDE, and the comparisons that include nonlinear SDEs.
3sHJQANwy7.main_concern: Novelty over Helmholtz-SDE is limited, and the advantages in efficiency and state-dependent diffusion are mostly left to the appendix, with possibly high cost on larger systems.

CogAa0mqHD.one_liner: Proves that diffusion models cannot both overfit and generalize without exponentially many samples in the intrinsic dimension.
CogAa0mqHD.problem: It is natural to assume diffusion models, which share machinery with standard deep learning, also show benign overfitting and double descent, but this assumption is untested.
CogAa0mqHD.method: The paper proves an architecture-agnostic impossibility result, then analyses a linear random-feature model to show that score matching lacks the kernel-target alignment that helps regression. It also identifies implicit regularization from time-smoothness of the score, and early stopping, as mechanisms that prevent overfitting.
CogAa0mqHD.key_idea: Score matching lacks the kernel-target alignment that makes interpolation benign in regression, so fitting the training data is irreparably harmful unless sample size grows exponentially with intrinsic dimension.
CogAa0mqHD.evidence: A theorem covering any score estimator, a linear random-feature (two-layer linear) model analysis, and high-dimensional experiments.
CogAa0mqHD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the architecture-agnostic lower bound is a general, rigorous result and that the linear analysis gives useful explanations of overfitting and regularization in diffusion.
CogAa0mqHD.main_concern: The linear random-feature analysis is narrow and partly overlaps prior work, and the absence of benign overfitting is conflated with the absence of double descent, which the theorem does not rule out.

YpJHxdxExF.one_liner: Characterizes weak-to-strong generalization in random feature networks, showing student error scales as the square of teacher error.
YpJHxdxExF.problem: Weak-to-strong generalization, where a student trained on a weak teacher's labels beats the teacher, lacks sharp asymptotics for ReLU networks.
YpJHxdxExF.method: Random matrix theory gives deterministic equivalents for the population errors of an optimally trained teacher and a gradient-flow student in two-layer random feature networks, where width sets model strength.
YpJHxdxExF.key_idea: Use deterministic equivalents from random matrix theory to compute teacher and early-stopped gradient-flow student errors, giving sharp rates under a Gaussian universality assumption.
YpJHxdxExF.evidence: Theory for ReLU activation with a pure spherical harmonic target and multi-degree targets under a Gaussian universality assumption, plus numerical experiments per reviews.
YpJHxdxExF.claimed_gains: For ReLU and a pure spherical harmonic target, student error scales as the square of the teacher error, attaining the general lower bound of Medvedev et al. (2025).
YpJHxdxExF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical setting and exposition are clear and that the deterministic-equivalent analysis sharpens prior results, including the quadratic improvement.
YpJHxdxExF.main_concern: The contribution relative to Medvedev et al. (2025) is not clearly positioned, and two reviewers dispute a stated rate in Section 6 within the stopping-time window.

OUSIqfNRkx.one_liner: Falsification-guided self-testing trains code agents with SFT, action-level RL and trajectory rewards to write tests that expose bugs.
OUSIqfNRkx.problem: Code agents pass their own local tests yet fail held-out tests, either because tests miss bugs or because outputs that expose bugs are misread (Fix-Test Collapse).
OUSIqfNRkx.method: Falsification-Guided Self-Testing combines protocol SFT, action-level reinforcement learning and trajectory rewards under a single-trajectory interface that withholds reference outputs and hidden verdicts from the policy. Offline scorers reward diagnostic tests on contest tasks, and an issue-grounded judge updated with on-policy hard negatives supplies the signal on repository tasks.
OUSIqfNRkx.key_idea: Reward tests that falsify the agent's own patch, scored by offline references or an on-policy-updated judge, while hiding reference outputs and verdicts from the policy.
OUSIqfNRkx.evidence: Three model families on CodeContests, LiveCodeBench, SWE-bench Pro and DeepSWE, plus a matched control from an identical SFT checkpoint over three paired training seeds.
OUSIqfNRkx.claimed_gains: Pass rates improve by up to 34.7% on CodeContests and 19.5% on LiveCodeBench; Qwen3.5-35B reaches 48.3% on 731 SWE-bench Pro tasks and 28.3% on the 113-task DeepSWE split; falsification RL beats final-only RL by 7.7 points on Pro and 10.6 on DeepSWE on average.
OUSIqfNRkx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the matched post-SFT control with paired seeds and the careful separation of conditional collapse from all-instance failure.
OUSIqfNRkx.main_concern: Conditional collapse can fall simply by validating less and the paper omits coverage and all-instance counts, and repository gains are not cleanly attributed to falsification since that arm gets extra supervision.

ORg442EApD.one_liner: CARE-Attn corrects FP4 attention QAT residuals per component: high-precision QK tiles, P-exact QAT, and mean-centered V.
ORg442EApD.problem: Attn-QAT leaves a measurable quality gap for FP4 attention, and it adapts unevenly: QK error drops while P and V errors barely change.
ORg442EApD.method: The paper analyzes QK, P and V residuals separately, then recomputes predicted high-error QK tiles in higher precision under adaptive budgets, decouples training and inference precision through P-exact QAT, and removes V channel offsets with exactly compensated mean-centering.
ORg442EApD.key_idea: Match a separate correction to each residual's structure: sparse QK errors, quantizer-limited P errors, and channel-offset V errors.
ORg442EApD.evidence: Video diffusion transformers and language models, with comparisons against the released and retrained Attn-QAT, BF16 fine-tuned references, ablations, and training and attention-kernel throughput measurements.
ORg442EApD.claimed_gains: On video diffusion transformers, improves generation quality over Attn-QAT, gets closer to the BF16 fine-tuned model, and reduces QAT overhead; no numbers stated in the abstract excerpt.
ORg442EApD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the component-wise error analysis is insightful and that each correction follows clearly from it.
ORg442EApD.main_concern: Efficiency is shown only for the attention kernel and training step, not end-to-end generation or serving latency, and video results use a single seed.

vDfzO7dndH.one_liner: Self-supervised real-world dehazing that calibrates relative optical-depth shifts between haze-intervened views, then anchors absolute values by closed-form projection.
vDfzO7dndH.problem: Different combinations of transmission and clean radiance explain the same hazy image, so physical reconstruction alone cannot supervise adaptation to unlabeled real images.
vDfzO7dndH.method: Relative-State Calibration trains a teacher to match prescribed optical-depth differences between views with known transmission scaling. Absolute-State Anchoring projects the teacher's predictions onto an observation-compatible family via a per-pixel closed-form scalar solution, giving targets for a student that keeps the original backbone.
vDfzO7dndH.key_idea: Controlled haze interventions fix relative optical-depth shifts, and the one unknown absolute offset per pixel is resolved by closed-form projection onto the feasible family.
vDfzO7dndH.evidence: Experiments on six real-world benchmarks, a bound on relative optical-depth error, and a proof that anchoring does not increase weighted joint target error when the true state is feasible.
vDfzO7dndH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the split into identifiable relative information and prior-guided absolute selection insightful, with promising results and no added inference overhead.
vDfzO7dndH.main_concern: The independent contribution of ASA's projection over plain teacher-student distillation and multi-view aggregation is not isolated, and the theory assumes global atmospheric light and linear radiance.

NXCIy3ulhn.one_liner: Prior-data fitted network meta-trained on synthetic tasks built from real functional-connectivity matrices to predict behavior in one forward pass.
NXCIy3ulhn.problem: Kernel ridge regression on FC matrices needs per-score and per-cohort fitting, does not transfer, and degrades with few subjects, while brain foundation models have not consistently beaten it on continuous behavior scores.
NXCIy3ulhn.method: BrainPFN is meta-trained on a domain-specific prior built from about 7k real FC matrices, from which one billion synthetic training samples are drawn; at inference a labelled context is passed through the network in a single forward pass with no refitting.
NXCIy3ulhn.key_idea: Meta-train a PFN on synthetic regression tasks drawn from a kernel-function prior over real connectomes, so prediction is amortized in-context without per-cohort fitting.
NXCIy3ulhn.evidence: Four independent cohorts, compared with KRR and recent brain foundation models pre-trained at four to nine times larger scale.
NXCIy3ulhn.claimed_gains: Beats KRR on small-sample prediction and leads recent foundation models pre-trained at four to nine times larger scale across four independent cohorts.
NXCIy3ulhn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that handling small clinical sample sizes with an amortized, prior-data fitted approach is an interesting, valuable direction supported by experiments on multiple datasets.
NXCIy3ulhn.main_concern: Reviewers say ridge regression matches or beats BrainPFN beyond roughly 150 to 200 subjects, and that there is no interpretability or statistical analysis.

RJK3xPQTFj.one_liner: Flow matching for accelerated MRI whose source distribution and velocity field are structured by the acquisition operator during training.
RJK3xPQTFj.problem: Generative MRI reconstruction methods typically introduce acquisition operators and data consistency only at inference.
RJK3xPQTFj.method: CAST uses acquisition operators to structure both the source distribution and the velocity field during flow-matching training, so that sampling corresponds to completing missing k-space data.
RJK3xPQTFj.key_idea: Build the flow source from the zero-filled image plus noise confined to the unmeasured subspace, and project the velocity with the acquisition operator, so sampling completes missing k-space.
RJK3xPQTFj.evidence: Evaluation on 2D, 3D, cardiac cine and low-field MRI, plus prospectively acquired free-breathing cine.
RJK3xPQTFj.claimed_gains: Individual samples or averages of a few give the lowest KID, and averaging more samples matches or exceeds state-of-the-art unrolled networks in PSNR; no numbers stated.
RJK3xPQTFj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the acquisition-structured construction is principled, the evaluation is broad across anatomies and 2D and 3D settings, and the method is efficient at inference.
RJK3xPQTFj.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited relative to residual conditional flow matching and related work (e.g., HFS-SDE, MC-DDPM, null-space networks), and that ablations, error bars and baselines such as rcGAN are insufficient.

aIdrg5gk9T.one_liner: Schedule-free spectral optimizer SF-NorMuon matches tuned AdamW for language-model training without a horizon-tied learning-rate schedule.
aIdrg5gk9T.problem: Standard training depends on horizon-tied learning-rate schedules, and the schedule-free SF-AdamW consistently underperforms well-tuned AdamW.
aIdrg5gk9T.method: SF-NorMuon is a schedule-free version of the NorMuon spectral optimizer run with a single hyperparameter configuration; the authors prove a stationarity guarantee for schedule-free spectral dynamics and identify weight decay at the fast iterate as essential for long-horizon stability.
aIdrg5gk9T.key_idea: Apply schedule-free iterate averaging to the NorMuon spectral update, with weight decay at the fast iterate for stability, so any checkpoint is usable without a fixed horizon.
aIdrg5gk9T.evidence: 125M and 772M parameter language models across 1 to 8x Chinchilla horizons, plus a stationarity theorem for schedule-free spectral dynamics.
aIdrg5gk9T.claimed_gains: Matches or exceeds tuned AdamW with a single configuration and trails cosine-scheduled NorMuon by only about 0.03 nats.
aIdrg5gk9T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree anytime training matters for single-pass language-model training and that SF-NorMuon works well empirically, with supporting convergence and weight-decay analysis.
aIdrg5gk9T.main_concern: Reviewers say the theory covers SF-spectral descent with momentum rather than SF-NorMuon itself, and that a gap to tuned NorMuon and a missing comparison with the related AMUSE optimizer remain.

qJAEHVeSFS.one_liner: Theory-of-Mind benchmark on psychological manipulation dialogues with hidden intentions, covering 16 manipulation mechanisms and explicit, dynamic and applied questions.
qJAEHVeSFS.problem: Most ToM evaluations use benign settings and overlook hidden intentions and adversarial social influence, where a manipulator conceals its goal.
qJAEHVeSFS.method: ManipToM covers 16 manipulation mechanisms across cognitive, affective and identity domains, using a controlled generation pipeline that instantiates manipulative interactions, tracks agents' evolving mental states, and builds and validates questions automatically from that state; it has 645 dialogues and 13,734 questions.
qJAEHVeSFS.key_idea: Generate manipulation dialogues while explicitly tracking each agent's evolving mental state, then derive validated ToM questions from that structured state.
qJAEHVeSFS.evidence: Evaluation of nine LLMs on explicit, dynamic and applied ToM questions, including chain-of-thought prompting.
qJAEHVeSFS.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports that strong explicit mental-state performance does not extend to tracking state changes or predicting behavior, without numbers).
qJAEHVeSFS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a gap by testing ToM under psychological manipulation and that the error analysis by question type (explicit, dynamic, applied) is thorough.
qJAEHVeSFS.main_concern: Reviewers say validity is not independently established: dialogues, mental states and validation are LLM-generated with no human evaluation, and synthetic third-person QA may not reflect real social intelligence.

oodc536owR.one_liner: Restores diversity in distilled few-step diffusion models by training a tiny seed-response bias adapter on the first denoising step only.
oodc536owR.problem: Distilled student models often map different initial noises to similar outputs under the same prompt, and the largest loss of response to noise occurs at the first, high-noise step.
oodc536owR.method: ReSeed adds a seed-response bias adapter only to the first student step and aligns its velocity with the teacher's first-interval secant velocity, leaving all student weights and later denoising steps unchanged.
oodc536owR.key_idea: Train a first-step bias adapter to match the teacher's first-interval secant velocity, since replacing only the first student step with the teacher's recovers most diversity.
oodc536owR.evidence: Three text-to-image models (SD3-Medium, SD3.5-Medium, FLUX.1-dev) and one text-to-video model (Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B), plus a teacher-prefix replacement diagnostic on SD3-Medium.
oodc536owR.claimed_gains: Restores lost diversity while maintaining competitive image quality (TL;DR); for 4-step FLUX.1-dev it adds 0.00196% trainable parameters and trains on 8,000 prompt-noise pairs, with result magnitudes cut off in the abstract.
oodc536owR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the post-hoc repair of a frozen student with a tiny adapter is simple and practical, supported by a convincing teacher-prefix diagnostic and diversity gains across the image models.
oodc536owR.main_concern: Novelty is limited because prior work (Gandikota and Bau; DP-DMD) already found first-step diversity loss and used teacher-based first-step supervision, leaving the post-hoc adapter as the main new element.

hmcSnEcYXB.one_liner: Quantization-aware training with a convex compressed-size proxy that jointly balances sparsity and codebook symbol entropy.
hmcSnEcYXB.problem: Pruning and quantization shrink networks that are usually not trained to be compressible before lossless coding, and prior methods handle sparsity and symbol distribution through separate terms that act independently.
hmcSnEcYXB.method: PRESTO adds to the loss a proxy for the compressed size of the weights: the value of a convex inner problem, in perspective form, over the quantization grid learned by LSQ. A Lagrangian relaxation makes it separable and an envelope argument gives a (sub)gradient.
hmcSnEcYXB.key_idea: Add a perspective-form convex inner problem over the LSQ grid to the loss, made separable by Lagrangian relaxation, balancing sparsity and symbol distribution in one term.
hmcSnEcYXB.evidence: ImageNet experiments on ResNet-18, ResNet-50, ViT-B/16, DeiT-Small and EfficientNet-B0 with sizes measured on the whole checkpoint after lossless coding, compared with LSQ and NNCodec baselines.
hmcSnEcYXB.claimed_gains: Compression of 20.4x on ResNet-18, 19.5x on ResNet-50, 22.6x on ViT-B/16, 11.0x on DeiT-Small and 9.9x on EfficientNet-B0, above full-precision accuracy on the two ResNets and up to about 0.8 points below it on the other three.
hmcSnEcYXB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the joint formulation is well motivated and technically sound, with well-designed controlled experiments and good compression relative to the LSQ baseline.
hmcSnEcYXB.main_concern: Training is much slower than the LSQ baseline (3.3x to 12.6x per epoch), and no L1 baseline isolates the contribution of the perspective formulation.

Toj14ZUKpv.one_liner: Proves tight bounds for randomized contract scheduling, with and without interruption-time predictions, including smoothed schedules and a sequential trust-calibration game.
Toj14ZUKpv.problem: The benefits of randomization in contract scheduling for interruptible systems are largely unexplored, both without predictions and when the scheduler receives a prediction of the interruption time.
Toj14ZUKpv.method: Proves a tight lower bound on randomized schedules in the agnostic setting, then gives a lower bound and a randomized schedule with nearly matching consistency-robustness guarantees under predictions. Smoothing yields gradual degradation under prediction error, and a sequential learning game uses historical predictions to calibrate trust.
Toj14ZUKpv.key_idea: Use randomized contract schedules, optimized for the consistency-robustness tradeoff and smoothed against prediction error, to beat deterministic schedules.
Toj14ZUKpv.evidence: Theorems giving lower and upper bounds plus smoothing guarantees, and numerical experiments with synthetic multiplicative prediction noise.
Toj14ZUKpv.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract gives no numbers; reviews cite an optimal randomized acceleration ratio of approximately 2.4554).
Toj14ZUKpv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that settling the agnostic randomized lower bound and showing a better randomized consistency-robustness tradeoff than deterministic schedules fill real gaps in the literature.
Toj14ZUKpv.main_concern: The tradeoff bounds are not fully tight and partly computer-aided, the ideas build heavily on online bidding work, and experiments cover only synthetic prediction noise.

mH80MOIRnu.one_liner: Inverts a window of states to per-state turning points of a multitask stochastic interpolant, then regenerates them under observation guidance.
mH80MOIRnu.problem: Existing generative filters condition on a fixed history and assimilate only the most recent observation, so they cannot revise past states when new observations arrive and errors accumulate.
mH80MOIRnu.method: DAWIS replaces the single flow time of a state-level prior with a multitask stochastic interpolant over a window of consecutive states, each with its own flow time. An assimilation cycle inverts the window to per-state turning points and regenerates it under observation guidance, covering filtering, fixed-lag smoothing and block smoothing, and can absorb the forecast step.
mH80MOIRnu.key_idea: Give each state in a window its own flow time in a multitask interpolant, so per-state turning points control whether each state is held fixed, revised or regenerated from scratch.
mH80MOIRnu.evidence: Experiments on nonlinear systems (the abstract is cut off); reviews mention an SQG benchmark with four observation settings against many baselines and a SEVIR block-smoothing experiment.
mH80MOIRnu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that windowed inversion addresses the fixed-history limitation by revising recent states, and that one framework covering filtering, fixed-lag and block smoothing is a useful unification with thorough experiments.
mH80MOIRnu.main_concern: The posterior targeted by the sequential update is unclear, since previously assimilated states are re-guided on observations already used, and the theory covers only the block smoother under exact guidance.

h1fHUUgbUh.one_liner: Designs antibodies by searching discrete CDR-shape combinations with Bayesian optimization, using a shape-conditioned generative model of epitope-binding antibodies.
h1fHUUgbUh.problem: Antibody design in a joint space of discrete residues and continuous coordinates is feedback-inefficient, even though CDR backbones recur in a few canonical conformations.
h1fHUUgbUh.method: Experimental CDR conformations are clustered by type, length and backbone similarity into 772 shapes. A controllable generative model conditioned on a target epitope and a combination of six CDR shapes produces antibodies that bind the epitope with those conformations, and feedback-guided Bayesian optimization searches shape combinations at test time.
h1fHUUgbUh.key_idea: Search over combinations of six clustered CDR backbone shapes with Bayesian optimization, using a generator conditioned on epitope and shape tokens, instead of searching continuous coordinates.
h1fHUUgbUh.evidence: Comparison against direct generation with test-time scaling in continuous space under the same budget; reviews also mention epitope-constrained co-folding, inverse folding and multi-objective optimization.
h1fHUUgbUh.claimed_gains: Reduces CDR structural deviation by 1.87x under the same budget relative to direct generation with test-time scaling in continuous space, and matches its performance with 13x fewer evaluations.
h1fHUUgbUh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the biologically grounded discrete shape representation is well motivated, the control interface is well executed, and the framework supports several tasks with strong co-folding results.
h1fHUUgbUh.main_concern: The main efficiency comparison confounds search space, generator (with an extra trained control branch) and search algorithm, and uses native-structure-referenced CDR RMSD, so the gain cannot be attributed to the shape space alone.

ekpKJqze4k.one_liner: Learns the carre du champ operator of a process from natural perturbations, giving diffusion geometry that is observation-equivariant.
ekpKJqze4k.problem: Geometric methods use the ambient space's induced geometry, which entangles the process's true geometry with distortions introduced by indirect, arbitrary observations.
ekpKJqze4k.method: Intrinsic Geometry Matching (IGM) learns the carre du champ operator of the process from natural perturbations such as steps in a time series, so it is observation-equivariant. Because equivariance relates geometries across spaces, additional data from another space can also be used for training; the reviews describe a LogDet divergence loss.
ekpKJqze4k.key_idea: Fit the carre du champ (local covariance) of the process from naturally occurring perturbations with a LogDet loss, giving a geometry that transforms equivariantly under changes of observation.
ekpKJqze4k.evidence: Molecular dynamics, image, and video data, compared with neural and graph-based geometric tools, with held-out transition likelihood as the main metric in some tasks (per reviews).
ekpKJqze4k.claimed_gains: Reports better performance and scaling than existing neural and graph-based geometric tools on molecular dynamics, image, and video data; no numbers stated.
ekpKJqze4k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical framing is clean and well motivated, connecting stochastic processes, the carre du champ, and observation equivariance, with LogDet justified by linear congruence invariance.
ekpKJqze4k.main_concern: Experimental comparisons conflate data source with method (IGM trains on real transitions while baselines get isotropic noise, and held-out transition likelihood is IGM's own objective), so the geometry-learning advantage is not isolated.

dW4eqjqltk.one_liner: Multimodal LLM treating sonar as a native modality, with a sonar encoder, physics-aware enhancement, and reliability-aware fusion with optical features.
dW4eqjqltk.problem: Optical MLLMs degrade in turbid water and cannot model sonar's range-azimuth structure and acoustic artifacts, or adaptively exploit sonar-optical complementarity.
dW4eqjqltk.method: SonarLLM combines a sonar-specific encoder, modality-specific physics-aware feature enhancement, and reliability-aware hierarchical fusion that aligns acoustic structure with optical semantics and adjusts modality contributions as sensing quality changes. SonarBench is a paired benchmark of recognition, counting, VQA, and captioning in sonar-only, optical-only, and fusion settings.
dW4eqjqltk.key_idea: Give sonar its own encoder and range-aware enhancement, and fuse it with optics through a gate supervised by optical degradation severity.
dW4eqjqltk.evidence: SonarBench with four tasks and three input settings, holding scene and sonar fixed while varying optical degradation, plus ablations of the sonar stem, polar positional encoding, and gate.
dW4eqjqltk.claimed_gains: 72.0% macro accuracy across sonar-only recognition, counting, and VQA, outperforming the strongest baseline by 34.4 percentage points, and 68.7% under fusion, exceeding the best baseline by 25.1 points.
dW4eqjqltk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem framing is strong, a dedicated sonar pathway beats treating sonar as RGB, and the SonarBench controlled-degradation design usefully isolates cross-modal complementarity.
dW4eqjqltk.main_concern: The reliability-aware gate is only a supervised proxy for a known optical degradation parameter evaluated on the same synthetic degradation family, and its benefit over equal weighting is modest.

8P9XSKFW9N.one_liner: Fuses optical and SAR inputs for ship detection using a cross-modal density consensus that weights multiscale fusion.
8P9XSKFW9N.problem: Multimodal detectors fuse at the feature level without modeling object distribution and spatial organization, which hurts performance in dense scenes such as optical and SAR ship detection.
8P9XSKFW9N.method: DeCo maps optical and SAR observations into a shared latent density space, estimates spatially varying modality reliability to build a cross-modal density consensus, and uses it to allocate modality contributions in multiscale feature fusion. A box-aware Bayesian density objective supervises density learning through instance-level mass assignment without manual density profiles.
8P9XSKFW9N.key_idea: Estimate per-modality latent density and spatial reliability to form a consensus map that regulates fusion weights, supervised by a box-aware Bayesian mass-assignment loss.
8P9XSKFW9N.evidence: Optical-SAR ship detection on DenseShip6K and MOS-Ship with ablations on density estimation versus consensus-guided fusion (abstract truncated before results).
8P9XSKFW9N.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining optical and SAR is well motivated, that consensus in a shared distribution space is intuitive, and that DeCo outperforms existing methods on DenseShip6K and MOS-Ship with reasonably complete ablations.
8P9XSKFW9N.main_concern: The density consensus looks like a weighted sum of two features resembling ordinary adaptive fusion, density is not directly supervised or defined, and the dense-scene evidence leans on synthetic SAR data.

Rmn5gtWC7k.one_liner: Deep research agent splitting exploration and exploitation into a critic and a generator that iteratively refine an outline.
Rmn5gtWC7k.problem: Existing deep research agents merge information exploration and exploitation into one module such as an outline or report generator, limiting flexibility and optimization.
Rmn5gtWC7k.method: AgentDisCo casts deep research as adversarial optimization between a critic agent, which critiques generated outlines and refines search queries, and a generator agent, which retrieves results for the refined queries and updates the outline. The refined outline and accumulated search results go to a downstream report writer.
Rmn5gtWC7k.key_idea: Separate a critic that refines search queries from a generator that updates outlines, coordinated as a game, so exploration is not judged by the same module that exploits it.
Rmn5gtWC7k.evidence: DeepResearchBench, the new GALA benchmark built from real user interaction data, ablations, cross-model experiments, and human evaluation (per reviews); the abstract states no results.
Rmn5gtWC7k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that assigning exploration and exploitation to separate roles is intuitive and clear, with substantial improvement on DeepResearchBench and a useful new GALA benchmark.
Rmn5gtWC7k.main_concern: Evaluation may be biased by an internal SummaryQA scoring agent and possibly a judge sharing the Gemini-2.5-Pro backbone, and the critic-generator design is not clearly distinct from existing multi-agent systems.

OqrXuWcTGJ.one_liner: Training-free long-video QA that iteratively reweights a temporal frame-sampling distribution using a VLM's internal query-dependent saliency signals.
OqrXuWcTGJ.problem: Long-video understanding needs sparse, query-relevant evidence from visually redundant content, making exhaustive frame processing inefficient.
OqrXuWcTGJ.method: QSTAR starts from sparsely sampled frames, uses the VLM's internal visual reasoning signals to estimate query-dependent frame saliency, and propagates it over the timeline to refine a temporal sampling distribution until consecutive distributions change by less than a threshold. A small set of informative frames then goes to final multimodal reasoning, with optional complementary sampling and diversity-aware model fusion.
OqrXuWcTGJ.key_idea: Score frames by projecting visual-token representations onto the LM-head directions of generated answer tokens, and iteratively update the temporal sampling distribution until it converges.
OqrXuWcTGJ.evidence: Five video-understanding benchmarks against 17 open- and closed-source VLMs, with finite-round guarantees on reconstruction and sampling-distribution error; reviews cite NeXT-QA and MLVU with an InternVL3-78B backbone.
OqrXuWcTGJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using internal VLM signals for frame selection without key-frame supervision is technically interesting, lightweight, and backed by extensive benchmarks and ablations.
OqrXuWcTGJ.main_concern: The backbone comparison does not match total test-time compute (QSTAR calls the model about 3 to 3.7 times and processes more cumulative frames), and novelty over similar question-aware frame selection work is unclear.

sygOnqXQVE.one_liner: Self-evolving agent harness that captures, repairs, and derives skills from execution evidence and binds skills to context, without weight updates.
sygOnqXQVE.problem: As skill libraries grow, overlapping scopes and uneven quality complicate retrieval, and static instructions fail to generalize across task contexts.
sygOnqXQVE.method: OpenSpace uses evidence-grounded acquisition (abstracting verified methods from raw trajectories), quality-driven maintenance (integrating repairs and derivations while tracking empirical utility), and context-aware activation (binding skills to the runtime environment). The reviews describe CAPTURE, FIX, and DERIVE operations with version records.
sygOnqXQVE.key_idea: Evolve an external skill library through three coupled operations (capture, fix, derive) driven by execution evidence and tracked utility, rather than updating model weights.
sygOnqXQVE.evidence: EvoAgentBench (twelve backbone-domain settings), SkillFlow, and LiveMCPBench, compared against the strongest non-oracle baselines and published harness results.
sygOnqXQVE.claimed_gains: Outperforms the strongest non-oracle baselines across all twelve backbone-domain settings on EvoAgentBench by 5.4-34.5 percentage points and raises SkillFlow task completion from 36.14% to 42.77%.
sygOnqXQVE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the CAPTURE/FIX/DERIVE structure with evidence tracking and versioned skills is a clear, practical design with gains across multiple domains and backbones.
sygOnqXQVE.main_concern: The comparisons do not isolate skill evolution (no OpenSpace-without-evolution baseline in the main table, and the same 6.63-point evolution gain appears for Claude Code), and review, FIX/DERIVE, and quality tracking are not ablated.

71clOPyEJg.one_liner: A 1,500-image street-view benchmark for social-activity localization, plus an N-LSE confidence score and DBA evaluation for open-vocabulary detectors.
71clOPyEJg.problem: Open-vocabulary detectors are inconsistent across phrasing and overconfident in multi-label settings, and no multi-label benchmark covers individual and group activities in still street-level images.
71clOPyEJg.method: ELSA contains 1,500 manually annotated images with more than 6,000 bounding boxes. Normalized Log-Sum-Exp (N-LSE) scores a box using every label in the query rather than the single Max-Logit token, and Dynamic Box Aggregation (DBA) penalizes contradictory predictions for the same person.
71clOPyEJg.key_idea: Score detections with a normalized log-sum-exp over all query labels instead of Max-Logit, and evaluate with an algorithm that penalizes contradictory labels on one person.
71clOPyEJg.evidence: Several open-vocabulary detector families (MDETR, OWL-ViT, Detic, Grounding DINO, LLMDet) and a two-stage SigLIP 2 baseline evaluated on ELSA, with budget, temperature, and aggregation analyses.
71clOPyEJg.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports qualitatively that modern OVD models perform poorly on ELSA and that N-LSE gives less inflated rankings and better detection results.
71clOPyEJg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-label benchmark is a useful, clearly defined resource with careful evaluation design, an adequate set of tested detectors, and a well-written presentation.
71clOPyEJg.main_concern: The evaluation is narrow and under-validated: only detectors are tested (no vision-language models), DBA's reliability is not validated against human judgments, and annotation details and alternative benchmarks are lacking.

etPuFmogcJ.one_liner: Splits the entropy-minimization gradient into radial and tangential logit components and projects out conflicting radial updates for calibrated test-time adaptation.
etPuFmogcJ.problem: Entropy minimization improves accuracy under distribution shift but yields miscalibrated predictions.
etPuFmogcJ.method: After removing the softmax-invariant mean of the logits, the EM gradient is decomposed into a radial component that raises the centered-logit norm and a tangential component that changes relative class scores. CAREM projects conflicting radial gradients onto the tangential gradient's orthogonal complement and is combined with freezing later layers; direct regularization of the centered logits is the simpler alternative.
etPuFmogcJ.key_idea: Treat the tangential gradient as the accuracy driver and the radial gradient as the confidence driver, and project out the radial part that conflicts with the tangential parameter gradient.
etPuFmogcJ.evidence: Test-time adaptation experiments across several datasets and architectures (for example ViT-Base with corruptions, plus ZeroSiam as a plug-in base), per reviews; the abstract is truncated before results.
etPuFmogcJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the centered-logit radial/tangential decomposition is mathematically correct and offers an interesting geometric view, and that CAREM is simple, backward-pass-only, and adds no hyperparameters.
etPuFmogcJ.main_concern: Gains are limited or sometimes negative on a strong baseline (ZeroSiam), and it is unclear whether improvement comes from resolving gradient conflict or from changing the effective update size, with the layer-freezing choice poorly justified.

iuwZXznlaH.one_liner: Builds a shared low-rank basis from a LoRA adapter stream, choosing directions by their effect on adapter predictions.
iuwZXznlaH.problem: A stream of trained LoRA adapters needs a shared memory that preserves past solutions and supports new ones, but weight-space energy alone does not determine which directions recover task behavior.
iuwZXznlaH.method: Functional Memory of Low-rank subspaces (FML) corrects the update scale after projecting an adapter into existing directions, then uses the adapter's predictions on unlabelled task inputs to guide growth of a shared basis. Each admitted task is stored as coefficients and a global scale so the original adapter and inputs can be discarded, and previously admitted reconstructed updates stay unchanged as the basis expands.
iuwZXznlaH.key_idea: Select new shared-basis directions by their effect on the adapter's outputs on unlabelled inputs, after rescaling the projected update, rather than by retained weight energy.
iuwZXznlaH.evidence: Continual retention and basis growth over a large SNI adapter stream (a 440-adapter experiment per reviews) and several ViT image-classification benchmarks, plus target-data-free LoRA initialization and description-conditioned LoRA generation on unseen tasks.
iuwZXznlaH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the functionally motivated direction selection and scale correction are clearly motivated and coherent, with append-only basis growth preserving admitted tasks and a more compact basis than weight-based selection.
iuwZXznlaH.main_concern: The sources of gains are not isolated (some downstream scores equal the baseline without global rank allocation), and the comparisons may use different adapter streams and protocols, with resource benefits not fully quantified.

YZBzeHixEZ.one_liner: A Lean 4 library formalizing 30 papers on language generation in the limit, used for case studies and LLM experiments.
YZBzeHixEZ.problem: Language generation in the limit is a young, fast-moving theory field whose literature lacks a shared, machine-checkable formal structure for reuse and AI-assisted research.
YZBzeHixEZ.method: GenLimitLib is a source-aligned Lean 4 library with formal developments for 30 papers. It extracts shared definitions and reusable proof components while keeping paper-specific assumptions and statements, and records relationships across papers.
YZBzeHixEZ.key_idea: Factor shared definitions and proof components into a common Lean library while retaining each paper's own assumptions, with explicit cross-paper links.
YZBzeHixEZ.evidence: Mathematical case studies (a repaired gap in a published proof, a construction transferred between papers, and a special case of an open problem) and LLM proof-generation experiments with and without library material on five theorem tasks.
YZBzeHixEZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the library is timely, reusable infrastructure whose case studies show value beyond collecting results, with explicit formalization boundaries and meaningful experimental controls.
YZBzeHixEZ.main_concern: Soundness reporting is thin: the audit of formalized claims and source alignment is unclear, and the LLM evidence rests on only five library-informed theorem tasks, one of which drives most of the gain.

vI9sDMoXj0.one_liner: fMRI video encoding model with per-parcel cross-attention that routes V-JEPA-2 features jointly over space and time to predict voxel responses.
vI9sDMoXj0.problem: Most video-computable encoding models use simple linear mappings from model tokens and ignore the spatiotemporal structure shared by video representations and neural responses.
vI9sDMoXj0.method: Per-parcel cross-attention dynamically routes features from a self-supervised video model (V-JEPA-2) across space and time, and is fit to fMRI responses to short video clips. Joint spatiotemporal attention is compared with factorized and selectively constrained alternatives.
vI9sDMoXj0.key_idea: Use per-parcel cross-attention queries to select spatial and temporal positions of video-model tokens jointly, yielding stimulus-specific attention maps for each cortical parcel.
vI9sDMoXj0.evidence: Held-out video prediction of fMRI responses across higher visual regions with spatial, temporal, factorized, and joint routing variants matched on backbone, readout, and training, across backbones, layers, and subjects.
vI9sDMoXj0.claimed_gains: Joint routing improves predictions of brain responses to held-out videos across higher visual regions, most consistently in lateral and dorsal areas; no numbers stated.
vI9sDMoXj0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matched comparison of spatial, temporal, factorized, and joint routing is the paper's strength, with consistent improvement in lateral visual cortex (for example MT and EBA).
vI9sDMoXj0.main_concern: Temporal claims are weakly constrained because fMRI gives one response amplitude per voxel per 3-second clip, and the model-selection protocol may have used test-set scores while atlas granularity is untested.

xggDEhWFpH.one_liner: A coding-RL testbed with deliberately exposed loopholes, execution-based gold labels, and controls for initial hacking tendency and reward difficulty.
xggDEhWFpH.problem: Reward hacking in RLVR is hard to monitor and mitigate because few testbeds reproduce hacking and reliably identify it.
xggDEhWFpH.method: CATCH exposes environmental loopholes and labels hacking by comparing success under a vulnerable evaluator with task correctness under an independent audit. It controls the model's initial hacking tendency through SFT data mixtures and reward difficulty through reward design, and evaluates detection and mitigation methods.
xggDEhWFpH.key_idea: Label hacking from the gap between a vulnerable evaluator and an independent audit, and independently control initial hacking tendency and reward difficulty.
xggDEhWFpH.evidence: RL training trajectories in one coding environment with a Qwen3-4B model (per reviews), plus evaluation of chain-of-thought monitoring and other detection and mitigation methods including a chi-squared mitigation.
xggDEhWFpH.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that a chain-of-thought monitor initially suppresses hacking but its protection erodes as training proceeds (abstract truncated).
xggDEhWFpH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controllable setup with detector-independent gold labels and separate control of hacking tendency and reward difficulty is a useful testbed for studying monitors and mitigations during RL.
xggDEhWFpH.main_concern: All results come from a single coding environment and a single Qwen3-4B model, and hacking is taught through SFT rather than emerging naturally, so findings may not generalize.

R037Bt6wPM.one_liner: Adaptive vertex-ordering propagation achieves exact community recovery in geometric hidden community models without spatial discretization.
R037Bt6wPM.problem: Earlier exact-recovery algorithms for the Geometric Hidden Community Model rely on spatial blocks with a chosen block size and stronger witness requirements, which exclude models such as symmetric ones with three or more communities.
R037Bt6wPM.method: The algorithm uses the information a labeled neighbor carries about community pairs to choose which vertex to label next, with no spatial blocks. It assumes observed locations and known model parameters, and a fast initializer with a guarantee is given for the constant symmetric model.
R037Bt6wPM.key_idea: Choose the next vertex to label adaptively by how informative its already-labeled neighbors are, replacing spatial blocks with information-based propagation ordering.
R037Bt6wPM.evidence: Proofs of polynomial-time exact recovery under conditions on informative-neighbor density plus initialization and regularity assumptions; experiments compare propagation errors against spatial and count-based orderings and test parameters estimated from the initial region.
R037Bt6wPM.claimed_gains: For symmetric models in dimension at least two the guarantee matches the information-theoretic threshold, and the ordering makes fewer propagation errors than spatial and count-based orderings in most tested settings (no numbers stated).
R037Bt6wPM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theory weakens the earlier all-witness requirement, covers broader models including symmetric multi-community ones, and that the information-based propagation is sound.
R037Bt6wPM.main_concern: The proven algorithm assumes known parameters and an exhaustive-MAP initializer with a possibly large polynomial exponent, and reviewers question practical deployability and the broader significance of the specialized model.

8w2dqQfiH3.one_liner: LLM agent synthesizes Lyapunov and barrier certificates, routing proof obligations to SMT solvers or Lean proof repair.
8w2dqQfiH3.problem: Synthesizing and verifying Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates for nonlinear, high-dimensional systems is hard, existing verifiers are conservative or scale poorly, and benchmarks favor low-dimensional polynomial systems.
8w2dqQfiH3.method: An LLM proposes candidate certificates and each resulting proof obligation is routed to an SMT solver or to a Lean Proof-Repair agent. The paper also introduces DynaCertBench, 105 instances built from 80 non-redundant literature systems plus high-dimensional, control-constrained, and new coupled variants.
8w2dqQfiH3.key_idea: Verify each certificate obligation separately, keeping SMT successes and sending only unresolved obligations to an LLM Lean proof-generation-and-repair agent.
