8w2dqQfiH3.evidence: Evaluation on DynaCertBench with an SMT-only ablation of the framework; reviewers also note results on previously unresolved BarrierBench systems.
8w2dqQfiH3.claimed_gains: LLM2Cert verifies 81 of 105 instances (77.1%), a 16.2 percentage point improvement over a baseline whose name is cut off in the abstract.
8w2dqQfiH3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value combining SMT checks with Lean-checked LLM proofs at the level of individual obligations and the broad DynaCertBench benchmark.
8w2dqQfiH3.main_concern: The gain over prior LLM-based certificate synthesis such as the BarrierBench pipeline is unclear because the ablation uses only an SMT-only variant of LLM2Cert, and some reported counts are inconsistent across tables.

ONtFnsNZzW.one_liner: Scales hyperparameters with model size and epochs and adds ensembling as a third axis for data-constrained LLM training.
ONtFnsNZzW.problem: Existing data-constrained scaling prescriptions hold hyperparameters such as weight decay fixed across scales and ignore ensembling as a scaling axis.
ONtFnsNZzW.method: The method prescribes how to scale key hyperparameters and how to allocate compute among epochs, model parameters, and ensemble members, using a parametric form for hyperparameter scaling.
ONtFnsNZzW.key_idea: Fit parametric hyperparameter scaling rules across model size and epochs, then split compute among epochs, model size, and ensemble members.
ONtFnsNZzW.evidence: Controlled comparisons of validation loss against existing baselines at fixed training corpus size and compute budgets; the abstract does not name datasets or model sizes.
ONtFnsNZzW.claimed_gains: Significantly lower validation loss than existing baselines, with a gap that grows at larger scales (no numbers stated).
ONtFnsNZzW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated, the experimentation careful and clearly written, and the hyperparameter-scaling analysis valuable.
ONtFnsNZzW.main_concern: Ensembling is questioned as a realistic scaling axis because inference memory grows with members, and the differences from prior work that also varies hyperparameters and ensembles are not made clear.

yFJbbGKKEs.one_liner: MASH optimizes multi-agent harnesses at node, edge, and graph levels via root-cause failure diagnosis and staged constraint filtering.
yFJbbGKKEs.problem: Manual harness design is labor-intensive and automatic generation focuses on individual agents, missing inter-agent and group-level failures, while extending the diagnose-and-repair loop across levels causes duplicate diagnoses and constraint candidate explosion.
yFJbbGKKEs.method: Structured failure diagnosis traces symptoms to shared gaps between the information a decision requires and receives. MASH then generates coordinated cross-level constraints for each diagnosed failure and applies progressively more expensive quality checks.
yFJbbGKKEs.key_idea: Trace failure symptoms to shared gaps between information needed and received to dedupe diagnoses, then screen cross-level constraint candidates with increasingly costly checks.
yFJbbGKKEs.evidence: Experiments on four benchmarks including Finance-Agent against baselines such as Meta-Harness, with analyses of which levels the accepted fixes touch and a node-only edit ablation.
yFJbbGKKEs.claimed_gains: not stated (a review mentions gains of up to 5.3 points in a workflow where agents do not exchange messages).
yFJbbGKKEs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the node, edge, and graph framing is clear and well motivated and that the experiments show improvements for multi-agent systems.
yFJbbGKKEs.main_concern: It is unclear whether gains come from the node/edge/graph idea or from the general optimization setup, and results lack uncertainty estimates or repeated optimization runs.

BgPQgWKsdP.one_liner: Simulated study participants grounded in social theory evaluate AI interviewers, with simulation scores validated against human studies.
BgPQgWKsdP.problem: Evaluating AI interviewers is hard because they operate in extended multi-turn interactions where they must adapt to participant behavior.
BgPQgWKsdP.method: InterviewPlayground simulates participants whose behaviors are grounded in social theory (traits, memory construction) and produces an InterviewReportCard that scores each AI interviewer on a suite of validated measures.
BgPQgWKsdP.key_idea: Simulated participants with trait-dependent behavior and noisy memory retrieval, scored on validated measures, serve as a proxy for human interview studies.
BgPQgWKsdP.evidence: 15 real qualitative studies with five AI interviewers, three interview topics, and 450 human participants, compared against matching simulated studies.
BgPQgWKsdP.claimed_gains: Interviewer performance in simulation predicts performance in human studies with an average Pearson correlation of 0.86 across 12 measures.
BgPQgWKsdP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the substantial human validation with 450 participants and the social-science grounding of the simulated participants.
BgPQgWKsdP.main_concern: The 0.86 correlation may reflect pooling across studies or other confounds, and the system lacks ablations showing which components matter.

tIrGxQ9xFX.one_liner: Jointly denoises future video and query-based 3D trajectories in a Mixture-of-Transformers world model under rectified flow.
tIrGxQ9xFX.problem: Video world models leave 3D dynamics implicit, action-based formulations are tied to specific robot configurations, and flow-only 3D motion models give a limited learning signal for physical dynamics.
tIrGxQ9xFX.method: 3D motion is parameterized as continuous displacement tokens aligned with the video grid, and a unified Mixture-of-Transformers backbone denoises video and motion together with a rectified-flow objective. The model is trained on 1.44 million object-level samples from simulated and real domains.
tIrGxQ9xFX.key_idea: Represent 3D motion as displacement tokens aligned with the video grid so one Mixture-of-Transformers denoises video and trajectories together.
tIrGxQ9xFX.evidence: Trained on 1.44 million object-level samples and evaluated on WorldFlowBench's three evaluation sets, including SpatialCog, against video-generation-plus-tracking and direct flow-generation baselines.
tIrGxQ9xFX.claimed_gains: WorldFlow reaches the lowest ADE and FDE among evaluated learning-based methods on all three evaluation sets, and on SpatialCog the joint model reduces ADE by 55.9% (the FDE figure is cut off).
tIrGxQ9xFX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating 3D flow as an explicit generative modality alongside video is well motivated and that the data scale and baseline comparisons make the study broader than one benchmark.
tIrGxQ9xFX.main_concern: Evaluation is limited to the authors' own WorldFlowBench, and a static zero-flow reference excluded from ranking beats WorldFlow on some Real3 metrics, so margins and generalization are unclear.

vkkZQI800a.one_liner: Streams the KV cache forward across compaction steps instead of flushing it, speeding agentic RL training.
vkkZQI800a.problem: Most context compaction strategies for long-horizon agentic LLMs prefill the context many times over, which limits training throughput.
vkkZQI800a.method: KV-streams is a plug-and-play strategy compatible with any compaction strategy that keeps and streams the KV cache forward rather than flushing it after each compaction, with a custom attention mask keeping training consistent with inference.
vkkZQI800a.key_idea: Retain the KV cache across compactions, with attention masks matching inference, so context need not be re-prefilled after each compaction.
vkkZQI800a.evidence: Three compaction strategies including SWE-bench Verified workloads, plus a controlled setting showing the streamed KV cache can act as a recurrent state learned by RL alone.
vkkZQI800a.claimed_gains: A 2.6 to 5x wall-clock training speedup across three compaction strategies, with no evidence of hindering performance.
vkkZQI800a.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method simple and practically useful, with experiments across several compaction strategies and realistic workloads showing meaningful training-time gains.
vkkZQI800a.main_concern: Novelty over prior KV-retention work such as MEMENTO is unclear, and KV-cache consistency, long-term training stability, and the recurrent-state claim are not fully verified.

6Wr00SZDjl.one_liner: Benchmark that holds forecasting history fixed while varying future scenarios to test whether multimodal forecasters respond appropriately.
6Wr00SZDjl.problem: Accuracy alone does not show whether multimodal time series forecasters use external information appropriately; models may ignore relevant information, fail to separate scenarios, or overreact to weak signals.
6Wr00SZDjl.method: WIT builds controlled scenario sets that fix the forecasting state and systematically vary future scenarios, enabling Factual, Relational, and Grounded Comparison evaluations.
6Wr00SZDjl.key_idea: Compare each scenario's forecast with the model's own neutral forecast under a fixed history, checking expected direction, contrast, intensity, and restraint relations.
6Wr00SZDjl.evidence: Experiments on multimodal forecasting models; reviewers state the benchmark has 114 forecast instances from three domains, with Grounded Comparison covering 20 of 3,078 alternative pairs.
6Wr00SZDjl.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports only that factual accuracy gains do not consistently translate into appropriate responses to alternative scenarios.
6Wr00SZDjl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating responses to alternative scenarios beyond factual accuracy is a sound, well-motivated reframing that yields non-obvious findings.
6Wr00SZDjl.main_concern: The relation labels and scenario assessments are LLM-assisted with no human audit, the grounded check covers only 20 of 3,078 pairs, and the benchmark is small.

jGZZsA2wTr.one_liner: Scores trajectory tailness by autoencoder reconstruction error across motion, social, and topology dimensions, then conditions decoding on tail prompts.
jGZZsA2wTr.problem: Trajectory prediction models underperform on rare safety-critical scenarios, and existing long-tail methods measure tailness along a single dimension and overlook the decoding stage.
jGZZsA2wTr.method: Tail samples are treated as anomalies relative to head-dominant patterns and scored with autoencoder reconstruction errors on motion dynamics, social interactions, and topological constraints. Dimension-wise contrastive learning shapes representations and a prompt-guided decoder generates prompts from the tailness estimates.
jGZZsA2wTr.key_idea: Use autoencoder reconstruction error against head-dominant patterns as a per-dimension tailness score that drives contrastive learning and prompts steering the decoder.
jGZZsA2wTr.evidence: Experiments on Argoverse2 and nuScenes under several tail criteria, including KF-error and state-based criteria, with ablations of the components.
jGZZsA2wTr.claimed_gains: not stated (reviews cite a nuScenes KF Top-1% minFDE improvement from 7.67 to 5.61).
jGZZsA2wTr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the decomposition into motion, interaction, and topology tailness and the prompt-guided decoding as sensible, with evaluation on two datasets.
jGZZsA2wTr.main_concern: The framework combines components with existing precedents (autoencoder anomaly detection, contrastive learning, prompt pools), so novelty is compositional and the benefit of each design choice is not isolated.

q3rmY8FPcu.one_liner: Graph diffusion model with constraint correction at each reverse step generates feasible discrete decisions for mixed-integer optimization.
q3rmY8FPcu.problem: Mixed-integer problems require jointly choosing discrete and continuous decisions under complex combinatorial constraints, and online combinatorial search over the binary variables is costly.
q3rmY8FPcu.method: CGD learns a conditional distribution over discrete decisions with a graph-based diffusion model on continuous relaxations, injecting constraint information into reverse diffusion to steer predictions toward feasibility. After the discrete decision is recovered and fixed, a numerical optimizer solves the remaining continuous problem.
q3rmY8FPcu.key_idea: Correct intermediate diffusion predictions toward the feasible region at every reverse step on relaxed binaries, then fix discrete values and solve the continuous part numerically.
q3rmY8FPcu.evidence: Experiments on AC-OPF with branch switching and discrete portfolio optimization, compared with learning-based baselines and MIP solvers, plus ablations.
q3rmY8FPcu.claimed_gains: Substantial improvements in feasibility and solution quality over learning-based baselines, with speedups of up to 543x over MIP solvers on large instances.
q3rmY8FPcu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating discrete and continuous variables and correcting predictions inside the diffusion process is well motivated, with promising results and well-targeted ablations.
q3rmY8FPcu.main_concern: Novelty is incremental relative to prior work on constraint projection in diffusion models for MILPs, recent baselines are missing, and the theory covers only exact convex projection.

Bz7nWBpnu6.one_liner: Latent-space multi-task offline RL for urban decisions with masked-autoencoder semi-supervised reward learning and policy fusion.
Bz7nWBpnu6.problem: Offline RL for realistic multi-task urban decision-making is underexplored, with sparse reward labels in the target task, implicit rewards, and high-dimensional states.
Bz7nWBpnu6.method: MORSE compresses urban states into a latent space and trains a trajectory masked autoencoder (TrajMAE) with a reward ensemble network in a semi-supervised way, using sparse labeled target data and abundant unlabeled related-task data. The learned reward is then used to relabel data, followed by adaptive knowledge fusion across policies.
Bz7nWBpnu6.key_idea: Train a trajectory masked autoencoder with a reward ensemble on labeled and unlabeled trajectories, then relabel cross-task data with the learned reward.
Bz7nWBpnu6.evidence: Evaluation in a learned passenger-seeking simulator built from an ensemble of seven dynamics models, as described in the reviews; the abstract text is cut off before the results.
Bz7nWBpnu6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the sparse-reward, multi-task urban offline RL setting is practically relevant and that state compression, semi-supervised reward learning, and policy fusion form a coherent framework.
Bz7nWBpnu6.main_concern: Reviewers raise paper-code discrepancies, doubts about the validity of the retrospective reward formulation, and reliance on a learned simulator for all evaluation.

UD6qMQOhR0.one_liner: Sequential Shapley credit assignment scores search-agent steps by interaction and sequential dependency, integrated with GRPO as SPGRPO.
UD6qMQOhR0.problem: Assigning informative scores to intermediate search steps without a critic model must capture both evidence interaction effects and sequential dependencies between steps.
UD6qMQOhR0.method: Sequential Shapley evaluates each subset of search steps through a continuation-induced closure within the observed trajectory; coalition values model sequential dependencies via expected future contributions and Shapley attribution aggregates marginal contributions across coalitions. The resulting step rewards are combined with GRPO to form SPGRPO.
UD6qMQOhR0.key_idea: Define coalition value through a continuation-induced closure within the trajectory, then take Shapley attribution over search steps to obtain step-level rewards.
UD6qMQOhR0.evidence: Seven search-augmented QA benchmarks with Qwen2.5-3B and 7B, ablations against standard Shapley and IGPO, and theory relating Sequential Shapley to standard Shapley with a backward-redistribution interpretation.
UD6qMQOhR0.claimed_gains: SPGRPO improves average success rates over the strongest baseline by 2.8 and 1.4 percentage points for Qwen2.5-3B and 7B, respectively.
UD6qMQOhR0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the sequential Shapley formulation reasonable and theoretically supported, with consistent average gains across seven QA benchmarks.
UD6qMQOhR0.main_concern: Novelty is overclaimed because SSVPO already formulated sequential Shapley credit assignment for LLM reasoning, and the continuation model uses length-normalized likelihoods with substantial calibration errors and modest gains over standard Shapley.

RODTcb3w1P.one_liner: Converts reference patches into replay-verified, access-isolated training trajectories for software engineering agents via plan repair and redundancy slicing.
RODTcb3w1P.problem: Reference patches do not provide reliable interaction traces for training software engineering agents, since rejection sampling discards failed attempts and patch-conditioned traces can contain unsupported reasoning and redundant steps.
RODTcb3w1P.method: ASSERT separates privileged plan recovery from the execution evidence that justifies supervised decisions. DCTR repairs failed plans within dependency regions identified by failure feedback, RCDS removes redundant interactions under evidence, replay, and final-test constraints, a patch-blind runner supplies observations, and an isolated rationale writer explains fixed actions.
RODTcb3w1P.key_idea: Recover plans with patch access but justify each supervised action only with replayed, patch-blind execution evidence, after repairing failed plans and slicing redundant steps.
RODTcb3w1P.evidence: SWE-bench Verified and Multi-SWE-bench with GPT-5.5 and GLM-5.2 teachers, student training at matched task coverage, and ablations of the repair and slicing components.
RODTcb3w1P.claimed_gains: With GPT-5.5 and GLM-5.2 teachers, ASSERT retains up to 2.93 times as many trajectories as the largest baseline pool and improves student Pass@1 by up to 5.84 percentage points over the strongest baseline in each setting.
RODTcb3w1P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practical and that gains are consistent across two teachers and two languages, with matched-task experiments and ablations supporting the components.
RODTcb3w1P.main_concern: The conceptual advance over prior reference-patch-guided methods such as P2T is unclear, and the advantage over simply spending the same construction budget on more rejection sampling is not established.

5kXox7ovrd.one_liner: Continuous adversarial training pushes LLMs toward honest answers and away from dishonest ones, transferring across honesty benchmarks.
5kXox7ovrd.problem: Despite alignment training, LLMs still output claims that contradict some knowledge or are unsupported by what is accessible in context.
5kXox7ovrd.method: CATCH, inspired by a method for robustly refusing harmful queries, trains the model toward an honest answer and away from a dishonest one with adversarial perturbations while maintaining capabilities. It uses hundreds of targets built from self-reporting scenarios and a new approach to generating utility data.
5kXox7ovrd.key_idea: Train toward honest and away from dishonest answers under continuous adversarial perturbations, with self-reporting scenario targets and generated utility data preserving capabilities.
5kXox7ovrd.evidence: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and Qwen3-3.6-27B evaluated on MASK, the multi-agent game Among Us, and AuditBench, compared with prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and honesty activation steering.
5kXox7ovrd.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract says CATCH outperforms prompting and supervised fine-tuning, is on par with honesty activation steering, and surpasses steering in maintaining utility.
5kXox7ovrd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree there is substantial evidence of transfer across distinct dishonesty settings (MASK, Among Us, AuditBench) and that the controls guard against trivial success.
5kXox7ovrd.main_concern: Honesty results are inconsistent across tables (86.0 and 90.7 versus 73.9 and 74.1 for the same utility scores), and evaluation covers only two architectures with no multi-seed results.

AenXyGuGX8.one_liner: Quantization for VLA models that picks activation precision by execution step and compensates rotation drift using accumulated quantization residuals.
AenXyGuGX8.problem: Existing VLA quantization trades inference speed against performance without studying how quantization alters runtime errors, which show wider translation-error variance and cumulative rotation drift in closed-loop execution.
AenXyGuGX8.method: DyQ-VLA dynamically selects activation precision according to execution steps and tracks and compensates rotation errors via accumulated quantization residuals, with operators and runtime adaptation strategies built for dynamic-precision execution.
AenXyGuGX8.key_idea: Vary activation bit-width per execution step to limit translation-error dispersion, and use accumulated quantization residuals to cancel cumulative rotation drift.
AenXyGuGX8.evidence: Simulation benchmarks and real-world robotic tasks (ten trials per task, per a review), compared with other VLA quantization methods such as ActQuant and HoloQ-VLA.
AenXyGuGX8.claimed_gains: 1.88x to 1.93x inference speedups with comparable or higher average task success rates, and mean execution steps reduced by 17.7% to 19.8%.
AenXyGuGX8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method clearly presented and motivated by a closed-loop view of quantization error, with evaluation across simulation and real robots.
AenXyGuGX8.main_concern: Real-world evidence is thin at ten trials per task, and the runtime-error definition (deviation from a reference trajectory) and the speed-accuracy tradeoff of dynamic precision are not fully justified.

UaZP4CzI6V.one_liner: Tests whether regular numeral systems are easier for LSTM learners to generalize from skewed data, under RL and supervised training.
UaZP4CzI6V.problem: It is unclear what pressures during linguistic evolution select for the regularity of human recursive numeral systems.
UaZP4CzI6V.method: The authors compile 20,732 numeral systems (human and artificial) and train learners with reinforcement and supervised learning as analogues of human learning, measuring how well each derives a generalisable representation of the whole system from skewed, limited data.
UaZP4CzI6V.key_idea: Define learnability as generalizing from scarce, skewed input to the whole numeral system, and compare regular human-like systems against irregular unattested ones.
UaZP4CzI6V.evidence: A dataset of 20,732 numeral systems with reinforcement and supervised learners (LSTMs, per the reviews), different training and test distributions, and exploratory analyses of factors affecting learnability.
UaZP4CzI6V.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that regular human-like systems are more learnable than irregular ones only under the generalisation-based measure, with a larger advantage for reinforcement learning.
UaZP4CzI6V.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the link between regularity, learnability, and linguistic evolution interesting and the large collection of systems and training/test distributions informative.
UaZP4CzI6V.main_concern: Only LSTM learners are tested and the generalization test uses less frequent numbers rather than held-out ones, so it is unclear the conclusions extend beyond this architecture or offer non-obvious insight.

xatSW5dTU9.one_liner: Natural actor-critic for concave general-utility RL learns the policy-gradient pseudo-reward directly with a neural critic and multilevel Monte Carlo.
xatSW5dTU9.problem: RL with general utilities optimizes nonlinear functionals of occupancy measures, and approaches that first estimate the occupancy measure are hard to scale to large or infinite state-action spaces.
xatSW5dTU9.method: A natural actor-critic for concave objectives with an exact variational dual representation learns the pseudo-reward as a function of the state-action pair with a neural critic trained by projected stochastic updates. Multilevel Monte Carlo combines outputs across training horizons to control critic bias at logarithmic expected cost.
xatSW5dTU9.key_idea: Learn the occupancy-based pseudo-reward directly as a state-action function with a neural critic, and control critic bias with multilevel Monte Carlo over horizons.
xatSW5dTU9.evidence: Theoretical convergence and sample-complexity analysis that accounts for dual optimization, critic approximation, and neural linearization errors under policy-transfer, dual-stability, and local critic-regularity conditions; no experiments appear in the visible abstract.
xatSW5dTU9.claimed_gains: The method achieves O~(T^-1/2) global convergence using O~(T) expected transitions and reference samples, giving O~(epsilon^-2) sampling complexity above the approximation floor for a fixed critic representation.
xatSW5dTU9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the algorithm avoids explicit occupancy-density estimation and that the theoretical analysis is thorough and technically sound.
xatSW5dTU9.main_concern: Reviewers question the positioning against the closest prior work (Barakat et al.) and the novelty relative to existing MLMC natural policy gradient techniques, and note that the guarantee rests on many assumptions of unclear validity.

FqSwKEkUG1.one_liner: Interventions on SIREN weights show Meta Weight Transformer classifiers rely mainly on per-neuron biases encoding coarse color and brightness.
FqSwKEkUG1.problem: Existing measures of class structure in INR parameters show what can be read from the parameters, not what a classifier uses, so why Meta Weight Transformer classifiers work is unclear.
FqSwKEkUG1.method: This is an analysis rather than a new method: nearest-neighbor and nearest-centroid readouts are compared with trained classifiers across six MWT training configurations, then classifier inputs are altered without retraining (for example replacing biases with layer means) and the low-dimensional bias variation is analyzed.
FqSwKEkUG1.key_idea: Intervene on the inputs of trained MWT classifiers by replacing biases or same-sized weight columns with layer means to find which parameters carry class information.
FqSwKEkUG1.evidence: Six MWT training configurations, readout comparisons, input interventions without retraining, and PCA-based analysis, on small 10-class image datasets according to the reviews.
FqSwKEkUG1.claimed_gains: Biases make up less than 0.4% of the classifier input, yet replacing them by layer means lowers accuracy by 16.3 points on average, versus 0.3 for the same change to a weight column of the same size.
FqSwKEkUG1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the finding that per-neuron biases carry class information interesting and supported by broad experiments and interventions.
FqSwKEkUG1.main_concern: Configurations change several factors at once with no clean ablations, the study covers only small 10-class datasets, and the interventions are handcrafted.

KHQHyObYrJ.one_liner: Training-free retrieval of gripper-object geometry from successful trajectories gives frozen VLA policies future targets under distribution shift.
KHQHyObYrJ.problem: VLA policies are brittle under distribution shift without reliable guidance about future interaction outcomes; world models add training or test-time cost, and retrieval methods reuse actions tied to the original scene geometry or need heavy 3D perception.
KHQHyObYrJ.method: RAAG retrieves geometrically compatible experience using gripper-object relations, retargets successful relations to the current scene, and gates guidance by policy risk and retrieval reliability, while the frozen VLA still decides how to reach the targets.
KHQHyObYrJ.key_idea: Transfer relative gripper-object geometry, not scene-specific motion paths, from retrieved successful memories as future targets, gated by policy risk and retrieval reliability.
KHQHyObYrJ.evidence: Five benchmarks, three simulators, and a real robot, with replay and visual-servoing controls, multiple policy backbones, and gating and memory-budget analyses described in the reviews.
KHQHyObYrJ.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (a review cites ManiSkill3 out-of-distribution success rising from 24.0% to 69.6% for the base policy).
KHQHyObYrJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that transferring interaction geometry while keeping the frozen policy's action prior is well motivated and that the evaluation is broad across backbones, shifts, and real-robot trials.
KHQHyObYrJ.main_concern: The specific benefit of relational retrieval is not isolated from matched geometric-guidance baselines and the rest of the pipeline, and reviewers also note paper-code perception discrepancies and untested sim-to-real transfer.

1oon6lKQdR.one_liner: Four-level algebraic hierarchy of word problems classifies state-tracking ability of transformers and Gated DeltaNet, with a long-horizon benchmark.
1oon6lKQdR.problem: State tracking is mostly benchmarked on the hard S5 word problem, leaving open whether simpler forms of state tracking, more relevant in practice, already explain differences between architectures.
1oon6lKQdR.method: The paper defines a hierarchy of word problems with four levels (r-trivial, aperiodic, soluble, general), proves where transformers and Gated DeltaNet fall in it, and provides a new benchmark for long-horizon state tracking.
1oon6lKQdR.key_idea: Use algebraic automata theory (r-trivial, aperiodic, soluble, general word problems) to locate which classes transformers and Gated DeltaNet can express.
1oon6lKQdR.evidence: Expressivity proofs (GDN with positive eigenvalues expresses exactly the aperiodic problems; the regular languages recognized by certain transformers are exactly the soluble ones) plus a benchmark covering learning and existing capabilities with sensitivity analysis.
1oon6lKQdR.claimed_gains: not stated; results are expressivity claims, such as the class transformers are thought to length-generalize on not containing all aperiodic state tracking.
1oon6lKQdR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating simpler levels of state tracking, not only a hard permutation task, gives an informative and controlled comparison of model capabilities.
1oon6lKQdR.main_concern: Reviewers question technical details in the lemmas and the significance beyond known class differences between GDN and transformers, and note the Krohn-Rhodes-based theory is hard to access.

QVUumcYNAX.one_liner: Diffusion language model corrupting token embeddings with spherical Brownian motion and sampling through an exact ancestral heat bridge.
QVUumcYNAX.problem: Spherical continuous diffusion language models use geodesic and vMF paths, but it is unclear which forward process to use on the sphere and how much that choice matters relative to the inference rule.
QVUumcYNAX.method: SBD uses Brownian motion, the canonical isotropic diffusion on the sphere, as the forward process; its heat semigroup gives an additive dimension-free noise clock and an exact ancestral bridge, and a clean-token posterior trained with cross-entropy supports multiple samplers. Approximation rates show moment-matched vMF approaches Brownian corruption at the critical noise scale.
QVUumcYNAX.key_idea: Corrupt token embeddings with spherical Brownian motion and sample via its exact heat bridge, separating how much noisy state is retained from token selection.
QVUumcYNAX.evidence: Sudoku, GSM8K, and LM1B (plus OpenWebText per the reviews) with controlled kernel and sampler comparisons and a decomposition of the sampler gain using the ancestral bridge.
QVUumcYNAX.claimed_gains: With matched training and sampling, kernels differ by at most 5 points on reasoning tasks while samplers span 20 to 25 points, and on LM1B the sampler effect exceeds the kernel effect in every setting.
QVUumcYNAX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written with a principled mathematical formulation and extensive controlled experiments, though at small scale.
QVUumcYNAX.main_concern: SBD does not consistently beat existing baselines (it trails several diffusion methods on GSM8K and MDLM and Duo on OpenWebText), and the motivation for a spherical token space is unclear.

wCoO5R6GEC.one_liner: Query-adaptive KV cache compression that keeps cluster representatives where error is low and expands clusters with high importance and distortion.
wCoO5R6GEC.problem: Repeatedly accessing the full KV cache bottlenecks long-context decoding, and small query-specific subsets approximate full attention but their union covers nearly the whole cache.
wCoO5R6GEC.method: The KV cache is split into clusters; compact representatives replace clusters that incur negligible error while the rest expand to their original KV entries. Selection uses a criterion derived from an upper bound on attention-output error with importance and distortion terms.
wCoO5R6GEC.key_idea: Rank clusters per query by an attention-output error bound combining cluster importance and within-cluster distortion, expanding only the risky ones at decode time.
wCoO5R6GEC.evidence: Experiments on two models and three benchmarks that report both attention-phase speedup and actual decoding latency.
wCoO5R6GEC.claimed_gains: Near-full-attention quality with up to 7.6x speedup in the attention phase and 1.66x faster decoding.
wCoO5R6GEC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the error analysis clean and the importance-versus-distortion selection criterion well motivated, with latency reported end to end.
wCoO5R6GEC.main_concern: Reviewers say the bound is too loose in the reported range to give the claimed error control, the risk score is not ablated against simpler scores, and the singleton-cluster result in Table 2 is inconsistent.

J7iOy8XxLM.one_liner: Estimates label reliability, corrects noisy multi-label supervision, and initializes cross-modal hashing with Soft-Jaccard relations before discrete optimization.
J7iOy8XxLM.problem: False-positive and missing-positive labels distort cross-modal semantic alignment in supervised multi-label cross-modal hashing, and existing robust methods under-use fine-grained multi-label structure after correction.
J7iOy8XxLM.method: RBCDH estimates instance-class-level label reliability from intra-modal neighborhood label support and cross-modal consistency, applies controlled bidirectional correction, and builds continuous Soft-Jaccard relations from the corrected label overlaps as a reliability-aware initialization. It then derives binary reliable relations from the same corrected supervision for discrete hash optimization.
J7iOy8XxLM.key_idea: Reuse one corrected label matrix for both a continuous Soft-Jaccard initialization and binary relations in discrete hashing, with reliability from neighborhood support and cross-modal consistency.
J7iOy8XxLM.evidence: Experiments on cross-modal retrieval benchmarks including NUS-WIDE and MM-IMDb with fixed pre-extracted features and shared splits for the compared methods, plus ablations and label-reliability diagnostics described in the reviews.
J7iOy8XxLM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method addresses both label-noise distortion of cross-modal relations and loss of fine-grained semantics, and that reusing the same corrected supervision in continuous and discrete stages is well motivated.
J7iOy8XxLM.main_concern: The label-correction module fixes only a small part of the noise, so gains may come mainly from the Jaccard initialization, and neighborhoods learned from noisy labels may reinforce wrong associations.

yVlGHbtU7J.one_liner: Query a human decision-maker to compare matched unit pairs to elicit unobserved confounders explaining differing treatment decisions.
yVlGHbtU7J.problem: Observational causal inference is hindered by unobserved variables that affect both treatment allocation and outcome, while randomized trials are costly or constrained.
yVlGHbtU7J.method: A human expert who makes treatment decisions compares pairs of units proposed by a principled matching strategy, with the goal of eliciting unobserved variables that explain why treatment decisions differ. The paper gives theory on when this elicits confounders and applies the design to ICU treatment effects.
yVlGHbtU7J.key_idea: Elicit unobserved confounders by asking the treating decision-maker why two matched units received different treatment, separating matching from explanation extraction.
yVlGHbtU7J.evidence: Theory with propositions and theorems on matching strategies, empirical evidence that ICU electronic health records have unobserved confounding, and semi-synthetic experiments checking whether adding the selected candidates helps downstream.
yVlGHbtU7J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that querying the decision-maker's treatment intent is a well-motivated and practically significant reframing, with a clear analytical framework separating matching from extraction.
yVlGHbtU7J.main_concern: Two reviewers doubt Theorem 3 holds for discrete confounders because ties are not handled, and one notes the theory identifies causes of treatment rather than common causes of treatment and outcome.

YpFhYPbsdF.one_liner: Trains diffusion transformers by progressively growing active attention heads and MLP channels across noise levels using a gradient-based need score.
YpFhYPbsdF.problem: Diffusion Transformers are expensive to train, and existing dynamic-width methods reduce only inference cost by pruning a pretrained dense model, leaving pretraining cost unchanged.
YpFhYPbsdF.method: GrowDiT starts from a narrow network and progressively activates attention heads and MLP channel groups across diffusion noise levels, selecting units with a gradient-based need score under an increasing compute budget. FLOPs saved in early updates are reallocated to additional optimization steps.
YpFhYPbsdF.key_idea: Activate model width in proportion to noise-level need during training, choosing which heads and channel groups to grow with a gradient-based need score.
YpFhYPbsdF.evidence: ImageNet-256 and FFHQ-256 under a fixed training-FLOP budget and approximately matched inference FLOPs across DiT-S/2, DiT-B/2, and DiT-L/2, against fixed-width, random-growth, dense, depth-growth, and DyDiT-inspired train-then-prune baselines.
YpFhYPbsdF.claimed_gains: On the 130M-parameter DiT-B/2, GrowDiT improves FID by 6% over fixed-width training at the same nominal training and inference FLOPs, with a smaller gain when budgets are matched by wall-clock.
YpFhYPbsdF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree GrowDiT consistently improves FID over fixed-width training across datasets and model sizes, with gains persisting under wall-clock-matched comparisons.
YpFhYPbsdF.main_concern: The gain of need-score selection over random growth is small and reported as two-seed means without variability estimates, and gradient-guided growth and timestep-dependent allocation have precedents.

B17yL0u5sl.one_liner: Shows representational alignment metrics can be driven by small neuron subsets and miss encoding-manifold topology, motivating neuron-level encoding analysis.
B17yL0u5sl.problem: Representational geometry measured by RSA and similar alignment metrics is taken as evidence of similar computation, but it may be shaped by a small subset of neurons rather than the whole population.
B17yL0u5sl.method: The paper adopts a complementary encoding paradigm that characterizes how neurons are organized globally by their responses, applies it to biological recordings and deep learning models, and runs a controlled MNIST experiment that manipulates encoding topology.
B17yL0u5sl.key_idea: Compare neuron-level encoding manifolds, meaning how function is distributed across neurons, alongside decoding-based alignment metrics to expose differences those metrics miss.
B17yL0u5sl.evidence: Biological electrophysiology datasets and several deep learning models, plus a controlled MNIST experiment comparing RSA, CKA, and Procrustes with encoding-based measures.
B17yL0u5sl.claimed_gains: In a controlled MNIST experiment that manipulates encoding topology, alignment metrics shift by at most 2.5 seed-to-seed standard deviations, compared with 19 for encoding (the rest of the sentence is cut off).
B17yL0u5sl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is timely and important, the encoding-manifold view is a well-grounded complementary perspective, and the experiments span biological and deep-learning systems.
B17yL0u5sl.main_concern: Novelty is limited because RSA, CKA, and Procrustes are known to be insensitive to neuron identity, and the MNIST result in Table 2 is confounded by shared initialization in the clustered comparison.

xKI2CbEsCU.one_liner: World model predicts downstream conflicts of scene-editing decisions and ranks earlier decisions to repair in 3D indoor scene generation.
xKI2CbEsCU.problem: Agentic 3D indoor scene generators overlook that currently valid decisions can block later spatial and functional requirements, causing delayed failures and costly revisions.
xKI2CbEsCU.method: A decision-consequence world model predicts how candidate decisions affect placement feasibility and constraint satisfaction during generation. During repair, an attribution model uses the failure context and historical decision graph to rank earlier decisions, and the world model scores replacements for local regeneration, with both models supervised by the 100k-record SceneWiseDB across 20 room categories.
xKI2CbEsCU.key_idea: Predict the downstream placement and constraint consequences of each candidate decision, and reuse that predictor to choose decisions and to rank and replace earlier ones during repair.
xKI2CbEsCU.evidence: Experiments measuring task success, constraint satisfaction, and editing counts against external baselines, with an ablation against a direct-risk predictor, using the new SceneWiseDB dataset.
xKI2CbEsCU.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (reviews cite 84.0% success versus 62.0% for the strongest external baseline on coupled-requirement tasks).
xKI2CbEsCU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and that reusing consequence prediction for both generation and targeted repair is coherent.
xKI2CbEsCU.main_concern: Reviewers say the added value of structured consequence prediction and historical attribution is not firmly established (small gain over a direct-risk predictor, no uncertainty estimates, related method SceneReVis omitted), and the SceneWiseDB generation pipeline is under-specified.

OHC78ch1GT.one_liner: Splits a high-resolution input into polyphase subproblems at the pretraining resolution, applies the neural operator to each, and recombines predictions.
OHC78ch1GT.problem: Neural operators trained on coarse grids degrade substantially on finer grids, which limits training on cheap low-resolution data and deploying at higher resolution.
OHC78ch1GT.method: Polyphase Inference decomposes the high-resolution problem into subproblems at the pretraining resolution, applies the pretrained operator to each, and recombines predictions at the target resolution without high-resolution training data. Polyphase Fine-Tuning learns the decomposition and adds fine-tuning modules when high-resolution examples exist.
OHC78ch1GT.key_idea: Present high-resolution fields to a fixed low-resolution operator as multiple pretraining-resolution polyphase components, then recombine the outputs on the target grid.
OHC78ch1GT.evidence: Several PDE benchmarks and architectures (FNO, UNet, Transolver, LaMO per the reviews) and DPOT, including independently simulated coarse and fine datasets, with low-data fine-tuning compared against parameter-efficient baselines.
OHC78ch1GT.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers; the abstract says Polyphase Inference improves cross-resolution accuracy over direct zero-shot evaluation and Polyphase Fine-Tuning substantially outperforms standard parameter-efficient methods in the low-data setting.
OHC78ch1GT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the resolution-mismatch problem is well motivated and that the polyphase decomposition is a simple, clearly presented approach that works across architectures.
OHC78ch1GT.main_concern: The experimental setup, where low-resolution data comes from subsampling high-resolution simulations, may favor the method and not test the claimed scenario, and novelty relative to multi-image super-resolution is unclear.

qtnG90teyC.one_liner: Multi-scale predictive alignment objectives on the encoder for offline goal-conditioned RL, covering dynamics, behavior, and temporal structure.
qtnG90teyC.problem: In sparse-reward offline goal-conditioned RL, aligning state and goal latents is hard, and the encoder can learn goal-agnostic features that destabilize policy learning.
qtnG90teyC.method: MSPR trains the encoder with alignment objectives that capture the environment at multiple scales, from local physical dynamics to long-horizon goal-directed structure, using multi-scale predictive supervision on top of a goal-conditioned TD3-BC backbone.
qtnG90teyC.key_idea: Combine predictive objectives at local-dynamics and long-horizon goal scales to force the latent space to align states with goals.
qtnG90teyC.evidence: OGBench vision and state-based tasks per reviews, with ablations, failure-case analysis, and varied data regimes, compared with the GCTD3 backbone and other flat and hierarchical methods.
qtnG90teyC.claimed_gains: Claims strong performance on vision and state-based tasks and retained performance under challenging data regimes; no numbers are stated.
qtnG90teyC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the experiments are convincing and thorough: MSPR clearly beats its GCTD3 backbone, outperforms other flat methods on average, and ablations show task-specific benefits of each objective.
qtnG90teyC.main_concern: The objectives lack an overarching principle and their novelty is unclear, and the claim that all three alignments are necessary rests on ablations of a single algorithm without model-based RL baselines.

PyJFsTVQJf.one_liner: Calibrates the distribution of task-relevant semantics over sampled black-box LLM responses with labeled data, then applies MBR decoding.
PyJFsTVQJf.problem: Fine-tuning an LLM on in-domain labels can be costly or intractable when access is limited to sampling responses from a black-box model.
PyJFsTVQJf.method: Represents sampled free-form responses as a distribution over task-relevant semantics such as ratings or class labels, calibrates the full distribution with in-domain labels, and applies Minimum Bayes Risk decoding to select the response minimizing expected task loss. It needs no model weights or token probabilities.
PyJFsTVQJf.key_idea: Recalibrate the model's sampled outcome distribution on labeled data (Dirichlet calibration per reviewers), then pick the MBR response under the task loss while the LLM stays frozen.
PyJFsTVQJf.evidence: Experiments across tasks and models including open-weight and closed-source LLMs, comparisons with classifier, decision-calibration and LoRA baselines per reviewers, and a proof of optimality among output-distribution decoding strategies under ideal recalibration.
PyJFsTVQJf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and practical for black-box LLMs, training only a small calibrator on sampled responses and labels, with broad evaluation across tasks and models.
PyJFsTVQJf.main_concern: Novelty and cost: it combines standard Dirichlet calibration with task-space MBR and needs about 20 samples per query plus auxiliary answer-extraction models, so the lightweight claim is not established.

PcLf36bZTY.one_liner: Injects scene and ego-conditioned trajectory tokens into the visual encoder and adds EMA-teacher JEPA objectives for end-to-end driving.
PcLf36bZTY.problem: ViT-based end-to-end planners add trajectory queries only after visual feature extraction, and compact scene tokens receive only auxiliary supervision without self-supervision on their latent representations.
PcLf36bZTY.method: ST-JEPA places camera-aware scene tokens and ego-conditioned trajectory tokens inside the visual encoder, with interleaved temporal global-register attention across frames. An online scene-trajectory JEPA objective predicts compact representations from masked observations against targets from an EMA teacher on unmasked inputs, alongside a second JEPA mechanism that is truncated in the abstract.
PcLf36bZTY.key_idea: Trajectory and scene tokens interact with image patches throughout encoding, and a training-only JEPA objective predicts their latents from masked inputs against an EMA teacher.
PcLf36bZTY.evidence: Experiments on NAVSIM and HUGSIM with cumulative ablations (Table 3) and information-fusion ablations (Table 7) according to reviews.
PcLf36bZTY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving trajectory-conditioned tokens into visual encoding is a reasonable, coherent change and that the ablations support the full configuration.
PcLf36bZTY.main_concern: The methodological increment over DrivoR, register-based temporal attention, and Drive-JEPA is modest and the conceptual novelty is unclear, with evaluation limited to nominal driving conditions.

XFmFWOA1Ex.one_liner: Multi-view Transformer jointly predicts depth and camera pose, trained self-supervised with photometric and geometric consistency from image warping.
XFmFWOA1Ex.problem: Humans learn 3D structure with little explicit geometric supervision, but existing self-supervised multi-view methods are weaker at camera pose and depth estimation.
XFmFWOA1Ex.method: Warp3R is a simple multi-view Transformer that jointly predicts depth maps and camera poses and is trained with an image warping loss enforcing photometric and geometric consistency across views. The same objective can extend supervised training on unlabeled data.
XFmFWOA1Ex.key_idea: A classical reprojection (warping) loss over predicted depth and pose provides photometric and geometric consistency supervision for a modern multi-view Transformer.
XFmFWOA1Ex.evidence: Camera pose and depth evaluation across diverse datasets against self-supervised baselines such as E-RayZer and NAS3R, with an RE10K-trained comparison and broad ablations according to reviews.
XFmFWOA1Ex.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the objective is simple and clean, the zero-shot camera pose results are strong, and the ablation study is broad and informative.
XFmFWOA1Ex.main_concern: The source of the improvement is not isolated because E-RayZer and NAS3R differ in architecture and training, and the rigid-scene warping assumption limits handling of deformation, illumination change, and view-dependent effects.

JthSLrEkea.one_liner: Generates humanoid motion with time-conditioned flow matching on root and pose, then selects candidates using a learned Motion Compatibility Evaluator.
JthSLrEkea.problem: Generated humanoid motions can reach a spatial goal but be wrong for the requested time, because contact patterns and whole-body poses must adapt to the time budget rather than merely speed up or slow down.
JthSLrEkea.method: TAMGen's generator uses flow matching with a root-pose architecture conditioned on spatial goals and explicit time budgets. A Motion Compatibility Evaluator scores complete candidates to select those with better target accuracy and physical quality, and picks both duration and motion when none is specified.
JthSLrEkea.key_idea: Condition root-pose flow matching on explicit time budgets so motion content changes with duration, then rerank candidates with a learned compatibility evaluator.
JthSLrEkea.evidence: LAFAN and BoneSeed comparisons with MotionBricks, plus real-world robot demonstrations including online target updates and replanning after a disturbance.
JthSLrEkea.claimed_gains: Compared with MotionBricks, reduces root endpoint error by 81.6% on LAFAN and 84.9% on BoneSeed, and mean foot-sliding speed by 48.6% on LAFAN and 31.6% on BoneSeed.
JthSLrEkea.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the time-appropriate motion problem matters, the system is coherent with strong endpoint accuracy and reduced foot sliding, and real-robot demonstrations support feasibility.
JthSLrEkea.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate the effect of time-aware generation: there is no comparison against time-warping a fixed-length motion, no duration-embedding ablation, and no simpler-scorer baseline for the evaluator.

NX0xRYJEQf.one_liner: Forecasts with node representations from long-term histories, dynamically retrieved support nodes, and training-time masking of the most-relied-on patches.
NX0xRYJEQf.problem: Spatio-temporal forecasters are tied to their training environments through node-specific representations, predefined spatial support, and consistent observations, which limits generalization under temporal shifts, spatial changes, and missing observations.
NX0xRYJEQf.method: VaryST derives node representations from long-term histories, dynamically selects functionally relevant support nodes beyond predefined neighborhoods and combines them with recent and long-term target states and global context, and selectively masks the historical patches it relies on most during training.
NX0xRYJEQf.key_idea: Build predictive context dynamically from available long-term observations and mask the most-relied-on historical patches in training to force use of alternative dependencies.
NX0xRYJEQf.evidence: Experiments on six datasets (abstract cut off), with traffic forecasting and PM2.5 data mentioned in the keywords and reviews.
NX0xRYJEQf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unifying problem of temporal, spatial, and observation shifts is practically important, and that deriving context from long-term observations and dynamic support retrieval rather than fixed node identity is a sensible design.
NX0xRYJEQf.main_concern: The dynamic support retrieval is not isolated by ablation (no random, fixed, graph-neighbor, or no-support controls), and novelty and comparisons against UniST and STONE are not established.

GICPSMuCNI.one_liner: Compiles natural-language procedural manuals into a history-dependent runtime shield that blocks violating tool calls and guides compliant progress.
GICPSMuCNI.problem: Runtime guards for tool-using agents only block problematic tool calls locally, leaving the agent without guidance and sometimes overly conservative, since calls may be problematic only in certain contexts.
GICPSMuCNI.method: MENTOR builds a history-dependent runtime shield from the procedural manual through a multi-step autoformalization pipeline, and uses a game-based technique for robustness to runtime uncertainty without over-restricting the agent. It also provides guidance toward compliant progress.
GICPSMuCNI.key_idea: Autoformalize the manual into a history-dependent shield, solved with a game-based method, that both forbids context-violating tool calls and suggests compliant next steps.
GICPSMuCNI.evidence: Multiple domains with open-weight and proprietary LLM agents (including tau-2 domains per reviewers), compared against LLM-judge and rule-based shields.
GICPSMuCNI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method fits the problem, combining LTL strategy templates with SMT-based argument checking, and that experiments across domains and agent backbones show meaningful gains in task success.
GICPSMuCNI.main_concern: Reliability depends on error-prone LLM formalization and labeling steps that are not evaluated, the evaluation lacks component ablations and baselines such as ReAct and Plan-and-Act, and the method cannot check natural-language outputs.

JS3u9BIyB2.one_liner: PRISMS curates candidates from expert pairwise rankings of multiple fidelities, escalating queries to costlier experts by information gain.
JS3u9BIyB2.problem: Validation congestion leaves candidate designs abundant but experimental capacity scarce, and regression models that predict absolute scores need substantial experimental data to begin with.
JS3u9BIyB2.method: PRISMS uses pairwise rankings from one or more experts of differing fidelity and cost to identify promising candidates without data-hungry regressors, escalating pairwise queries from lower-fidelity to higher-fidelity experts.
JS3u9BIyB2.key_idea: Drive curation with pairwise rankings and escalate comparisons from cheap to expensive experts where information is most needed, instead of regressing absolute scores.
JS3u9BIyB2.evidence: Drug-discovery and engineering datasets (14 datasets per a review) with multiple seeds, ablations and sensitivity analyses across three noise models, mostly with a simulated high-fidelity ranker and a limited LLM-ranker test on three tasks.
JS3u9BIyB2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the shift from absolute scores to pairwise comparisons well motivated and the framework coherent, with extensive experiments, ablations and sensitivity analyses.
JS3u9BIyB2.main_concern: Most results rely on a simulated 75%-accurate high-fidelity ranker, while the real LLM ranker is tested on only three tasks and three seeds, performs worse, and lacks baselines using the same ranker.

4xvSiRNHA2.one_liner: Controls that remove sample variation while keeping the reference adjustment separate system gains from the value of predicted sample differences.
4xvSiRNHA2.problem: Prediction systems can reduce error by correcting an overall offset, removing harmful baseline variation, or predicting useful sample differences, and headline gains do not show which of these drives them.
4xvSiRNHA2.method: Fixed drug-response and histology predictions are compared with controls that remove sample variation while retaining the reference adjustment, varying constant references, amplitude, risk weighting and the stage (expression versus final score) at which variation is removed, with a precipitation case under RMSE.
4xvSiRNHA2.key_idea: A telescoping loss decomposition against constant-reference controls splits a system's gain into baseline-variation removal and the contribution of retained predicted variation.
4xvSiRNHA2.evidence: Fixed drug-response predictions (28 comparisons), histology-based gene expression with downstream Hallmark scores in COAD, BRCA and GBM, and a precipitation case under RMSE.
4xvSiRNHA2.claimed_gains: In four of 28 drug comparisons the system improves on the adjusted baseline even though its added predictive variation increases error, and moving removal from expression to final scores changes 25, 43 and 38 positive contribution intervals to unresolved in COAD, BRCA and GBM.
4xvSiRNHA2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question important and the analysis careful, with sound comparisons under fixed conditions and practical guidance for computing gene-set scores from predicted expression.
4xvSiRNHA2.main_concern: Methodological novelty is unclear because the core tools (the telescoping identity, skill-score numerator, alignment-amplitude split) match established forecast-verification decompositions such as Murphy (1988).

A6gcELggqm.one_liner: Benchmark for reconstructing every active key and its full value from an initial state and ordered update history.
A6gcELggqm.problem: Existing benchmarks use query-specific evaluation, synthetic data, or uncontrolled real histories, so they cannot jointly test recovering evolving text collections and complete final values for all active items.
A6gcELggqm.method: StateTracking has 3,420 histories adapted from five datasets (document editing, online discussions, software issue workflows, financial orders, network records), with difficulty controlled by final active-key count N, transition count T, and deletion frequency rho.
A6gcELggqm.key_idea: Score complete state reconstruction (key set plus every retained value) while varying active-key count, transitions, and deletions, so updating, preservation, and invalidation are tested at once.
A6gcELggqm.evidence: Evaluation of multiple state-of-the-art LLMs on three real revision or workflow histories and synthetic histories with exact-match metrics.
A6gcELggqm.claimed_gains: Benchmark of 3,420 histories adapted from five datasets; no model results appear in the visible abstract.
A6gcELggqm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the complete-state reconstruction task relevant to long-running assistants and the benchmark well constructed across real and synthetic domains with controlled difficulty factors.
A6gcELggqm.main_concern: Exact-match scoring conflates state-tracking failures with text-fidelity errors (such as whitespace), and the fixed-history setup is removed from real assistant workflows.

uBHXpJZ3Uw.one_liner: Clusters MLLM hidden states to compare with human cognitive categories, then tests cluster-guided attention-head interventions on accuracy.
uBHXpJZ3Uw.problem: It is understudied how closely human cognitive taxonomies of perception and reasoning abilities characterize how MLLMs actually organize reasoning.
uBHXpJZ3Uw.method: Examples are clustered using model hidden-state representations and compared with human cognitive categories across five MLLMs. A shared attention-head intervention is then learned per human category or per model cluster, and the effects on accuracy are compared.
uBHXpJZ3Uw.key_idea: Define task groups by clustering hidden states, then learn one shared attention-head intervention per group and compare it against one per human category.
uBHXpJZ3Uw.evidence: Five MLLMs, clustering metrics (NMI, AMI, ARI), cluster-guided versus category-guided interventions on held-out accuracy, and ablations on cluster count, mask matching and layer depth.
uBHXpJZ3Uw.claimed_gains: Cluster-guided interventions outperform those guided by human cognitive categories and improve held-out test accuracy by 3.75-7.98% over the unmodified models.
uBHXpJZ3Uw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing representational comparison with functional interventions is informative and that cluster-guided gains are consistent across all five MLLMs.
uBHXpJZ3Uw.main_concern: It is unclear what the clusters represent, since heterogeneous data sources and formats may drive them, and gains over human categories shrink when cluster and category counts are matched.

bbhfFx9iqO.one_liner: Memory-efficient local learning that trains a per-block proxy network by distillation to estimate backpropagation gradients in transformers.
bbhfFx9iqO.problem: End-to-end backpropagation must store all activations until the loss gradient returns, while local learning avoids this but typically loses accuracy.
bbhfFx9iqO.method: For each transformer block, a local proxy network is trained by distillation to predict the global network output, and gradients propagate independently through the proxy while approximating backpropagation gradients. A residual proxy is used for non-linear residual models, with exactness shown for deep linear networks and bounded gradient error otherwise.
bbhfFx9iqO.key_idea: Distill the downstream network's output into a per-block residual proxy so gradients through the proxy approximate the true backpropagated gradient.
bbhfFx9iqO.evidence: Theory (exact for deep linear networks, bounded error for residual models), numerical gradient-estimation checks, CIFAR-100 with vision transformers, and LLM fine-tuning against zeroth-order methods.
bbhfFx9iqO.claimed_gains: Better accuracy/memory trade-off than other local algorithms on CIFAR-100 vision transformers, and for LLM fine-tuning it trains faster and reaches higher performance than zeroth-order memory-efficient algorithms at comparable memory; no numbers are stated.
bbhfFx9iqO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method addresses an important memory problem by explicitly approximating the backpropagated gradient and performs close to standard backpropagation at much lower memory than other local learning methods.
bbhfFx9iqO.main_concern: Limited practical advantage over exact-gradient memory savers such as checkpointing, given about 1.5x slower training and approximate gradients.

VKUL0FnHgB.one_liner: Shows nonlinear attention yields inverse-depth loss decay in controlled in-context tasks, via selective focus and layer aggregation.
VKUL0FnHgB.problem: Depth and parameter scaling laws lack a mechanistic explanation, and linear-attention theory ties scaling to a power-law data spectrum because such models cannot attend selectively.
VKUL0FnHgB.method: Controlled in-context learning tasks compare linear and nonlinear attention across data spectra, analyze individual spectral directions, and use a loss decomposition R_L = C_L + (A_L - C_L)/L that separates shared error from layer-specific disagreement.
VKUL0FnHgB.key_idea: Nonlinear attention focuses on relevant tokens so strong and weak spectral directions are learned in parallel, and layer aggregation averages out layer-specific error like a central limit theorem.
VKUL0FnHgB.evidence: Controlled in-context learning experiments across tested data spectra with fitted depth exponents (top-2 and top-16 tasks) and proofs in the appendix.
VKUL0FnHgB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating attention nonlinearity as the experimental variable and the shared-error versus disagreement decomposition give a clear, interpretable mechanistic picture.
VKUL0FnHgB.main_concern: The linear versus nonlinear comparison is confounded (different data parameters, masking, and context updates), and no error bars or run counts support the fitted exponents.

NVycuB8MlJ.one_liner: Humanoid generalist policy that predicts motion latents shared by human and robot encoders, executed by pretrained body and hand controllers.
NVycuB8MlJ.problem: Humanoid action spaces are large and tightly coupled, and robot demonstrations are scarce, while human motion cannot be used directly as a robot command.
NVycuB8MlJ.method: VioLA predicts body and hand motion latents instead of joint commands, which a pretrained body controller and hand decoder execute. Motion encoders map human and robot motion into the same latent spaces, so human recordings are labeled in the policy's action space (140.6 million converted frames, 93.2% human).
NVycuB8MlJ.key_idea: Predict shared human-robot motion latents rather than joint commands, so frozen controllers execute them and human data supervises the same action space.
NVycuB8MlJ.evidence: Real-robot experiments on a Unitree G1 covering locomotion, posture changes, and manipulation across three policy backbones, with human-only transfer and matched-step comparison against robot-only training.
NVycuB8MlJ.claimed_gains: VioLA reaches 100% zero-shot locomotion success where GR00T N1.7 and Psi_0 reach 16.7% and 0%, and reaches 77.5% manipulation success without task-specific fine-tuning.
NVycuB8MlJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared action representation is a practical, well-motivated way to use human demonstrations, with real-robot results across locomotion, posture, and manipulation.
NVycuB8MlJ.main_concern: The contribution of the latent action representation is not isolated from differences in training and execution machinery, the evaluation is narrow (one robot, 13 tasks), and the shared hand latent is undocumented.

gYisE3gqPU.one_liner: Refines layerwise sparsity allocations for LLM pruning through a regularized update of keep ratios using measured reconstruction responses.
gYisE3gqPU.problem: At high sparsity, layerwise allocations from importance scores or predefined rules ignore the reconstruction response of the chosen pruning backend, and different allocations under the same global budget give very different perplexity.
gYisE3gqPU.method: Plug-and-Prune takes a uniform or existing allocation, measures layerwise reconstruction responses under the selected backend, and applies a regularized update of the keep ratios that penalizes deviation from the input allocation and enforces the global budget and per-layer bounds. Within-layer mask construction is left to the backend.
gYisE3gqPU.key_idea: A proximal, budget-constrained update of per-layer keep ratios driven by the backend's measured reconstruction error at the input allocation.
gYisE3gqPU.evidence: WANDA and SparseGPT on LLaMA, Qwen3, and Phi-4 models, primarily at 70% unstructured sparsity, supplemented by sparsity-sweep and structured-pruning experiments.
gYisE3gqPU.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says the method generally lowers perplexity relative to the input allocation and improves zero-shot accuracy, without figures).
gYisE3gqPU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is a flexible plug-in that works with different allocators and pruning backends and gives consistent perplexity reductions at high sparsity.
gYisE3gqPU.main_concern: Novelty and justification are limited: the single-point quadratic surrogate is not validated at other sparsity levels, pruning time grows substantially, and most experiments use 70% sparsity on older models.

csa1maQQt3.one_liner: Training-free sparse attention system for long autoregressive video diffusion that offloads KV to CPU while overlapping transfers with attention.
csa1maQQt3.problem: AR-DiTs keep only a short local window of frames, causing forgetting and drift, while access to the full KV history exceeds GPU memory and increases attention FLOPs.
csa1maQQt3.method: Overlap-Aware Execution uses tiered storage and selectively overlaps KV transfers with attention computation to hide transfer latency. Residency-Aware Sparse Attention adaptively selects two-level sparsity configurations based on how much of the KV cache is resident on the GPU.
csa1maQQt3.key_idea: Hide CPU-to-GPU KV transfer latency behind attention on resident KV and choose sparsity levels by GPU residency, so the full history stays accessible without training.
csa1maQQt3.evidence: Applied to Self Forcing and LongLive (as named by reviewers) and compared with Light Forcing, LongLive-RAG, OmniMem, and a GPU-only variant on quality and latency.
csa1maQQt3.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract gives no figures).
csa1maQQt3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the long-history problem is well motivated and the training-free system design is coherent, with transfer overhead largely hidden at no quality cost.
csa1maQQt3.main_concern: The quality benefit of full-history retrieval is small (for example 0.8176 to 0.8248 total score), baseline fairness is unclear, and comparisons with Forcing-KV, MemFlow, and other long-video methods are missing.

KfBBa010L8.one_liner: Generates long-tail driving scenarios by guiding a diffusion model with gradients of a planner's uncertainty and learnability costs.
KfBBa010L8.problem: Existing long-tail scenario generators need domain knowledge of what makes a scene critical, do not reflect what the planner has not learned, and need extra components to keep scenarios learnable.
KfBBa010L8.method: POSG combines the diffusion model's score estimate with the gradient obtained from the planner's uncertainty, and identifies learnable scenarios using a generative model of the entire scene. It needs no domain knowledge or additional networks.
KfBBa010L8.key_idea: Steer a scene-level diffusion model with the gradient of the planner's own uncertainty plus learnability costs derived from the same generator.
KfBBa010L8.evidence: Planner training comparisons using in-distribution data, in-distribution plus unguided synthetic samples, in-distribution plus POSG-guided samples, and all available data; the abstract is cut off before other settings.
KfBBa010L8.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says POSG scenarios induce a higher planner error than unguided samples, but is cut off before figures).
KfBBa010L8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that deriving scenario difficulty from the planner's own uncertainty, without domain knowledge or extra components, is a low-cost and scalable formulation.
KfBBa010L8.main_concern: The evidence is thin: the gain over unguided synthetic data is small (0.058 against a 0.042 separability threshold), evaluation is open-loop, and POSG scenarios have more collisions (9.2% vs 3.9%).

K80HMQtm3H.one_liner: Question-level comparisons and trajectory edits test whether tool use expands what multimodal agents can solve beyond tool-free reasoning.
K80HMQtm3H.problem: Aggregate accuracy gains of tool-using multimodal agents do not show whether tools expand the set of solvable problems or only provide alternative paths to answers already within reach.
K80HMQtm3H.method: They compare DeepEyesV2, Thyme, and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct with tool-free counterparts across 15 benchmarks, train a Pure-Text Reasoner from DeepEyesV2 data, and edit tool-use trajectories (removing calls or returned results) to isolate their roles.
K80HMQtm3H.key_idea: Check whether each tool-enabled success is reproduced by a tool-free or text-only reference, and ablate calls versus returned results in edited trajectories.
K80HMQtm3H.evidence: Three agents on 15 benchmarks, a Pure-Text Reasoner trained from DeepEyesV2 data, trajectory-editing interventions, and success-set overlap analysis.
K80HMQtm3H.claimed_gains: Tool access yields no consistent performance advantage, and the Pure-Text Reasoner exceeds both specialized agents on 10 of 15 benchmarks without tool-calling supervision.
K80HMQtm3H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of whether tools add capability is important and that the question-level success-set analysis and trajectory-editing interventions give concrete evidence of how different tools contribute.
K80HMQtm3H.main_concern: The tool-free references differ in prompts, context, and sampling, so they do not cleanly identify causal tool contribution, and the findings overlap with recent audits and cover only small models on tasks where the needed information is already in the input.

iAG0c17ipQ.one_liner: Decouples search allocation from visual selection in thermal UAV tracking via a trajectory-geometry branch and reliability-gated Recrop.
iAG0c17ipQ.problem: Bounded local trackers cannot recover a target that leaves the search crop, and enlarging the region adds background clutter while ambiguous local cues make it unclear where to search.
iAG0c17ipQ.method: TGTrack's time-aware Temporal Geometry Branch encodes center and scale evolution, visual confidence, and temporal information from sparsely sampled trajectory states to predict target geometry and localization reliability. When the predicted center leaves the normal search support it allocates one bounded geometry-guided Recrop with a Gate-Hann spatial prior scaled by predicted reliability, and final cross-region selection uses raw visual confidence.
iAG0c17ipQ.key_idea: Use predicted trajectory geometry to decide where to recrop, and use appearance confidence alone to choose among candidate regions.
iAG0c17ipQ.evidence: Anti-UAV thermal infrared benchmarks including AntiUAV410 and direct cross-dataset transfer to AntiUAV, built on a LoRAT-L baseline and compared with local-search trackers (abstract truncated).
iAG0c17ipQ.claimed_gains: Best results among the compared local-search trackers; reviewers cite AUC gains of 2.86 points on AntiUAV410 and 4.03 points under direct cross-dataset transfer.
iAG0c17ipQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating geometry-guided search allocation from appearance-based selection is a reasonable, well-motivated way to handle targets that leave the search region, with consistent gains.
iAG0c17ipQ.main_concern: Limited technical novelty and scope, since the components resemble existing motion-guided and re-detection trackers and experiments center on LoRAT-L and anti-UAV data, with the contribution of each component and of Gate-Hann left unclear.

Y9B4VrxiyZ.one_liner: Encodes whole graphs into single latent vectors with a permutation-invariant transformer VAE and an order-based reconstruction loss without graph matching.
Y9B4VrxiyZ.problem: Graph-level autoencoders need a cubic-cost graph-matching step in the reconstruction loss to handle node order.
Y9B4VrxiyZ.method: A transformer-based VAE with a permutation-invariant encoder maps each graph to one fixed-dimensional latent vector; the reconstruction loss compares predictions to targets directly in a consistent node order, reducing complexity from cubic to quadratic.
Y9B4VrxiyZ.key_idea: Keep the encoder permutation-invariant but relax invariance in the reconstruction loss, comparing predictions to targets in the training data's consistent node order.
Y9B4VrxiyZ.evidence: Large molecular graph datasets for reconstruction and single-step generation, latent-space interpolation, molecular editing, property optimization, and property regression from latents.
Y9B4VrxiyZ.claimed_gains: Claims 'state-of-the-art' reconstruction accuracy on large molecular graph datasets and reduced matching cost from cubic to quadratic complexity; no numbers stated.
Y9B4VrxiyZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question about where permutation invariance is needed interesting, and praise the clear, well-motivated architecture and the wide set of molecular experiments.
Y9B4VrxiyZ.main_concern: Related work is incomplete: prior graph-level latent models (for example GLAD and other graph-level autoencoders) are not discussed or compared.

ZWwyCHLg8l.one_liner: Classifies the computational complexity of factual and counterfactual explanations for graph classification by fixed GNNs.
ZWwyCHLg8l.problem: Formal complexity guarantees for local post-hoc GNN explanations, meaning sufficient subgraphs and minimal edits that change a prediction, are largely overlooked.
ZWwyCHLg8l.method: It formalizes factual and counterfactual explanation problems, characterizes their complexity with the GNN treated as fixed rather than as input and shows hardness even then, and proves fixed-parameter tractability on bounded-treewidth graphs for fixed bounded GNNs.
ZWwyCHLg8l.key_idea: Treat the GNN as fixed so hardness lives in the explained graph, and exploit bounded treewidth for fixed-parameter tractability with bounded GNNs.
ZWwyCHLg8l.evidence: Theoretical complexity proofs (hardness reductions and a fixed-parameter tractability result); reviewers note there is no empirical validation.
ZWwyCHLg8l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that hardness persisting for a fixed GNN is the key contribution and that the formal analysis complements existing empirical and taxonomic studies of GNN explanations.
ZWwyCHLg8l.main_concern: Scope: the hardness proofs lean on binary node-attribute flips and the tractability result holds only for AC-GNNs with bounded readout, so implications for structural explanations and common sum or mean GNNs are limited.

T4RaCxTzv9.one_liner: L2T learns a latent representation from baseline data and runs a one-sided test on deployment latents for dynamic instability.
T4RaCxTzv9.problem: Stability of DAE-governed safety-critical systems must be reassessed as the context distribution shifts, but repeated large-scale DAE simulation is prohibitive in high-dimensional or real-time settings.
T4RaCxTzv9.method: It learns a latent representation from baseline context-trajectory data that preserves stability-relevant information, then performs a one-sided test on the deployment latent distribution, calibrated over the composite null of stable deployments, to test a trajectory-level chance constraint from deployment contexts alone.
T4RaCxTzv9.key_idea: Test the latent distribution of deployment contexts against a calibrated null of stable deployments instead of re-estimating physical parameters or re-solving the DAE.
T4RaCxTzv9.evidence: Theory of finite-sample validity under class-conditional latent invariance with robustness to deviations, and experiments on simulated dynamical systems, a power-system benchmark, real-world chatbot deployments and driving camera data.
