T4RaCxTzv9.claimed_gains: Maintains valid false-alarm control with detection power comparable to or higher than baselines; no numbers stated.
T4RaCxTzv9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well posed and the framework well articulated, replacing expensive DAE simulation with a principled latent hypothesis test.
T4RaCxTzv9.main_concern: The experiments lack methodological detail and appear disconnected from the theory, and the link to classical stability definitions and the invariance assumption is questioned.

Gpv16PvafA.one_liner: Diffusion model for human-object interaction with path, part and contact factors, waypoint residuals, and foot-refinement post-processing.
Gpv16PvafA.problem: Generating coordinated human-object motion from sparse waypoints while following user-specified routes and keeping stable contacts remains hard.
Gpv16PvafA.method: A reference path interpolated from sparse waypoints conditions generation and is the baseline for planar object translation, with learned residuals. A part-based spatiotemporal denoiser keeps separate temporal and part axes, hand-object and foot-ground guidance refine contacts, and a foot-refinement network drives world-space foot anchoring and temporal inverse kinematics after sampling.
Gpv16PvafA.key_idea: Object translation is predicted as a residual on a waypoint-interpolated reference path, with separate part-axis and time-axis attention and contact guidance during denoising.
Gpv16PvafA.evidence: Experiments on FullBodyManipulation, a residual versus absolute translation ablation, tests on unseen 3D-FUTURE objects without retraining, and a blinded user study per reviews.
Gpv16PvafA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pipeline is well designed with each component serving a clear purpose, and that it outperforms prior baselines on most metrics with convincing results.
Gpv16PvafA.main_concern: Contributions are not clearly separated from prior work, since the method integrates established ideas (factored trajectory, motion and contact representations, separate spatial and temporal attention, inverse kinematics), and factorized attention lacks comparison against full attention.

HdZogiR5K1.one_liner: Sliding-window LLM processes chunks as a multi-turn conversation and learns to write brief notes that carry key information forward.
HdZogiR5K1.problem: Constant-memory architectures such as linear attention and pure sliding window attention lose information beyond their fixed state or window.
HdZogiR5K1.method: R-Notes feeds fixed-size input chunks as a multi-turn conversation under a single SWA session and trains the model to emit brief notes that propagate key information across chunks within the window. It is built on Qwen3-8B and, per a reviewer, trained with SFT and RL.
HdZogiR5K1.key_idea: The model writes self-generated notes after each chunk that stay inside the sliding window, so key content survives after the original tokens scroll out.
HdZogiR5K1.evidence: Built on Qwen3-8B and evaluated on LongBench cross-task QA, RULER-HQA at 112K, and RULER-SQuAD at 128K against a Qwen3-14B full-attention baseline and MemAgent.
HdZogiR5K1.claimed_gains: 73.4% vs 71.3% for Qwen3-14B full attention on LongBench cross-task QA, and 87.50% vs 78.12% on RULER-HQA at 112K and RULER-SQuAD at 128K, with KV cache bounded by the window and compute linear in chunks.
HdZogiR5K1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem matters, the chunk-wise note mechanism is clearly presented and simple (no hybrid architecture or external memory), and the RULER and LongBench experiments show effectiveness.
HdZogiR5K1.main_concern: Missing comparisons with Smooth Reading and external-memory or agent methods (same-backbone MemAgent, LLMxMapReduce), and no latency or wall-clock cost measurements.

ISFE4l0Y9y.one_liner: Rollback of KGE optimization updates ranks query-candidate paths into compact influential subgraphs, encoded as latent prefixes for LLM reranking.
ISFE4l0Y9y.problem: LLM-based knowledge graph completion needs query-specific structure, but structurally connected context is not necessarily useful for a given prediction and verbose graph descriptions are costly.
ISFE4l0Y9y.method: RISE traces triple-level KGE optimization updates and uses rollback-induced prediction changes to prioritize query-candidate paths, which are aggregated into compact influential subgraphs. These are encoded and fused with candidate representations as latent structural prefixes for LLM reranking.
ISFE4l0Y9y.key_idea: Score paths by how much rolling back training updates changes the KGE's prediction for a query-candidate pair, then feed the top paths as latent prefixes to an LLM reranker.
ISFE4l0Y9y.evidence: Experiments on four datasets against compared methods, plus analyses of prediction-relevant subgraph selection and compact latent conditioning; candidates come from RotatE per a reviewer.
ISFE4l0Y9y.claimed_gains: Best performance on most evaluation metrics among compared methods on four datasets; no numbers stated.
ISFE4l0Y9y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well organized with clearly described implementation, the empirical results support the method, and prediction-aware subgraph selection (structural connection is not usefulness) is well motivated.
ISFE4l0Y9y.main_concern: Limited novelty over Gradient Rollback, GradPath, KGExplainer, KoPA, and DrKGC; reviewers also flag the transductive reranking-only setting bounded by RotatE top-K recall and the absence of significance tests.

FY9KgzCqoE.one_liner: Coarse-to-fine denoiser aggregation constructs a temporal score prior for inference-time adversarial purification.
FY9KgzCqoE.problem: Single-noise or uniformly weighted diffusion defenses underuse distinct coarse and fine denoising scales when balancing robustness and semantic fidelity.
FY9KgzCqoE.method: TARO combines high-noise denoising views for global structure with low-noise views for image-specific detail. A guidance coefficient controls the temporal residual correction during test-time purification.
FY9KgzCqoE.key_idea: Form a coarse-to-fine residual target from denoisers at different noise levels and control its correction strength during purification.
FY9KgzCqoE.evidence: Experiments cover multiple datasets and adaptive threat models, including fully unrolled attacks and comparisons of coarse and fine objectives.
FY9KgzCqoE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find multi-noise denoiser aggregation useful and appreciate compatibility with existing diffusion purification objectives.
FY9KgzCqoE.main_concern: Multiple reviewers question whether the theoretical interpretation and methodological differences sufficiently justify the claimed advance over existing purification methods.

apbevOolq5.one_liner: Synthetic multi-day work environments test whether assistants apply evolving user norms to tool-generated artifacts.
apbevOolq5.problem: Assistants can complete explicit tasks while violating user-specific work norms established in earlier interactions.
apbevOolq5.method: PersonalWorkEnv generates personas, simulated workdays, CLI tasks, and progressively introduced or superseded profiles. Deterministic validators and rubric checks distinguish surface completion from profile compliance, with mixed-curriculum RL as a training baseline.
apbevOolq5.key_idea: Introduce and replace user norms across workdays, then separately validate task completion and norm compliance in generated artifacts.
apbevOolq5.evidence: PersonalWorkEnv-50 contains fifty double-audited environments, evaluates seven models, and tests mixed-curriculum RL on small Qwen3.5 models.
apbevOolq5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating actual artifact compliance with evolving user norms separately from surface task success.
apbevOolq5.main_concern: Reviewers find personalization failures confounded with instruction-following difficulty and increasing constraint load because memory is supplied before each task.

T2AxHRI9eT.one_liner: Native quantization metadata assigns weight blocks to matched entropy-coding buckets for bit-exact compression.
T2AxHRI9eT.problem: Already-quantized LLM weights retain redundancy that generic compressors miss, while further quantization can reduce generation quality.
T2AxHRI9eT.method: Q3.6 deterministically groups blocks by stored metadata such as scales and encodes each bucket using a matched table-based entropy model. Decoding preserves the exact quantized weights.
T2AxHRI9eT.key_idea: Condition entropy models on native quantization metadata by deterministically grouping similar weight blocks into shared coding buckets.
T2AxHRI9eT.evidence: Evaluation spans three models, five quantized formats, and three bit widths, with metadata-routing controls and GPU implementation results.
T2AxHRI9eT.claimed_gains: Q3.6 saves about 10% on average relative to uncompressed target tensors and stores less than zstd in every evaluated setting.
T2AxHRI9eT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate metadata-conditioned lossless coding, explicit storage accounting, and evidence from several quantization settings.
T2AxHRI9eT.main_concern: Multiple reviewers identify the lack of a matched comparison with the closest lossless quantized-weight compression approach.

d0TazczdMV.one_liner: Null-space parameterization and successive temporal coarsenings generate fine-scale trajectories that exactly match coarse observations.
d0TazczdMV.problem: Coarse states and temporal aggregates leave unresolved trajectory variability that probabilistic downscaling must recover consistently.
d0TazczdMV.method: MUNDO enforces linear observation consistency through a null-space parameterization in one network evaluation. Reverse Markov learning factors the observation operator into levels that model degrees of freedom lost between adjacent resolutions.
d0TazczdMV.key_idea: Generate only observation-null-space degrees of freedom and recursively learn variability lost between successive temporal resolutions.
d0TazczdMV.evidence: Tests cover two-scale Lorenz-96, four two-dimensional physical systems, and multivariate European ERA5 for temporal interpolation and disaggregation.
d0TazczdMV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the unified observation-consistent formulation and promising downscaling results.
d0TazczdMV.main_concern: Multiple reviewers request clearer differentiation and comparisons with existing temporal downscalers and hard-constrained generative methods.

67TYXrYPBb.one_liner: Effective-rank-guided neuron growth and activation-similarity pruning adapt reinforcement-learning critics to preserve plasticity.
67TYXrYPBb.problem: Static RL networks can lose representational capacity and adaptability as training data distributions change.
67TYXrYPBb.method: The method dynamically grows and prunes critic neurons using effective rank as an online architecture signal. Pruning targets redundancy among active neurons through activation similarity.
67TYXrYPBb.key_idea: Trigger critic expansion using effective-rank occupancy and remove correlated neurons to adapt capacity as reinforcement-learning distributions change.
67TYXrYPBb.evidence: SAC experiments cover continuous control, high update-to-data ratios, changing environment dynamics, and sequential tasks, with network-size and component analyses.
67TYXrYPBb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value using representation statistics to adapt network capacity and testing several forms of RL non-stationarity.
67TYXrYPBb.main_concern: Multiple reviewers question whether the effective-rank growth signal identifies capacity needs and offers benefits over alternative growth or pruning criteria.

hzdoP9YqZn.one_liner: Queryable local graph programs preserve boundary interactions and internal responses for reuse across changing graph assemblies.
hzdoP9YqZn.problem: Message-passing encodings depend on current graph connections, while boundary-only summaries cannot answer internal-node queries.
hzdoP9YqZn.method: CoGraC compiles graph components into numerical programs retaining boundary interactions and recoverable internal responses. Prediction gradients through joint execution train reusable local computations for new connections and queries.
hzdoP9YqZn.key_idea: Compile components into composable boundary operators with retained lifting and conditional factors that recover internal-node responses.
hzdoP9YqZn.evidence: Experiments cover compositional link prediction, frozen-compiler cross-domain transfer, node and graph classification, and reuse on changing real graphs.
hzdoP9YqZn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reusable component representations that support both global composition and internal queries.
hzdoP9YqZn.main_concern: Multiple reviewers find stronger evidence for global execution than for the claimed benefit of learning through composition.

vsdD1CizE9.one_liner: Compatible manifold kernels and potentials yield closed-form normalization and directly sampleable entropic transport conditionals.
vsdD1CizE9.problem: Manifold optimal-transport solvers often rely on costly iterative procedures or models that underuse geometric structure.
vsdD1CizE9.method: ManifoldLightOT constructs geometry-specific Gibbs kernels and potential families on spheres, tori, SO(3), SE(3), and their products. It optimizes potential parameters from samples with Monte Carlo estimates.
vsdD1CizE9.key_idea: Choose geometry-specific kernel–potential pairs whose products admit closed-form normalization and direct conditional sampling.
vsdD1CizE9.evidence: The paper derives constructions for several manifolds and compares learned transport on synthetic and real-world experiments.
vsdD1CizE9.reviewer_consensus: Positive reviews recognize the tractability obtained by matching manifold-specific Gibbs kernels with compatible potentials.
vsdD1CizE9.main_concern: Multiple reviewers question whether marginal-based metrics and differing transport objectives establish the quality of the learned couplings.

wTMH0baxky.one_liner: Scale-wise routers weight heterogeneous LoRA-adapted fusion experts to modulate depth contributions in RGB-D salient object detection.
wTMH0baxky.problem: Treating depth maps as uniformly trustworthy in RGB-D salient object detection causes negative cross-modal transfer when depth measurements are noisy, incomplete, or misaligned.
wTMH0baxky.method: MPLoRA-MoE combines a shared semantic backbone with modality-specific low-rank adapters and four heterogeneous fusion experts weighted at each spatial scale by an independent router over pre-fusion RGB and depth features, decoded through a single edge-semantic pathway without quality annotations.
wTMH0baxky.key_idea: Predict soft distributions over four heterogeneous fusion experts from pre-fusion RGB and depth features at each scale using modality-specific LoRA adapters.
wTMH0baxky.evidence: Evaluations span eight RGB-D salient object detection benchmarks, including unseen test sets, with ablations on expert heterogeneity, routing temperature, and adapter rank.
wTMH0baxky.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-expert RGB-D fusion architecture is clearly motivated and generalizes strongly across unseen RGB-D salient object detection benchmarks.
wTMH0baxky.main_concern: All three reviewers point out that the paper never directly validates that router weights respond to depth quality or corruption, lacking routing-weight analyses, uniform-weight no-router controls, and parameter/FLOPs reporting.

2beCDXIVOH.one_liner: Shared rubric criteria and item response theory calibrate query-local document preferences into cross-query relevance probabilities.
2beCDXIVOH.problem: Discrete relevance grades poorly separate similar rerankers, while relative LLM judgments lack a common scale across queries.
2beCDXIVOH.method: RCP combines listwise Bradley-Terry tournaments with increasingly stringent yes/no rubric criteria. Item Response Theory calibrates tournament scores across queries, and RCP-nDCG uses the resulting relevance probabilities.
2beCDXIVOH.key_idea: Use shared binary rubric responses as Item Response Theory anchors for calibrating query-specific Bradley-Terry scores.
2beCDXIVOH.evidence: Evaluation compares rerankers across multiple benchmarks and validates relevance scores against blind judgments from 46 external annotators.
2beCDXIVOH.claimed_gains: Calibration raises query-mean human-grade correlation from 0.538 to 0.795 and yields usefulness-ranking AUC of 0.910 versus 0.651 for the benchmark.
2beCDXIVOH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the substantial empirical validation, particularly comparisons with independent human judgments.
2beCDXIVOH.main_concern: Reviewers find the incremental benefit of IRT calibration insufficiently isolated from simpler scoring alternatives.

4qCL11laq3.one_liner: Sampling-aware Bayesian hypothesis tests quantify node membership privacy using node-specific priors and posterior membership probabilities.
4qCL11laq3.problem: Global attack accuracy and error rates overlook heterogeneous membership priors and stochastic graph sampling in GNN privacy analysis.
4qCL11laq3.method: Bayesian Membership Privacy incorporates node-dependent priors and sampling probabilities into membership hypothesis tests. A sampling-aware auditing mechanism estimates privacy parameters and connects the formulation with existing privacy definitions.
4qCL11laq3.key_idea: Treat known graph-sampling probabilities as node membership priors when converting attack evidence into posterior membership probabilities.
4qCL11laq3.evidence: The paper provides theoretical connections to privacy definitions and experiments on benchmark graph datasets, including audits of DP-GNN discussed in reviews.
4qCL11laq3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find sampling-dependent, node-specific membership risk a meaningful privacy problem and value incorporating membership priors.
4qCL11laq3.main_concern: Reviewers find insufficient validation that the practical audit estimates true privacy risk accurately under its statistical assumptions.

qiLUia8Trm.one_liner: Soft token roles control appearance editing and source preservation in streaming egocentric videos while protecting hand-object interactions.
qiLUia8Trm.problem: Video tokens near hand-object boundaries entangle editable appearance with interaction structure that should remain unchanged.
qiLUia8Trm.method: TRIVE assigns object, interface, hand, and background responsibilities and derives separate retention, appearance-access, and reference permissions. It applies role-aware attention and denoising controls plus appearance-anchor retrieval to a frozen streaming backbone.
qiLUia8Trm.key_idea: Convert shared soft token responsibilities into operation-specific permissions for attention, denoising, and appearance-reference retrieval.
qiLUia8Trm.evidence: Reviews report EgoEditBench, FiVE-Bench, robotic simulation, ablations, and downstream real-robot policy training using edited data.
qiLUia8Trm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the hand-object editing formulation and downstream robot-policy evaluation of the generated data.
qiLUia8Trm.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize dependence on reliable external hand masks and tracking, especially under occlusion or detection failures.

jJBbb4uEMi.one_liner: A positive-semidefinite compatibility penalty regularizes partial sequence alignments jointly across related sequence groups.
jJBbb4uEMi.problem: Individually plausible partial pairwise alignments can contradict one another across sequences observing a shared process.
jJBbb4uEMi.method: The supervised framework jointly predicts overlap boundaries and monotone alignments for sequence groups. It assembles directed soft correspondences into a relation matrix and penalizes distance to the symmetric positive-semidefinite cone.
jJBbb4uEMi.key_idea: Regularize assembled pairwise correspondence matrices toward a shared Gram-compatible structure through a symmetric positive-semidefinite distance penalty.
jJBbb4uEMi.evidence: Experiments on CMU ARCTIC speech and simulated stratigraphic sequences compare alignment and overlap errors, with direct and composed correspondence ablations.
jJBbb4uEMi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value explicitly modeling partial overlap and group-level compatibility beyond independent pairwise alignment.
jJBbb4uEMi.main_concern: Reviewers ask for clearer differentiation from existing alignment and group-consistency methods.

8unUoI9AXw.one_liner: Counterfactual visual interventions decompose task updates to select parameter directions for replay-free continual robot-skill protection.
8unUoI9AXw.problem: Continual VLA learning forgets prior skills, while replay requires stored demonstrations and task-specific modules expand model capacity.
8unUoI9AXw.method: CSD-VLA treats fine-tuning task vectors as skill proxies and uses task-preserving counterfactual interventions to identify environment-sensitive directions. It retains a protection basis for later training while discarding probes and historical demonstrations.
8unUoI9AXw.key_idea: Use counterfactual gradient contrasts to separate environment-sensitive task-vector directions from the parameter subspace protected during future learning.
8unUoI9AXw.evidence: Reviews describe LIBERO and RoboTwin evaluations, protection-strategy ablations, and tests under held-out visual changes.
8unUoI9AXw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value retaining skills without demonstration replay or expansion of the deployed policy.
8unUoI9AXw.main_concern: Reviewers find the evidence for the selective protection mechanism incomplete because relevant controls and decomposition validation are missing.

0nl7tNIEOi.one_liner: Information-theoretic analysis separates ordering errors from parallel factorization bias and motivates local prefix verification in masked diffusion decoding.
0nl7tNIEOi.problem: Parallel masked decoding can generate incompatible token combinations even when individual conditional predictions are accurate.
0nl7tNIEOi.method: The analysis studies model-induced rollout errors, dependence lost through parallel factorization, and whole-block rejection costs. Prefix-Consistent Parallel Decoding relaxes exact sampling by checking local prefix consistency.
0nl7tNIEOi.key_idea: Separate rollout-dependent conditional error from lost joint dependence, then check local prefix consistency during parallel decoding.
0nl7tNIEOi.evidence: Theory analyzes KL divergences and rejection costs; Block-HMM, LLaDA, and batched WeDLM experiments isolate sampling effects and quality-latency trade-offs.
0nl7tNIEOi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear distinction between marginal prediction quality and errors introduced by the sampling procedure.
0nl7tNIEOi.main_concern: Reviewers question how much the framework and decoding method add beyond existing analyses and related decoding approaches.

lWgOFhPbOV.one_liner: Parallel retries with test-based selection recover smaller or quantized language-model capability within local memory and latency budgets.
lWgOFhPbOV.problem: Large models exceed local memory budgets, while smaller or compressed models lose one-shot accuracy.
lWgOFhPbOV.method: The study runs multiple parallel attempts from smaller or compressed models and selects outputs using public tests, generated tests, or learned verifiers. It measures whether reachable correct outputs, verifier quality, and available compute permit recovery.
lWgOFhPbOV.key_idea: Spend otherwise idle local compute on parallel candidate generation and verification while reducing model memory.
lWgOFhPbOV.evidence: Experiments cover four code-generation benchmarks, model sizes and compression levels, NVIDIA GPUs, Apple Silicon, and mathematical reasoning with a learned verifier.
lWgOFhPbOV.claimed_gains: Eight Coder-7B attempts match or exceed one-shot Coder-32B with about 4.3× less model memory and 1.1–4.0× faster generation, remaining 1.3–1.8× faster including public tests on HumanEval+ and MBPP+.
lWgOFhPbOV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical memory-versus-retry question and the empirical examination of when repeated attempts help.
lWgOFhPbOV.main_concern: Reviewers question whether results generalize beyond single-turn code benchmarks to broader deployment tasks.

WZeauXj4FD.one_liner: Outcome-reward reinforcement learning trains language models to choose safe fallback behavior when task completion is unreliable.
WZeauXj4FD.problem: Success-only reinforcement-learning rewards encourage risky guesses, while naive intermediate fallback rewards cause brittle optimization.
WZeauXj4FD.method: GracefulRL modifies the optimization objective to promote safe fallback while preserving successful behavior. Training uses outcome-level rewards without fallback annotations or additional inference-time verification.
WZeauXj4FD.key_idea: Reshape policy optimization under success, fallback, and failure rewards to preserve incentives for both task completion and safe fallback.
WZeauXj4FD.evidence: Reviews describe theoretical analysis and experiments in maze navigation, mathematical reasoning, and multi-turn Minesweeper.
WZeauXj4FD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard safe fallback learning as practically meaningful and appreciate its theoretical and experimental support.
WZeauXj4FD.main_concern: Reviewers question the method's novelty beyond applying TailRL to ternary rewards.

8fF8uiQTAY.one_liner: Answer-clarification-answer consistency cycles recover the interpretations accessible to a particular language model.
8fF8uiQTAY.problem: Input-level ambiguity ignores that different models can access and answer different subsets of possible interpretations.
8fF8uiQTAY.method: The paper formalizes clarification uniqueness, faithfulness, and answer equivalence to connect answers with clarification classes. CIRCLECLAR estimates accessible answer sets through black-box consistency checks and supports answering, clarifying, or abstaining.
8fF8uiQTAY.key_idea: Generate a clarification for each candidate answer and check whether answering that clarification returns the same candidate.
8fF8uiQTAY.evidence: Experiments cover QA, task instructions, and Text-to-SQL, evaluating answer-set recovery, model-dependent ambiguity detection, and response selection.
8fF8uiQTAY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the model-dependent view of ambiguity and the simple answer-clarification consistency mechanism.
8fF8uiQTAY.main_concern: Reviewers question evaluation against estimated answer-support references that share method assumptions and depend on LLM judgments.

z8kDE8GxRH.one_liner: Paired prompt optimization jointly revises sender and receiver instructions and shared communication conventions along multi-agent edges.
z8kDE8GxRH.problem: Strong individual agents can collaborate poorly when messages and their interpretation are misaligned.
z8kDE8GxRH.method: PACO uses a state-aware discounted bandit to select communication edges and execution feedback to propose paired revisions. Staged end-to-end evaluation updates prompts while keeping model weights, roles, and workflow topology fixed.
z8kDE8GxRH.key_idea: Optimize both endpoints and the shared convention of a communication edge using end-to-end execution feedback.
z8kDE8GxRH.evidence: Experiments evaluate a four-agent workflow across multi-agent QA benchmarks, including transfer of HotpotQA-optimized configurations to other datasets.
z8kDE8GxRH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find communication edges a useful optimization unit for coordinating message construction and interpretation.
z8kDE8GxRH.main_concern: Reviewers find the fixed four-agent chain insufficient to establish effectiveness in branching or more complex workflows.

Amzw1xOCMF.one_liner: Source-isolated receiver branches compare specialist-induced token changes and commit medical answers only when enough source groups support revisions.
Amzw1xOCMF.problem: Mixing heterogeneous specialist outputs in a shared medical-VLM context entangles supportive and conflicting evidence before reliability can be assessed.
Amzw1xOCMF.method: MERIT runs separate specialist-conditioned branches and a no-expert anchor through the same frozen receiver with a shared answer prefix. Adaptive BARD proposes a revision from centered expert residuals and accepts it only with sufficient isolated-source support before synchronizing the chosen token.
Amzw1xOCMF.key_idea: Measure each specialist's influence on a shared receiver's next-token distribution and gate revisions by isolated source-group agreement.
Amzw1xOCMF.evidence: Experiments cover multiple medical benchmarks and two VLM backbones, including LLaVA-Med, with ten settings and ablations of naive evidence fusion.
Amzw1xOCMF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value training-free integration of heterogeneous specialist evidence through separate branches of a frozen receiver.
Amzw1xOCMF.main_concern: Evaluation on older receivers leaves effectiveness on stronger contemporary medical VLMs unestablished.

0VOTFMuV5K.one_liner: A future-environment pathway predicts revisions to a history-based forecast through conditional flow refinement.
0VOTFMuV5K.problem: Existing exogenous-variable forecasters emphasize how to inject future information without isolating what it adds beyond history.
0VOTFMuV5K.method: Environment-Guided Flow builds a reference forecast from complementary historical views and encodes future exogenous variables relative to a reference environment. Conditional flow progressively revises the reference, and the same response formulation serves as a lightweight adapter for existing forecasters.
0VOTFMuV5K.key_idea: Assign future exogenous information the role of predicting a correction to a history-only reference forecast.
0VOTFMuV5K.evidence: Forecasting experiments include matched Direct-versus-Response pathways, transfer across three representative TSF-X backbones, and a one-step correction ablation.
0VOTFMuV5K.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating historical reference forecasts from environment-induced corrections is intuitive and practically motivated.
0VOTFMuV5K.main_concern: The necessity of the complex flow-refinement design remains unclear because existing controls do not match its vector-field expressiveness.

TXzJcpPdUb.one_liner: Hierarchical retrieval and execution-based reliability updates organize heterogeneous tools into a shared action space for agents.
TXzJcpPdUb.problem: Large tool ecosystems exceed context budgets, change reliability over time, and return incompatible feedback formats.
TXzJcpPdUb.method: AnyAct retrieves task-relevant actions hierarchically and prunes unreliable actions through test-time reliability updates. A heterogeneous observation-grounding module unifies feedback while orchestration combines primitive GUI or command-line actions with semantic tools under success-cost tradeoffs.
TXzJcpPdUb.key_idea: Progressively retrieve actions and update their reliability from execution history while grounding heterogeneous observations into a shared orchestration layer.
TXzJcpPdUb.evidence: Evaluations use LiveMCPBench and the authors' OSMCP benchmark, with reliability examples involving rate limiting and changing tool availability.
TXzJcpPdUb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that tool scale, service instability, and heterogeneous observations are practical problems addressed by a coherent framework.
TXzJcpPdUb.main_concern: Execution-status reliability scores and limited controlled failure-recovery tests do not establish reliable adaptation to service faults or distinguish them from argument errors.

WcKOVk3bhc.one_liner: Estimated marginal search gains and a completion reserve adapt verifier-guided beam width under a fixed token budget.
WcKOVk3bhc.problem: Retaining more reasoning branches can consume the budget without sustained progress, completed answers, or successful final selection.
WcKOVk3bhc.method: SCA+ selects width at each search layer from an estimated marginal benefit and an estimated token reserve needed to complete a retained path. The study separately measures branch retention, progress, completion, and final answer selection with verifier calls included in costs.
WcKOVk3bhc.key_idea: Add a search branch only when its estimated gain justifies the cost while preserving enough budget to finish one path.
WcKOVk3bhc.evidence: Experiments use 195 MATH problems and exact-distance labels on 1.22 million planning candidates, with budget-aware baselines, shared selectors, and completion-reserve ablations.
WcKOVk3bhc.claimed_gains: Under total-token accounting, SCA+ improves MATH accuracy by 4.7 points over its strongest budget-aware baseline with 16% fewer charged tokens.
WcKOVk3bhc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the separation of search failure stages and the completion reserve's supported accuracy-efficiency gains under the stated accounting.
WcKOVk3bhc.main_concern: Charging re-fed inputs and verifier tokens equally with generation can penalize wide search and does not establish savings under cached, batched serving.

iTkHnmus2P.one_liner: Thresholded bounded query-key similarities enable exact rejection in parallel screening tiles for long-context language modeling.
iTkHnmus2P.problem: Query-key relevance that depends on competing keys or sequence length lacks a fixed interpretable scale and cannot always reject all keys.
iTkHnmus2P.method: Screening thresholds bounded query-key similarities into relevance values that can all be zero without length-specific calibration. Multiscreen combines parallel gated screening tiles with a normalization design for stable language-model training.
iTkHnmus2P.key_idea: Threshold bounded query-key similarities independently of competing keys so every key can receive exactly zero relevance.
iTkHnmus2P.evidence: Matched-backbone comparisons test 12 attention mechanisms, perplexity and retrieval beyond training context, ABCDigits and passkey tasks, and architecture and normalization ablations.
iTkHnmus2P.claimed_gains: The normalization design keeps Multiscreen stable at a learning rate of 1 and stabilizes an adapted Transformer at the same learning rate.
iTkHnmus2P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value controlled attention-rule comparisons and nested ablations that isolate screening's contribution to long-context behavior.
iTkHnmus2P.main_concern: Retrieval evidence centers on narrow token-lookup tasks, leaving realistic context-dependent retrieval insufficiently validated.

MiOw4iPFKM.one_liner: Functional-assay tasks test genomic models' prediction, context sensitivity, genetic interactions, and candidate selection for DNA design.
MiOw4iPFKM.problem: Existing genomic benchmarks do not adequately measure the capabilities needed to choose DNA sequences and edits for desired responses.
MiOw4iPFKM.method: DRAFT evaluates sequence priors, functional predictions, biological context, genetic interactions, and design selection using experimental data. It compares native outputs, frozen-representation linear readouts, and functional post-training while separating average effects from context-specific effects and interactions.
MiOw4iPFKM.key_idea: Decompose functional effects and evaluate selection against measured candidates to test whether prediction quality translates into useful DNA design choices.
MiOw4iPFKM.evidence: Eight tasks across five experimental datasets compare genomic models and simple baselines, with cross-assay and cross-gene transfer plus held-out candidate-selection measurements.
MiOw4iPFKM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value evaluating genomic models on real functional assays and measured candidate selection beyond sequence likelihood alone.
MiOw4iPFKM.main_concern: The benchmark's added value relative to existing functional and context-sensitive genomic evaluations remains insufficiently established.

SUDFPlQpLv.one_liner: An LLM revises shared gene-description protocols using prediction feedback to improve text representations for unseen genetic perturbations.
SUDFPlQpLv.problem: Fixed hand-designed gene descriptions leave unclear which biological knowledge and textual organization best support unseen-perturbation prediction.
SUDFPlQpLv.method: The approach holds the text encoder and prediction pipeline fixed while an LLM iteratively revises a shared description protocol using held-out predictions and trial history. Continuous Directed Overlap evaluates recovery of strong transcriptome-wide effects by rank and direction.
SUDFPlQpLv.key_idea: Optimize one reusable gene-description protocol through prediction feedback and search history while keeping the downstream representation pipeline fixed.
SUDFPlQpLv.evidence: Four Perturb-seq datasets and three search LLMs support comparisons across gene embeddings, predictors, cellular contexts, and single-cell generative models.
SUDFPlQpLv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled separation of biological information content from description structure and the resulting gene-representation evaluation.
SUDFPlQpLv.main_concern: The contribution needs clearer positioning against existing gene-representation and causal perturbation-prediction methods.

YW5dtuYLCv.one_liner: Pooling labels within sufficient explanation classes enables graph learning with guarantees that permit arbitrary within-class label noise.
YW5dtuYLCv.problem: Previous label-sharing guarantees require graphs with shared explanations to have nearly identical labels, excluding substantial within-class noise.
YW5dtuYLCv.method: Pooled ERM assigns each graph its explanation-class label frequency, fits weighted majority targets, and averages fitted predictions within observed classes. The analysis separates within-class representatives from class counts to handle reuse of the fitting sample.
YW5dtuYLCv.key_idea: Pool empirical label frequencies across graphs sharing an explanation that contains all label-relevant information.
YW5dtuYLCv.evidence: The paper proves sufficiency-based sample-complexity and risk bounds and evaluates GNNs using supplied explanations, repeated runs, paired tests, and descriptor controls.
YW5dtuYLCv.claimed_gains: Under I(Y;G|T(G))≤κ, pooled ERM returns a classifier within 3√(κ/2)+ε of the best risk in H with probability 1−δ from O((d+log(1/δ))/ε²) labels, even with infinite ordinary VC dimension.
YW5dtuYLCv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the theoretical relaxation from near-deterministic shared labels to sufficient explanations with unrestricted within-class noise.
YW5dtuYLCv.main_concern: The mined explanations used on real graphs have not been shown to satisfy the sufficiency assumption required by the theoretical guarantees.

ViiuyYgFPu.one_liner: Prefix-aligned candidate scoring and priority-based tree search expand diffusion drafts into paths likely to survive autoregressive verification.
ViiuyYgFPu.problem: Single-path diffusion drafts waste multi-candidate outputs, while prefix-blind diffusion marginals rank autoregressive verification paths unreliably.
ViiuyYgFPu.method: PRESTO combines prefix-aligned scoring with tree construction that prioritizes paths with high verification potential. The framework applies to dedicated diffusion drafters and self-speculative models that draft and verify within one forward pass.
ViiuyYgFPu.key_idea: Rank diffusion candidates using prefix-dependent evidence and allocate tree expansion to paths with higher expected verification acceptance.
ViiuyYgFPu.evidence: Benchmark evaluations compare acceptance length and end-to-end throughput for dedicated and self-speculative diffusion drafting, with targeted acceptance analysis and a matched-search DDTree comparison.
ViiuyYgFPu.claimed_gains: PRESTO reports average end-to-end speedups of 1.5× over DFlash.
ViiuyYgFPu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing prefix-blind diffusion ranking and extending tree drafting to both dedicated and self-speculative decoding.
ViiuyYgFPu.main_concern: The comparisons do not sufficiently isolate the proposed scoring and tree construction from naive or existing prefix-aware tree-drafting alternatives.

glhb0OP1Ux.one_liner: Inverse dynamics and feature reconstruction learn compact future targets for joint action and world-state prediction.
glhb0OP1Ux.problem: World-action models often predict high-dimensional native visual features, making future-state co-training expensive.
glhb0OP1Ux.method: PRISM learns compact representations from privileged current-future transitions using inverse-dynamics supervision and feature reconstruction. MiniWAM freezes that encoder and jointly predicts its future targets and robot actions from current observations.
glhb0OP1Ux.key_idea: Compress future supervision through a frozen transition encoder trained with inverse dynamics and reconstruction before joint world-action learning.
glhb0OP1Ux.evidence: LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0 simulation tests use DINOv3 and WAN2.1 VAE features, training-efficiency comparisons, and representation analyses.
glhb0OP1Ux.claimed_gains: MiniWAM uses 65× fewer native future feature tokens and achieves up to an 8× world-action training speedup, with a 0.25B model competitive with larger WAMs.
glhb0OP1Ux.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that compact future targets substantially reduce training cost while preserving competitive manipulation performance.
glhb0OP1Ux.main_concern: Simulation-only evaluation and missing end-to-end deployment measurements leave real-world effectiveness and control-time efficiency unverified.

bgEHNP4CeP.one_liner: Relates trajectory-level KL path cost in perturbed diffusion sampling to output statistic shifts via a dynamical response identity and zero-mean response factorization.
bgEHNP4CeP.problem: Perturbations with identical trajectory-level KL divergence (path cost) during diffusion sampling can produce vastly different effects on the final generated output distribution.
bgEHNP4CeP.method: Combines dynamical sensitivity analysis of diffusion sampling trajectories with an information-theoretic path cost (trajectory KL divergence), deriving a response identity that links step-wise perturbation propagation and accumulation to expected changes in an output statistic, alongside an exact factorization showing how local distributional changes can have zero first-order mean response.
bgEHNP4CeP.key_idea: Decompose expected output-statistic shifts under equal trajectory-KL perturbations into step-wise dynamical propagation operators to explain when sampling errors amplify or cancel.
bgEHNP4CeP.evidence: Theoretical response identity derivations and controlled equal-path-cost interventions across sampling stages and spatial DCT frequencies on pretrained diffusion models (including JiT, ADM, and DiT), plus a feature-caching window selection experiment.
bgEHNP4CeP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical framework explaining why equal-KL trajectory perturbations yield unequal output errors across timesteps and frequencies, as well as its high rank correlation in predicting risky feature-caching windows.
bgEHNP4CeP.main_concern: Reviewers note that the first-order local approximation diverges from observed response magnitudes under finite perturbations in DiT, connections to classical mean-reverting SDE contractivity are close, and the caching application is tested on only one eight-step reuse protocol without runtime cost comparisons.

uGNAFQPRb4.one_liner: Regularizes Flow Matching velocity fields with cubical persistent homology at the pixel level and Vietoris-Rips persistent homology across sample batches.
uGNAFQPRb4.problem: Conditional sampling in Flow Matching models exhibits a trade-off between sample fidelity and distributional diversity under standard pointwise MSE velocity training.
uGNAFQPRb4.method: Augments the Flow Matching velocity matching loss with two persistent-homology regularizers: a pixel-level fidelity loss using cubical complex filtrations on velocity sublevel sets to match local spatial topology, and a batch-level diversity loss using Vietoris-Rips filtrations on predicted velocity point clouds to align batch topology with the training distribution.
uGNAFQPRb4.key_idea: Align the persistent homology diagrams of predicted velocity fields with ground-truth velocities using cubical filtrations for intra-sample structure and Vietoris-Rips filtrations for inter-sample batch geometry.
uGNAFQPRb4.evidence: Evaluated on MNIST, CIFAR, and MS-COCO (with RAE DINOv2 and SD-2.1 VAE latents, plus SiT/XL-2) using FID, Precision, and Recall metrics.
uGNAFQPRb4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find batch-level Vietoris-Rips persistent homology regularization on velocity fields an interesting distributional complement to pointwise MSE that improves FID and Recall in RAE (DINOv2) latent space.
uGNAFQPRb4.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the pixel-level cubical fidelity loss degrades FID across datasets (contradicting the title's dual fidelity-and-diversity claim), while the Vietoris-Rips diversity loss only helps in DINOv2 RAE latents and fails to improve SD-2.1 VAE latents or SiT/XL-2.

E78ZlxZ1aF.one_liner: Separates candidate proposal coverage from selector identifiability at inference time and amplifies weak reasoning models via critic-gated all-pairs tournament selection.
E78ZlxZ1aF.problem: Repeated sampling from a weak reasoning model often generates a correct solution in the candidate pool, but imperfect verifiers struggle to reliably identify it, and higher coverage alone does not guarantee higher final accuracy.
E78ZlxZ1aF.method: Formalizes inference-time amplification by decomposing performance into proposal coverage and selector identifiability, characterizing when repeated noisy pairwise comparisons amplify a weak local selection signal and when proposal blind spots persist. Implements a critic-gated all-pairs pairwise comparator over candidate pools with additional task/repository context.
E78ZlxZ1aF.key_idea: Decompose test-time scaling into candidate coverage and selector identifiability, using critic-gated all-pairs pairwise verification to amplify weak local selection edges across sampled candidate pools.
E78ZlxZ1aF.evidence: Theoretical amplification conditions and empirical evaluation on SWE-bench Verified (with GPT-5.4 nano and other proposers), MATH L4-5, GSM-Plus, competitive programming, formal proof, and Blocksworld.
E78ZlxZ1aF.claimed_gains: On SWE-bench Verified, raises GPT-5.4 nano from 68.4% (single proposal, 79.0% pass@8 oracle) to 75.5-76.4% (recovering 75.5% of the oracle gap); on MATH L4-5 and GSM-Plus, recovers 85% and 77% of the oracle gap, beating majority vote by 12.6 and 8.6 points.
E78ZlxZ1aF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean decomposition separating proposal coverage from selector identifiability on cached candidate pools and the diagnostic negative controls showing when verification fails.
E78ZlxZ1aF.main_concern: Reviewers note limited empirical novelty over existing pairwise test-time verification literature, point out that the headline 76.4% SWE-bench score is the best entry of a hyperparameter sweep evaluated directly on the test set without a validation split, and note inconsistencies in baseline references.

gMrvm6HexL.one_liner: Decomposes LM causal steering into capacity, responsiveness, and alignment, and trains linear probes restricted to context-dependent causal subspaces.
gMrvm6HexL.problem: Localized latent structures in language model activation spaces differ substantially in their causal influence on behavior, leaving unclear what makes a representation actionable.
gMrvm6HexL.method: The authors decompose causal influence into three factors: capacity (output sensitivity to movement along a structure), responsiveness (concept promotability given context), and alignment (overlap with context-specific concept representations). They then restrict linear probe training to the low-dimensional subspace of causally effective directions to form causal probes.
gMrvm6HexL.key_idea: Factors causal influence into capacity, responsiveness, and alignment, and constrains linear probe training to a context-dependent low-dimensional causal subspace.
gMrvm6HexL.evidence: Empirical evaluation across 4 language model families and 50 concepts.
gMrvm6HexL.claimed_gains: Low capacity and responsiveness reduce causal effectiveness by 84% and 95% respectively, while causal probes achieve 17%-118% improvement in steering across models with only 3% reduction in concept detection.
gMrvm6HexL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the interpretable three-factor decomposition of causal influence and the empirical analysis linking concept detection to behavioral steering.
gMrvm6HexL.main_concern: Reviewers question the strict independence of the first-order factors, the validity of the token-occurrence concept metric, and whether causal probes offer clear gains over baselines like DiffMeans.

y4HN5TgiaE.one_liner: Retrieves and reasons directly over rendered page images for scientific deep research, trained via counterfactual credit reweighting.
y4HN5TgiaE.problem: Existing deep research agents reduce complex scientific documents to OCR-extracted text, losing information in tables, figures, and equations, while standard SFT weights noisy reasoning and action steps equally.
y4HN5TgiaE.method: The authors introduce DR Pixel, an end-to-end multimodal deep research agent that uses rendered page images as its retrieval and reasoning unit over a 1.06M-page corpus, alongside the DRPixelBench benchmark. For training, they propose counterfactual credit reweighting to weight individual reasoning and action steps by their contribution to the final answer.
y4HN5TgiaE.key_idea: Retrieves and reasons over rendered document page images directly and weights demonstration reasoning and action steps using counterfactual credit assignment.
y4HN5TgiaE.evidence: Evaluated on the newly constructed DRPixelBench benchmark over an open corpus of 1.06M pages across GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.5-Flash, and Qwen3.6-27B.
y4HN5TgiaE.claimed_gains: Counterfactual credit reweighting improves retrieval recall by about 20% and outperforms OCR-based baselines across GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.5-Flash, and Qwen3.6-27B with fewer tool calls.
y4HN5TgiaE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the complete pipeline spanning benchmark construction, systematic evaluation of page-native retrieval versus OCR, and retriever training.
y4HN5TgiaE.main_concern: Reviewers note omitted comparisons against existing visual retrieval and credit-assignment methods, potential selection bias in DRPixelBench toward multimodal queries, and single-page grounding limitations.

fbDRo6YCiH.one_liner: Constructs formal problem representations to retrieve algorithmic knowledge and application exemplars for generating auditable coding plans.
fbDRo6YCiH.problem: Implicit problem abstraction and free-form planning in LLM code generation lead to inappropriate algorithm selection, underspecified plans, and constraint-violating implementations on algorithmic problems.
fbDRo6YCiH.method: AlgoSAGE constructs a formal problem representation to make computational structure explicit and retrieves reusable Algorithmic Knowledge alongside Algorithmic Application Exemplars. It then adapts this retrieved evidence into target-specific, executable, and auditable plans prior to generating code.
fbDRo6YCiH.key_idea: Uses an explicit formal problem representation to hierarchically retrieve abstract algorithmic knowledge and concrete application exemplars before synthesizing executable coding plans.
fbDRo6YCiH.evidence: Experiments across CodeContests, APPS, xCodeEval, and function-level programming benchmarks using Qwen3.8-27B-Coder and additional LLM backbones.
fbDRo6YCiH.claimed_gains: With Qwen3.8-27B-Coder, AlgoSAGE achieves 70.3%, 76.0%, and 78.3% Pass@1 on CodeContests, APPS, and xCodeEval respectively, outperforming existing approaches by up to 6.7 percentage points.
fbDRo6YCiH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicit algorithm selection and combining reusable algorithmic knowledge with solved exemplars yield consistent improvements across benchmarks and backbones.
fbDRo6YCiH.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty of combining established RAG and planning components and note missing controlled comparisons against standard retrieval baselines under fixed memory and token budgets.

enabz2HQXZ.one_liner: Unifies heterogeneous robot sensor configurations in a single VLA via residual adapters, sensor-set FiLM conditioning, and utility-guided subset selection.
enabz2HQXZ.problem: Vision-Language-Action models are typically coupled to a fixed sensory interface, preventing a single policy from operating across robots with different optional sensors or sharing heterogeneous demonstrations.
enabz2HQXZ.method: FlexSense integrates three modules into a unified VLA framework: Shared-Residual Sensory Encoding (ShareRes) with zero-initialized scalar-gated residual adapters, Sensor-Set-Conditioned FiLM (SetFiLM) to condition action blocks on the active sensor set, and Utility-Guided Sensor Selection (UtilSelect) which distills counterfactual action errors of the frozen policy into a scorer to pick the lowest-error sensor subset.
enabz2HQXZ.key_idea: Combines shared-residual sensory encoders and active-sensor-set FiLM conditioning with a counterfactual-error scorer that selects sensor subsets at each action-chunk query.
enabz2HQXZ.evidence: Evaluated on LIBERO, ManiSkill, and real-world robotic manipulation across multiple sensor configurations.
enabz2HQXZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical motivation of handling heterogeneous sensor configurations with a single VLA checkpoint and value the controlled cross-configuration transfer experiments.
enabz2HQXZ.main_concern: Reviewers find the architectural components incremental over known multimodal techniques and note that UtilSelect offers very small gains (~0.45 percentage points) tested with only one seed while still encoding all sensors.

lc5pAtlEVo.one_liner: Learns task latents for offline meta-RL Decision Transformers by jointly optimizing contrastive, language-alignment, world-model, and Q-function losses on a shared LLM.
lc5pAtlEVo.problem: Effective generalization in offline meta-reinforcement learning requires accurately inferring compact, transferable latent task representations to guide policy generation across unseen tasks, including zero-shot settings.
lc5pAtlEVo.method: Contrastive Task-Aware Decision Transformer (CoTA-DT) learns latent task representations using a shared pretrained LLM backbone with LoRA by integrating trajectory contrastive learning, natural-language task alignment, a task-conditioned one-step world model, and a task-conditioned Q-function. It conditions a Decision Transformer policy on these latents and uses a language-grounded, self-adaptive rollout strategy for zero-shot and few-shot adaptation.
lc5pAtlEVo.key_idea: Trains a shared LLM backbone with contrastive, language-alignment, world-model, and Q-grounding objectives to produce task latents that condition a Decision Transformer.
lc5pAtlEVo.evidence: Experiments across four offline meta-RL benchmarks in zero-shot and few-shot generalization settings.
lc5pAtlEVo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the integration of language-based task initialization with trajectory-based latent adaptation practical and well-motivated for zero-shot and few-shot offline meta-RL.
lc5pAtlEVo.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over prior work like Meta-DT and T2DA, and point out a potential training-inference mismatch or target leakage in how transitions construct the task latent during training.

D2o00TZkSr.one_liner: Evaluates AI agents on 30 university course projects requiring active knowledge acquisition from course workspaces using a five-stage process rubric.
D2o00TZkSr.problem: Existing long-horizon AI agent benchmarks typically rely on pretraining knowledge or supply domain knowledge directly, failing to test whether agents can locate and operationalize instructional materials from a workspace.
D2o00TZkSr.method: The authors introduce CourseProject-Bench, a benchmark of 30 university course projects across five disciplinary domains paired with reconstructed hierarchical course workspaces. They evaluate agents using Process Correctness, a five-stage framework covering Task Understanding, Knowledge Access, Conceptual Understanding, Knowledge Operationalization, and Artifact Production.
D2o00TZkSr.key_idea: Pairs authentic university course projects with hierarchical course workspaces and scores agent trajectories and artifacts across five stages of knowledge acquisition and operationalization.
D2o00TZkSr.evidence: Evaluated eight frontier agent configurations across 30 university course projects spanning five disciplinary domains, including controlled harness and model comparisons.
D2o00TZkSr.claimed_gains: Across eight frontier agent configurations, the strongest achieves only 60.7% Process Correctness.
D2o00TZkSr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the realistic course workspace setting, the multi-domain project dataset, and the diagnostic five-stage evaluation separating process failures from final deliverables.
D2o00TZkSr.main_concern: Reviewers point out the lack of human-agreement validation for the automated judge on actual agent runs and the absence of an ablation removing course materials to prove tasks cannot be solved from pretraining knowledge alone.

ywss4aa3dP.one_liner: Models coupled dynamics of AI adoption, data dilution, and exogenous learner scaling to show path dependence in data pollution equilibria.
ywss4aa3dP.problem: As deployed AI models pollute future training data while model scale increases over time, it is unclear whether scaling can undo evidence degradation created by earlier deployment.
ywss4aa3dP.method: The authors formulate a dynamical model coupling AI adoption and evidence dilution under an exogenous learner scaling path and data curation rate. They analyze fixed-scale equilibria and prove path-dependent basins of attraction for delayed versus early scaling, supplemented by numerical simulations and multi-generation experiments with Qwen2.5.
ywss4aa3dP.key_idea: Couples endogenous AI-induced data dilution with exogenous learner scaling trajectories in a dynamical system to characterize path-dependent clean and degraded equilibria.
ywss4aa3dP.evidence: Theoretical proofs of equilibria and path dependence, numerical simulations under alternative degradation specifications, and controlled multi-generation experiments with Qwen2.5-1.5B.
ywss4aa3dP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the theoretical formulation showing that the timing of scaling and hysteresis in the data environment determine whether a system reaches a clean or degraded equilibrium.
ywss4aa3dP.main_concern: All three reviewers note that the empirical language model experiment holds model scale fixed (Qwen2.5-1.5B) and therefore does not empirically test the central theoretical claim about scaling schedules.

uHXlNKZ9A1.one_liner: Benchmarks long-context surgical video understanding with 30,000 VQA pairs tracking foreign objects across hour-long colorectal procedures.
uHXlNKZ9A1.problem: Existing video understanding benchmarks focus on short-term reasoning and fail to assess whether Vision-Language Models can maintain cumulative temporal consistency over multi-hour horizons.
uHXlNKZ9A1.method: The authors construct HeiCo-FOCUS, a dataset of 30,000 VQA pairs built on Heidelberg Colorectal surgery videos requiring continuous tracking of foreign objects as they are inserted, manipulated, occluded, and removed. It uses crowd and expert annotations (39 surgical experts) and a multi-track evaluation framework scaling from single frames to full procedures.
uHXlNKZ9A1.key_idea: Evaluates multi-hour temporal consistency in VLMs by querying instance-level foreign object states, timings, and counts across progressive temporal tracks in surgical videos.
uHXlNKZ9A1.evidence: Evaluated ten vision-language models alongside text-only and human baselines across 30,000 VQA pairs covering five core capabilities.
uHXlNKZ9A1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that foreign object tracking in hour-long surgeries is a clinically meaningful task and commend the substantial instance-level annotation effort.
uHXlNKZ9A1.main_concern: All three reviewers highlight a severe mismatch between uniform 300-frame video sampling (nearly 1-minute intervals on long procedures) and the strict ±5-second tolerance required for temporal grounding answers.

Vmfa4xG61U.one_liner: Audits ResearchCodeBench via paired paper-removal and code-masking interventions, showing scores depend heavily on visible enclosing code snippets.
Vmfa4xG61U.problem: Paper-to-code benchmarks report pass rates without identifying whether models rely on the research paper or on unmasked neighboring code in the target file, and naive masking interventions can introduce instruction artifacts.
Vmfa4xG61U.method: The authors perform paired interventions on ResearchCodeBench (RCB) that separately remove the paper or mask neighboring annotated code while keeping tasks and tests fixed, and further split masks between enclosing snippets and independent components. They also identify and correct an instruction artifact caused by altering visible placeholder counts during masking.
Vmfa4xG61U.key_idea: Uses paired paper-deletion and neighbor-code masking interventions with length and placeholder controls to attribute paper-to-code benchmark pass rates to their information sources.
Vmfa4xG61U.evidence: Evaluated across three open models and three commercial endpoints on ResearchCodeBench, plus a replication check on SciReplicate-Bench.
Vmfa4xG61U.claimed_gains: Across three models, removing the paper reduces pass rate by 1.6–8.1 percentage points (nominally significant for one model), whereas masking neighboring code reduces it by 16.8–25.4 points.
Vmfa4xG61U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the careful paired experimental design, confounding controls, and the discovery of the placeholder instruction artifact in ablation studies.
Vmfa4xG61U.main_concern: Reviewers note that the dominant neighbor effect comes mostly from visible enclosing functions of short nested targets specific to RCB, shrinks under RCB's line-weighted metric, and fails replication criteria on SciReplicate-Bench.

QYVowXx10h.one_liner: Organizes long contexts via boundary-aware semantic chunking, novelty-based memory budget allocation, and selective raw-text replay.
QYVowXx10h.problem: Existing context compression methods for long-context LLMs rely on fixed segmentation and uniform compression ratios, causing semantic fragmentation and loss of critical evidence.
QYVowXx10h.method: AdaMem segments long inputs into coherent units via boundary-aware chunking, estimates information novelty per chunk to adaptively allocate summary vector budgets, and accumulates chunk-level memories. At inference, it applies selective replay to recover raw text only when compressed memories are insufficient.
QYVowXx10h.key_idea: Combines boundary-aware semantic chunking and novelty-driven variable memory allocation with a selective replay fallback to raw context.
QYVowXx10h.evidence: Experiments and component ablations on three long-context question answering benchmarks (HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, TriviaQA) up to 1M tokens.
QYVowXx10h.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the coherent three-stage decomposition of memory organization and the thorough component ablations across datasets and context lengths.
QYVowXx10h.main_concern: Reviewers point out an unfair comparison where AdaMem is fine-tuned on 10K RULER-style HotpotQA examples while baselines are evaluated zero-shot without matching fine-tuning or latency improvements.

kgbdSBjGtq.one_liner: Formulates multi-group inference-time alignment under a shared sampling budget as maximin allocation using greedy and pessimistic best-of-N sampling.
kgbdSBjGtq.problem: When a single model serves diverse user groups or evaluation criteria with distinct reward models, allocating a finite shared inference-time sampling budget to protect worst-group quality under imperfect proxy rewards is unresolved.
kgbdSBjGtq.method: The authors formulate shared-budget inference-time alignment as a maximin budget allocation problem across groups. They analyze a greedy variant of Best-of-N (Greedy-BoN) for exact rewards and propose Batched Greedy Pessimistic (BGP) allocation, which uses pessimistic response selection to bound maximin regret against a proxy reward floor.
kgbdSBjGtq.key_idea: Allocates inference-time Best-of-N sampling batches greedily to the lowest-utility group using pessimistic reward estimates that account for proxy reward error.
kgbdSBjGtq.evidence: Theoretical regret bounds in exact-reward and proxy-reward settings, and empirical evaluation on a dataset spanning five domain groups.
kgbdSBjGtq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the Rawlsian maximin formulation of shared sampling budgets and the clear theoretical contrast between exact and imperfect proxy rewards.
kgbdSBjGtq.main_concern: Reviewers note that the experiments test disjoint domain prompts rather than conflicting group preferences on shared prompts, and adaptive allocation shows little empirical advantage over uniform pessimistic baselines.

JMwAql85jz.one_liner: Diagnoses robotic manipulation instruction following on 48 held-out RoboTwin 2.0 scenes using a sequential failure-attribution pipeline.
JMwAql85jz.problem: Aggregate task completion in robotic manipulation does not distinguish whether a policy genuinely follows the requested instruction or executes an instruction-independent routine learned from demonstrations.
JMwAql85jz.method: ManipScope defines an evaluation-only benchmark of 48 held-out scenes across six task families built on RoboTwin 2.0, where policies trained on unmodified demonstrations must reuse skills under changed task requirements. It pairs evaluation with a sequential chain of diagnostics and target-reassignment tests on identical initial states to isolate failure causes.
JMwAql85jz.key_idea: Tests policies trained on source demonstrations across held-out target-reassigned scenes and runs a sequential diagnostic chain to separate skill failures from instruction-following failures.
JMwAql85jz.evidence: Evaluated 12 policy checkpoints across 48 scenes (including 13,200 episodes on 11 selection scenes and 1,000 target-reassigned initial states) plus a GPT-6 agent positive control.
JMwAql85jz.claimed_gains: For twelve policy checkpoints, 84.6% of failures in 13,200 episodes on eleven selection scenes displace a distractor, and ten checkpoints follow every reassigned instruction on only 3.9% of 1,000 states (below 16% for an instruction-blind chooser), while a GPT-6 control reaches 88%.
JMwAql85jz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating instruction following from habit execution in robotic VLA models is well-motivated and value the granular failure and non-target grasp diagnostics.
JMwAql85jz.main_concern: Reviewers argue that evaluating on held-out scenes without training samples or direct verification of underlying skill mastery makes it hard to disentangle OOD execution failures from instruction-following failures.

Q1l5vgMXC4.one_liner: Coarsens text-attributed graphs by learning sparse soft node-to-anchor assignments primarily driven by pretrained text embedding reconstruction.
Q1l5vgMXC4.problem: Large scale and high-dimensional text semantics make GNN training on text-attributed graphs expensive, while existing graph coarsening methods prioritize topology over pretrained text semantics.
Q1l5vgMXC4.method: Adaptive Skeleton Coarsening (ASC) maps pretrained text embeddings and complementary structural descriptors through a joint encoder into a shared assignment space. It learns sparse soft node-to-anchor assignments using a semantic reconstruction loss and an auxiliary graph-level property prediction objective to export a compressed weighted skeleton graph.
Q1l5vgMXC4.key_idea: Uses a joint semantic-structural encoder trained with semantic feature reconstruction to learn sparse node-to-anchor soft assignments for graph contraction.
Q1l5vgMXC4.evidence: Evaluated across 11 text-attributed graph benchmarks at multiple compression ratios (including r=0.1 and r=0.01) across GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, and MLP architectures.
Q1l5vgMXC4.claimed_gains: At a compression ratio of r=0.1, ASC achieves the highest mean classification accuracy on all 11 benchmarks while substantially reducing peak memory consumption and training time of downstream GCNs, and maintains superior performance at r=0.01.
Q1l5vgMXC4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad evaluation across 11 datasets and multiple GNN backbones, as well as the practical memory and training-time savings from the reusable coarsened skeleton.
Q1l5vgMXC4.main_concern: Reviewers view the combination of K-means anchors, soft assignments, and feature reconstruction as incremental over existing feature-aware graph coarsening methods and ask for stronger text-only coreset baselines.

R2Mr0dlFxw.one_liner: Guides test-time text-to-video refinement by retrieving past trajectories from episodic memory to estimate decoupled quality and cost advantages.
R2Mr0dlFxw.problem: Iterative test-time text-to-video refinement methods process each prompt in isolation under fixed strategies, wasting expensive video generation calls and discarding experience from prior episodes.
R2Mr0dlFxw.method: Test-Time Policy Evolution (TTPE) is a training-free framework that stores completed refinement trajectories in an episodic memory. For a new prompt, it retrieves similar past trajectories to estimate decoupled long-horizon quality and cost advantages per action family, prunes Pareto-dominated actions in quality-cost space, and decides whether to stop or which refinement action to execute.
R2Mr0dlFxw.key_idea: Estimates decoupled long-horizon quality and generation-cost advantages from retrieved episodic refinement trajectories and selects non-dominated actions at test time.
R2Mr0dlFxw.evidence: Evaluated on text-to-video refinement benchmarks including StoryEval and VBench with generators such as HunyuanVideo against baselines like VISTA.
R2Mr0dlFxw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the training-free, practical approach to reducing expensive video generation calls while improving quality during test-time refinement.
R2Mr0dlFxw.main_concern: Reviewers question the sensitivity to prompt ordering as episodic memory accumulates online, note a reward definition flaw that penalizes temporary quality drops even when the max-quality video is returned, and point out code-paper discrepancies.

XOZ6lNL12D.one_liner: Detects runtime VLA backdoor activations on unseen tasks by monitoring input-token manifolds and adjacent-layer latent transition errors.
XOZ6lNL12D.problem: Detecting backdoor activation in Vision-Language-Action policies at runtime is difficult because malicious trajectories can consist of individually plausible actions while unseen tasks cause legitimate distributional shifts.
XOZ6lNL12D.method: TMT trains two monitoring branches on benign rollouts: a token manifold branch that assesses input-token structure and a latent transition branch that measures prediction errors in adjacent-layer latent dynamics, using confirmed suspicious rollouts to select transitions for monitoring. The paper also explores self-distillation for policy purification using benign-input actions from a frozen copy of the backdoored policy.
XOZ6lNL12D.key_idea: Combines input-token manifold anomaly scoring with adjacent-layer latent transition prediction error on benign rollouts to flag runtime backdoor triggers.
XOZ6lNL12D.evidence: Evaluated on unseen tasks across three VLA backdoor attacks against ten adapted backdoor, anomaly, and failure detection baselines, plus robot and purification experiments.
XOZ6lNL12D.claimed_gains: In a post-hoc comparison with ten baselines, TMT achieves state-of-the-art backdoor detection performance on unseen tasks across three VLA backdoor attacks.
XOZ6lNL12D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that runtime backdoor detection for VLA policies on unseen tasks is an important safety problem and appreciate the broad baseline adaptation and experimental scope.
XOZ6lNL12D.main_concern: Reviewers point out that incident-driven layer selection relies on observing an unverified suspicious rollout (blurring the benign-only threat model and risking confusion with benign OOD shifts) and lacks evaluation against adaptive white-box attackers.

kQI37ySWT6.one_liner: Credits visual agent crop actions during on-policy distillation by how much the executed crop reduces the teacher's answer entropy.
kQI37ySWT6.problem: In on-policy distillation for visual agents that crop before answering, action tokens are distilled before crop execution reveals their utility, improving the student's reader while degrading sampled crop precision toward a less precise teacher.
kQI37ySWT6.method: The authors diagnose this action-credit gap via reader-actor swaps and propose Execution-Conditioned Entropy Drop (Exec-ED). Without ground-truth labels, Exec-ED weights each sampled crop action by how much its executed image crop reduces the teacher's answer entropy relative to sibling crops sampled from the same state, combined with OPD's action KL.
kQI37ySWT6.key_idea: Weights sampled visual cropping actions during on-policy distillation by the sibling-centered reduction in teacher answer entropy after executing the crop.
kQI37ySWT6.evidence: Evaluated across two teacher sizes (including a 9B main setting) and two benchmarks including ZoomBench, with reader-actor swap diagnostics.
kQI37ySWT6.claimed_gains: In the main 9B setting, Exec-ED raises ZoomBench crop precision from 55.0% under OPD to 57.4–58.8% (Base: 59.2%) while maintaining comparable end-to-end accuracy.
kQI37ySWT6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean reader-actor swap diagnosis demonstrating that standard on-policy distillation improves crop reading while degrading sampled crop selection.
kQI37ySWT6.main_concern: Reviewers note that improved crop precision yields minimal end-to-end task accuracy gain, that ablating the action-KL anchor actually improves precision further (contradicting the anchoring narrative), and that evaluation is limited to single-crop four-option MCQs.

TQ2FLSi4wq.one_liner: Decomposes demographic disparities in RAG decision pipelines into database, retriever, and LLM aggregator contributions across causal fairness pathways.
TQ2FLSi4wq.problem: Existing fairness audits evaluate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems as a whole, leaving unclear whether demographic disparities stem from the historical database, the retrieval algorithm, or the LLM aggregator.
TQ2FLSi4wq.method: The authors model a RAG decision pipeline as a sequence of predictors coupled to a common underlying causal graph to decompose overall score disparity into contributions from the retrieval database, the retrieval algorithm, and the LLM aggregator. For causal fairness metrics, they further decompose each component's disparity contribution into direct, indirect, and spurious causal pathways.
TQ2FLSi4wq.key_idea: Models RAG as a sequence of stage-wise conditional score predictors over a shared causal graph to telescope total disparity across pipeline components and causal paths.
TQ2FLSi4wq.evidence: Theoretical decomposition proofs and empirical evaluations on semi-synthetic and real-world decision tasks across multiple retriever, race-disclosure, and fine-tuning configurations.
TQ2FLSi4wq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the rigorous causal formalization and the actionable, granular decomposition of fairness disparities across RAG components and causal pathways.
TQ2FLSi4wq.main_concern: Reviewers note that component attributions depend on the choice of auxiliary intermediate retrieval predictor, confidence intervals omit database sampling variance, and simplified RAG assumptions may not cover complex multi-tool pipelines.

lHCbJoYyFL.one_liner: Measures sycophancy across 13 checkpoints from 5 open LM lineages, separating initial answer firmness from claim push to distinguish deference from capitulation.
lHCbJoYyFL.problem: Prior studies disagree on whether sycophancy originates in pretraining or preference post-training because raw answer-flip rates confound how strongly a model holds its initial answer with how much an injected user claim shifts it.
lHCbJoYyFL.method: The authors evaluate 13 checkpoints across 5 open model lineages from base pretrained models through SFT and preference optimization, decomposing log-odds shifts into initial answer firmness (gap) and claim effect (push) across matched-firmness strata. They vary source credibility, claim strength, and single-turn prompt injection versus two-turn conversational objection.
lHCbJoYyFL.key_idea: Separates initial answer log-odds margin from claim-induced log-odds shift across matched firmness strata along training checkpoints to isolate prompt deference from conversational capitulation.
lHCbJoYyFL.evidence: Evaluated across 13 open checkpoints from 5 model lineages (7–8B primary models plus within-family size controls) on four multiple-choice datasets.
lHCbJoYyFL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating initial answer firmness from claim push across matched training checkpoints clarifies prior contradictions and cleanly distinguishes prompt deference from conversational capitulation.
lHCbJoYyFL.main_concern: Reviewers note that measuring logits at a single immediate multiple-choice answer token (with only a first-letter generation check) may not reflect full reasoning generations, and tested lineages are mostly 7–8B models where training stages vary both data and recipe.

e22tHE09ot.one_liner: Trains a historical frame compressor for long video generation via on-policy distillation using the same frozen generator as teacher and student.
e22tHE09ot.problem: Autoregressive video generators suffer from long-context degradation as frame history grows, while key-frame selection methods discard historical information needed for consistent future generation.
e22tHE09ot.method: Prediction-Aligned Context Compaction (PACC) introduces a learned compressor that aggregates past frames into compact memory tokens for a frozen video generator. The compressor is trained via on-policy distillation where the frozen generator conditioned on compressed memory acts as the student generating continuations, and the same frozen generator conditioned on the full history acts as the teacher providing denoising targets.
e22tHE09ot.key_idea: Updates only a history compressor by matching denoising predictions of a frozen video generator conditioned on compressed memory against the same generator conditioned on full history.
e22tHE09ot.evidence: Evaluated on MBench (using Causal-rCM and Causal Forcing backbones) and VBench-Long with MovieGen prompts.
e22tHE09ot.claimed_gains: PACC outperforms the strongest baseline on MBench by 6.63 points on Causal-rCM and 3.19 points on Causal Forcing.
e22tHE09ot.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate training the memory compressor directly for prediction preservation on a frozen video generator without requiring generator fine-tuning.
e22tHE09ot.main_concern: Reviewers point out an uncredited similarity to TinyHistory, unmatched active context token budgets against baselines (7,956 vs. 6,240 tokens), and single-seed evaluations on short (26-second) memory tests.

pj6t9B9bGN.one_liner: Forecasts time-series responses to counterfactual free-form event descriptions using a conditional diffusion model with factorized conditioning and swap objectives.
