pj6t9B9bGN.problem: While text descriptions of exogenous events improve factual time-series forecasting, existing models may not produce the appropriate numerical direction and magnitude changes when the same history is paired with a counterfactual free-form event description.
pj6t9B9bGN.method: The authors propose MEETS, a conditional diffusion model for multimodal time-series forecasting that uses factorized history-event conditioning. They train it with matched conditioning-swap objectives that encourage the denoiser to rely on both the numerical history and the free-form event text.
pj6t9B9bGN.key_idea: Combines factorized history-and-event diffusion conditioning with matched conditioning-swap training objectives to enforce sensitivity to counterfactual event text.
pj6t9B9bGN.evidence: Evaluated across traffic, energy, and treatment-response domains on factual forecasting, counterfactual event responses, and unseen event configurations.
pj6t9B9bGN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find counterfactual exogenous event forecasting well-motivated and acknowledge strong empirical performance across simulated and real-world datasets.
pj6t9B9bGN.main_concern: Reviewers question the reliability of DTW nearest-neighbor proxies used as counterfactual ground truth on real-world datasets, potential temporal confounding in swapped event texts, and dense presentation that relegates key unseen-event results to the appendix.

C5y0EAtAV9.one_liner: OpenSIR alternates teacher and student roles within one model, using diversity rewards and difficulty calibration for self-generated reasoning training.
C5y0EAtAV9.problem: Existing self-play methods lack sustained exploration and provide marginal or negative gains on post-trained reasoning models.
C5y0EAtAV9.method: A shared LLM generates and solves problems from a single seed without annotated data or external verifiers. Diversity rewards encourage unfamiliar concepts, difficulty calibration keeps tasks learnable, and majority answers supervise the student.
C5y0EAtAV9.key_idea: A shared teacher-student policy combines embedding-based diversity rewards, calibrated problem difficulty, and majority-answer supervision in a self-play loop.
C5y0EAtAV9.evidence: Experiments cover four instruction-tuned and reasoning models, seven math benchmarks, three general-reasoning benchmarks, and ablations of diversity and teacher training.
C5y0EAtAV9.claimed_gains: OpenSIR averages +3.6 on instruction models and +3.1 on reasoning models, surpasses GRPO trained on over 7K examples, and improves reasoning models by at least +4.4 points across three general-reasoning benchmarks.
C5y0EAtAV9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the gains across multiple starting models and the ablations supporting diversity rewards in mathematical self-improvement.
C5y0EAtAV9.main_concern: The contribution is insufficiently distinguished from prior shared-policy self-play and diversity-based problem-generation methods.

gkKjjKOXvb.one_liner: Mold-Instruct recovers standalone repository tests and code, then uses execution to construct and diagnose target-specific instruction data.
gkKjjKOXvb.problem: Synthetic tests can provide unreliable functional supervision when constructing code instruction-tuning data.
gkKjjKOXvb.method: Mold-Instruct converts repository-dependent tests into standalone executable test-code pairs. Test requirements guide instruction construction, while execution verifies samples and supports heuristic diagnosis of the target model's capabilities.
gkKjjKOXvb.key_idea: Recovered repository tests supply functional requirements and execution feedback for constructing training instructions tailored to a target code model.
gkKjjKOXvb.evidence: The pipeline constructs 46.7K test-code pairs and evaluates code generation with Qwen3-4B-Base and SmolLM3-3B-Base on standalone programming benchmarks including HumanEval and MBPP.
gkKjjKOXvb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard recovering executable supervision from real repository tests as a practical and useful engineering contribution.
gkKjjKOXvb.main_concern: The evaluation has limited scope, focusing on standalone programming tasks and small Python code models despite using repository-derived supervision.

YRq6mNzddk.one_liner: Random-walk spectral moment changes score edge removals and guide graph sampling toward target structural summaries.
YRq6mNzddk.problem: Local edge-removal decisions need an efficient measure of their effect on global graph structure.
YRq6mNzddk.method: The framework summarizes graphs through spectral moments of the random-walk transition matrix and scores edge changes by induced moment differences. Closed-form low-order updates use maintained local statistics, while a low-rank formulation supports arbitrary moment orders and batched removals.
YRq6mNzddk.key_idea: Measure each edge change by its effect on random-walk spectral moments, computed through local closed forms or endpoint-based low-rank updates.
YRq6mNzddk.evidence: Exact derivations and graph-sampling experiments assess moment changes and related structural properties against uniform random removal.
YRq6mNzddk.claimed_gains: For single-edge removal with a fixed number of moments, the low-rank method reduces cost from O(mn) to O(m), while low-order combinatorial updates take constant time with maintained statistics.
YRq6mNzddk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the interpretable moment-based edge signatures and efficient exact computations.
YRq6mNzddk.main_concern: Structural-preservation evaluation largely measures functions of the optimized moments, leaving broader graph properties insufficiently tested.

DpAo2wMfF9.one_liner: Direction-based weight clustering allocates local LoRA ranks according to frozen-weight spectral concentration.
DpAo2wMfF9.problem: Uniform projection-level LoRA ranks ignore spectral heterogeneity among local weight submatrices.
DpAo2wMfF9.method: GDPLoRA partitions frozen weight matrices into domains through direction-based clustering and redistributes a fixed per-projection rank budget using local spectral concentration. Offline grouping and rank assignment preserve exact merging without input-dependent routing.
DpAo2wMfF9.key_idea: Cluster pretrained weight directions into local domains and allocate each domain's adaptation rank using its spectral concentration.
DpAo2wMfF9.evidence: Experiments compare PEFT baselines across multiple models and tasks, with grouping and rank-allocation ablations.
DpAo2wMfF9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find within-matrix rank allocation well motivated by local spectral heterogeneity and supported by multi-model evaluations.
DpAo2wMfF9.main_concern: The spectral descriptor's ability to identify which groups benefit from additional rank lacks a clear general justification.

vvJWhc1ybk.one_liner: Diagnostic actions infer failure scope and produce capability contracts that restrict subsequent embodied-agent actions.
vvJWhc1ybk.problem: Repeated failures waste interactions, but isolated failures do not reveal whether a limitation is global, local, or temporary.
vvJWhc1ybk.method: WIMW uses reference tests and target verification to create cross-task capability contracts enforced by an execution guard. Patch-VOI selects diagnostic tests by expected reduction in scope errors while accounting for evidence-acquisition cost.
vvJWhc1ybk.key_idea: Use active tests to infer the scope of a failure, verify the resulting capability contract, and enforce it across future tasks.
vvJWhc1ybk.evidence: A frozen Qwen3-VL-32B planner runs 300-task streams on EB-ALFRED and EB-Habitat with injected faults and matched passive-inference controls.
vvJWhc1ybk.claimed_gains: Under injected skill-wide faults, unexplained failed picks fall by 95.0% and 96.0% versus No update, with further reductions of 12.3% and 13.3% versus passive global inference at unchanged mean completion.
vvJWhc1ybk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value framing reusable failure memory as a decision about how broadly a failure should restrict future actions.
vvJWhc1ybk.main_concern: Predefined faults restricted to a narrow skill interface do not establish effectiveness for the diversity of real embodied failures.

QImJkZ333v.one_liner: Calibrated observability gates flow-generated high-frequency residuals around a deterministic metalens reconstruction.
QImJkZ333v.problem: Generative metalens reconstruction can invent details where measurements do not uniquely determine image content.
QImJkZ333v.method: PCAR-Flow estimates local observability from optical transfer, sensor noise, and image statistics. A deterministic path reconstructs supported content, while conditional flow matching proposes unresolved high-frequency residuals subject to physical admission cues.
QImJkZ333v.key_idea: Separate deterministic measurement-supported reconstruction from flow-generated high-frequency residuals and gate residual admission using calibrated local observability.
QImJkZ333v.evidence: Reconstruction experiments, component ablations, frozen-weight transfer between two metalenses, and local-Gaussian uncertainty analysis support the method.
QImJkZ333v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers support separating reliable reconstruction from generated detail to balance perceptual quality with physical consistency.
QImJkZ333v.main_concern: Generalization of the calibrated reconstruction and admission gate beyond the tested optical systems and training conditions remains insufficiently established.

zX5MagxsNm.one_liner: Matched industrial-inspection episodes vary evidence access while trace-level scoring distinguishes acquired evidence from final-action correctness.
zX5MagxsNm.problem: Outcome-oriented inspection benchmarks cannot determine whether agents acquired the evidence required for operational decisions.
zX5MagxsNm.method: InspectionBench compiles grounded worlds into matched scenarios that vary evidence visibility, tool access, temporal validity, and guidance while preserving the world and gold decision. Agents collect provenance-tracked evidence and execute inspections before choosing operational actions.
zX5MagxsNm.key_idea: Hold the underlying world and correct decision fixed while varying evidence access and checking acquisition traces separately from final decisions.
zX5MagxsNm.evidence: The benchmark contains 4,120 episodes from 1,552 worlds and 21 templates across six asset types, evaluated with five frontier models.
zX5MagxsNm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value controlled scenario generation and separating final decision accuracy from successful evidence acquisition.
zX5MagxsNm.main_concern: Evidence acquisition checks do not establish whether agents actually used the acquired evidence to make their decisions.

mDDEcTyT5B.one_liner: Group-shared low-rank subspaces and Nyström neuron compression jointly reduce MoE expert storage without training.
mDDEcTyT5B.problem: Sparse expert activation reduces computation but leaves MoE parameter storage expensive.
mDDEcTyT5B.method: GS-MoE shares low-rank representations across expert groups while retaining expert-specific projections and compresses intermediate neurons with Nyström approximations. Reconstruction-energy gains guide grouping, and gradient-free layer importance allocates rank and width budgets.
mDDEcTyT5B.key_idea: Compress across experts through shared subspaces and within experts through Nyström width reduction, allocating budgets from calibration-based reconstruction statistics.
mDDEcTyT5B.evidence: Experiments on DeepSeek-MoE-16B-Base, Qwen, and Mixtral compare joint compression with rank-only and width-only variants.
mDDEcTyT5B.claimed_gains: At a 60% reduction in routed-expert parameters on DeepSeek-MoE-16B-Base, GS-MoE retains over 92% of average reasoning performance versus 73% for D²-MoE and achieves 30% lower out-of-domain perplexity.
mDDEcTyT5B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the framework's separate control of shared-subspace capacity and individual expert width without retraining.
mDDEcTyT5B.main_concern: The full framework does not consistently outperform simpler width-only compression, leaving the added benefit of subspace sharing unclear.

MOmf9cjGQ2.one_liner: Single-object scene edits test whether embodied VLM planners maintain earlier safety refusals.
MOmf9cjGQ2.problem: Fixed-scene safety tests do not measure whether an existing refusal survives an ordinary environmental change.
MOmf9cjGQ2.method: The study inserts everyday objects into scenes for tasks a constitution-guarded planner initially refused and checks for compliance reversals. It compares fixed-list and task-specific objects and uses open-source VLM signals to predict task susceptibility.
MOmf9cjGQ2.key_idea: Retest initially refused tasks after inserting one everyday object into the scene, measuring refusal reversals across object choices.
MOmf9cjGQ2.evidence: Experiments cover 846 initially refused tasks, synthetic diffusion-based scene edits, clean-image re-queries, and cross-model susceptibility prediction.
MOmf9cjGQ2.claimed_gains: One or more object insertions flip 20.2% of the 846 initially refused tasks to compliance.
MOmf9cjGQ2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that refusal stability under ordinary environmental changes exposes a useful gap in embodied-agent safety evaluation.
MOmf9cjGQ2.main_concern: Diffusion-edited images do not establish that real physical object placement causes the same refusal reversals.

kgAnVLWStL.one_liner: Latent conditional flow matching generates weather chunks that compose into six-hourly subseasonal ensembles.
kgAnVLWStL.problem: Subseasonal forecasting needs large ensembles that retain slowly evolving signals beyond initial-state predictability.
kgAnVLWStL.method: Marchuk-S2S trains a Transformer in a frozen weather autoencoder's latent space, conditioned on one atmospheric state and time of year. A single model trained on 1- to 8-day chunks rolls out autoregressively to 48 days.
kgAnVLWStL.key_idea: Jointly sample multi-day latent weather chunks with conditional flow matching and compose them autoregressively using a single checkpoint.
kgAnVLWStL.evidence: Tests over 2019-2021 compare LaDCast, FuXi-S2S, and the 51-member ECMWF ensemble using anomaly correlation, MJO skill, and CRPS.
kgAnVLWStL.claimed_gains: A 276M-parameter backbone matches LaDCast's medium-range skill versus 1.6B parameters, generating a 50-member, 48-day ensemble in 9.7 minutes on one H100 GPU, 7.6× faster.
kgAnVLWStL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize efficient long-range six-hourly ensemble generation with competitive performance against established forecasting systems.
kgAnVLWStL.main_concern: Precipitation and late-lead MJO performance remain weaker than key baselines, limiting the practical advantage of the efficiency gains.

2YtEGorbS3.one_liner: Paired RGB-event observations and aligned arm-hand references support joint upper-body and hand reconstruction.
2YtEGorbS3.problem: Hand-only event models miss body-induced motion ambiguity, while coupled arm-hand annotation often disrupts natural observations or wrist continuity.
2YtEGorbS3.method: EvUBody pairs simulated and real RGB-event observations with spatially aligned upper-body and detailed hand references. Its reconstruction model fuses RGB-event features and decodes hand joints relative to predicted body wrists.
2YtEGorbS3.key_idea: Fuse RGB-event features for joint body-hand estimation and express hand joints relative to body wrists to enforce wrist consistency.
2YtEGorbS3.evidence: The real subset contains 1,809 sequences from 15 participants across 120 tasks, with participant-disjoint splits and separate evaluation of timestamps lacking current RGB observations.
2YtEGorbS3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the dataset's coordinated upper-body and hand annotations paired with real event observations during natural manipulation.
2YtEGorbS3.main_concern: Missing matched hand-only and real-event RGB-only controls leave the claimed resolution of motion ambiguity insufficiently isolated.

ythPZ2iLaD.one_liner: Synthetic label-shift pretraining and inducing-token query summaries amortize adaptation of tabular in-context predictions.
ythPZ2iLaD.problem: Tabular foundation models that assume fixed class proportions can lose accuracy and calibration under label shift.
ythPZ2iLaD.method: ShiftICL pretrains on synthetic tasks with varied label distributions and shift severities. Inducing tokens summarize unlabeled query representations so the model can adjust predictions to target class proportions without retraining or test labels.
ythPZ2iLaD.key_idea: Train on shifted class priors while conditioning predictions on an inducing-token summary of the unlabeled query population.
ythPZ2iLaD.evidence: Evaluation spans 205 OpenML tabular datasets under controlled label shift, with smaller synthetic-task ablations.
ythPZ2iLaD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find label-shift adaptation through synthetic pretraining and unlabeled query-set conditioning well motivated.
ythPZ2iLaD.main_concern: Main comparisons change both pretraining and query conditioning, while limited ablations do not isolate their contributions at benchmark scale.

ocu4ln0Y39.one_liner: Conditional masked diffusion branches codeword candidates and prunes parity violations during error-correcting decoding.
ocu4ln0Y39.problem: Committing early to uncertain codeword bits can propagate decoding errors.
ocu4ln0Y39.method: A neural decoder estimates bit posteriors from fixed channel observations and a progressively revealed codeword. Maxwell beam search maintains multiple trajectories, prunes parity-infeasible candidates, and ranks survivors by accumulated reverse-transition log probabilities.
ocu4ln0Y39.key_idea: Maintain multiple masked-diffusion decoding paths, prune parity-infeasible branches, and rank surviving paths by reverse-transition probabilities.
ocu4ln0Y39.evidence: Experiments evaluate Polar, LDPC, and BCH codes with BPSK transmission over AWGN, comparing beam and single-trajectory decoding.
ocu4ln0Y39.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize consistent decoding gains from maintaining multiple candidates and applying code constraints.
ocu4ln0Y39.main_concern: The experiments do not adequately isolate diffusion's contribution from the gains of beam search and its associated decoding components.

ouOYsA7iRg.one_liner: Couples explicit SE(3) residue frame transport with continuous sequence-atom latents via flow matching for cyclic peptides.
ouOYsA7iRg.problem: Generating cyclic peptides requires satisfying sparse, nonlocal covalent ring-closure constraints across linked residues without degrading local stereochemical geometry.
ouOYsA7iRg.method: LaCPlow is a target-conditioned partially latent flow-matching model that explicitly transports residue rigid frames (rotations and translations) while encoding amino acid identities and local atomic coordinates in a continuous latent space. A specialized variant, LaCPlow-Cyc, adds cyclization-specific geometric supervision to a joint rotational, translational, and latent velocity network.
ouOYsA7iRg.key_idea: Jointly flow explicit SE(3) residue frames alongside continuous sequence and local-atom latents, adding cyclization supervision to enforce nonlocal ring-closure geometry.
ouOYsA7iRg.evidence: Evaluated with base and cyclization-supervised models trained from scratch on CPCore across bond-closure geometry, stereochemical quality, binding scores, and diversity.
ouOYsA7iRg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining explicit residue rigid frames with partially latent local structure is well suited to cyclic peptide ring-closure geometry and achieves strong pre-minimization closure rates.
ouOYsA7iRg.main_concern: Architectural novelty over existing partially latent protein flow models is incremental, structural diversity drops noticeably, and distance-window closure proxies leave ~39% of raw samples unclosed.

tvr3KccJz9.one_liner: Diagnoses LoRA backdoors via weight comparison to invented-trigger surrogates and applies mechanism-specific activation repair.
tvr3KccJz9.problem: Existing trigger-free backdoor defenses fail consistently across diverse attack objectives because they do not distinguish backdoors that insert new activation directions from those that hijack native model circuits.
tvr3KccJz9.method: TRIAGE trains reference surrogate backdoors with invented triggers and uses a weight-only router to classify a suspect adapter as either inserting a behavioral direction or diverting an existing circuit. For inserted directions it applies activation ablation along surrogate-derived directions followed by fine-tuning, while attenuating backdoor influence for diverted circuits.
tvr3KccJz9.key_idea: Route suspect adapters by weight similarity against invented-trigger surrogate backdoors to choose between surrogate-direction activation ablation and circuit-preserving attenuation.
tvr3KccJz9.evidence: Evaluated across five trigger formats and three attack objectives (jailbreak, negative sentiment, targeted refusal) on BackdoorLLM adapters including Llama-2-7B.
tvr3KccJz9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that distinguishing inserted behavioral directions from diverted native circuits provides a useful mechanistic explanation for trigger-free LoRA backdoor defense.
tvr3KccJz9.main_concern: Shared poisoned target datasets between surrogate and test adapters confound the claimed shared direction, and trigger-free hyperparameter selection and broader attack coverage remain undervalidated.

DIoUssxjoe.one_liner: Proves condition-number-independent logarithmic convergence for exact-polar Muon with momentum via scalar spectral dynamics reduction.
DIoUssxjoe.problem: Despite strong empirical LLM pretraining results, Muon's convergence rate and preconditioning advantages over Adam in the presence of momentum lack formal theoretical guarantees.
DIoUssxjoe.method: The authors analyze Muon with exact spectral orthogonalization and geometrically decaying step sizes on symmetric matrix factorization and structured softmax-attention in-context learning by reducing matrix updates to scalar spectral-mode recursions and bounding momentum overshoot. They also construct structured problem instances comparing Muon's iteration complexity directly against full-batch Adam.
DIoUssxjoe.key_idea: Reduce exact spectral-orthogonalized momentum updates to decoupled scalar spectral recursions to eliminate condition-number dependence under geometrically decaying learning rates.
DIoUssxjoe.evidence: Supported by theoretical convergence upper bounds, lower bounds against full-batch Adam on infinite-prompt in-context learning and matrix factorization, and numerical simulations.
DIoUssxjoe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the reduction to scalar spectral dynamics clearly explains how spectral orthogonalization equalizes progress across modes to remove condition-number dependence.
DIoUssxjoe.main_concern: Guarantees rely on spectral alignment and restrictive initialization and decay conditions—with hidden constants blowing up near unit momentum—that may not transfer to general neural networks.

vsh53iMl9J.one_liner: Recalibrates vision-language candidate probabilities at inference by prioritizing attended visual tokens that suppress rival answers.
vsh53iMl9J.problem: Large vision-language models frequently hallucinate incorrect answers even when their attention concentrates on the task-relevant visual region.
vsh53iMl9J.method: After finding that hallucinated responses lack 'inhibitory support tokens' that suppress competing candidates within attended regions, the authors introduce SPEAR, a training-free inference method. SPEAR selects an attention-derived region, prioritizes inhibitory support tokens while keeping direct and opposing token signals, and aggregates signed responses to recalibrate candidate probabilities within a bounded shift.
vsh53iMl9J.key_idea: Identify attended visual tokens that suppress competing answer candidates and aggregate their signed directional responses to recalibrate decoding probabilities without training.
vsh53iMl9J.evidence: Evaluated across multiple object hallucination benchmarks and LVLM families, accompanied by token-evidence analyses and matched-count ablations.
vsh53iMl9J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that analyzing rival-suppressing visual tokens inside attended regions offers an insightful perspective on LVLM hallucinations with solid multi-benchmark results.
vsh53iMl9J.main_concern: The manuscript is difficult to follow due to undefined jargon and opaque notation, and the link between inhibitory token counts and hallucinations lacks direct causal intervention tests.

Rj74QQxjOh.one_liner: Feasibility-first initial-noise optimization separately handles constraints and rewards in pretrained generative models.
Rj74QQxjOh.problem: Inference-time scientific inverse design typically steers generation toward either a target property or domain constraints.
Rj74QQxjOh.method: FINO optimizes the initial noise of pretrained diffusion or flow models, taking a constraint-restoration step outside the feasible set and a reward step inside it without retraining or tradeoff weights.
Rj74QQxjOh.key_idea: Alternate constraint-restoration and reward steps in initial-noise space so reward updates begin only inside the feasible set.
Rj74QQxjOh.evidence: Topological photonic inverse design and molecule generation test target-property error and constraint satisfaction, with independent FDTD simulations noted by reviewers.
Rj74QQxjOh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that feasibility-first optimization is intuitive and training-free, with promising constrained results for out-of-distribution targets.
Rj74QQxjOh.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite missing ablations and theory for the complete algorithm, leaving the factorization's benefit and convergence unclear.

sYlzZaMPnS.one_liner: Balanced cross-expert parameter updates embed multi-bit watermarks recoverable through sign voting without inference.
sYlzZaMPnS.problem: MoE parameter watermarks concentrated in a few experts are vulnerable to localized damage and must preserve model utility.
sYlzZaMPnS.method: SparseMark combines balanced expert allocation, response-based carrier selection, antisymmetric updates, and keyed block ordering, with verification by unit sign voting against stored baselines.
sYlzZaMPnS.key_idea: Spread antisymmetric codeword updates across experts with keyed block ordering, then recover bits by bounded unit-sign voting.
sYlzZaMPnS.evidence: Controlled experiments on three MoE backbones test clean 256-bit recovery, with OLMoE pruning, quantization, fine-tuning, and feedback-guided attack evaluations.
sYlzZaMPnS.claimed_gains: SparseMark achieves exact clean recovery of 256-bit codewords across three MoE backbones with small measured changes in perplexity.
sYlzZaMPnS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that balanced carrier allocation is a coherent MoE-specific design with lightweight verification and small utility effects.
sYlzZaMPnS.main_concern: The main concern is insufficiently established security, including unclear threat assumptions and limited distributed adaptive-attack tests.

jlYMtc9x7G.one_liner: A 3.18-million-trace benchmark tests structural representations on intrinsic, retrieval, and faulty-deployment tasks.
jlYMtc9x7G.problem: Distributed traces support production-system operations but have received little attention in machine-learning representation research.
jlYMtc9x7G.method: Iditarod combines commercial telemetry with Uber traces and four intrinsic or downstream tasks, evaluating text, call-path, and graph trace encoders.
jlYMtc9x7G.key_idea: Evaluate trace embeddings through property-preservation tasks and downstream retrieval and multimodal faulty-deployment detection on real traces.
jlYMtc9x7G.evidence: Iditarod evaluates twenty trace embedding methods on 3.18 million commercial traces plus Uber traces across four tasks.
jlYMtc9x7G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the large real-world corpus, expert-validated retrieval labels, and broad model evaluation benefit trace representation research.
jlYMtc9x7G.main_concern: Reviewers most often question construct validity and statistical support, especially handcrafted retrieval labels and only 169 faulty deployments.

Gccrrp7VGt.one_liner: Compatibility-guided rules redescribe sensory and behavioral features to improve linear prediction of neural responses.
Gccrrp7VGt.problem: Neural selectivity labels depend on an experimenter's fixed feature description, which can obscure linear dependence under a better description.
Gccrrp7VGt.method: A population encoder and sparse autoencoder generate activation patterns, which language-model proposals and shallow trees convert into executable binary rules selected for linear neural prediction.
Gccrrp7VGt.key_idea: Discover executable binary features whose descriptions make population responses predictable by a specified simple readout.
Gccrrp7VGt.evidence: Recordings from 575 mouse S1 neurons across 22 sessions are evaluated with four-fold nested cross-validation and a catalog of 164 full-data features.
Gccrrp7VGt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicit neural-encoding rules are potentially useful and that nested validation and held-out tests provide careful evaluation.
Gccrrp7VGt.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether the SAE and formal framework add value beyond decision-tree rules and known feature transformations.

S8lE8gliUO.one_liner: GNN predictions and neighborhood context augment tabular graph tools for LLM node classification.
S8lE8gliUO.problem: Graph-as-Code access does not ensure that LLMs capture local neighbor structure or global data bias in tabular graphs.
S8lE8gliUO.method: SCT varies interaction mode, GNN-prediction or topic-summary content, k-hop or random-walk aggregation, and model-dataset configuration to supply structural context.
S8lE8gliUO.key_idea: Supply graph-as-code inference with GNN predictions or topic summaries aggregated through k-hop neighborhoods or random walks.
S8lE8gliUO.evidence: Error-overlap and oracle analyses motivate fusion, followed by node-classification experiments across ten datasets and component ablations.
S8lE8gliUO.claimed_gains: Across ten datasets, SCT improves node classification accuracy by an average of 3.51 percentage points over the SCT-O baseline.
S8lE8gliUO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the complementarity analysis is clear and that GNN-prediction augmentation consistently helps across datasets.
S8lE8gliUO.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite missing simple fusion baselines and unclear method descriptions, leaving the source of modest gains uncertain.

K0XaXJFxdF.one_liner: Event-gated Householder transitions and binary-addressed associative memory reduce recurrent computation without perplexity loss.
K0XaXJFxdF.problem: Efficient sequence models still couple per-token transition work and associative storage, limiting event-proportional computation and fixed-size recall.
K0XaXJFxdF.method: FLINT applies a diagonal carry at every token and Householder transformations only at selected events, while EGAM stores associations through binary addressing, gated additive writes, and normalized reads.
K0XaXJFxdF.key_idea: Apply expressive recurrent transitions only at selected events while storing associations separately in fixed-size, binary-addressed slots.
K0XaXJFxdF.evidence: Shared-backbone synthetic tasks and WikiText-103 and FineWeb-Edu language modeling measure execution, arithmetic cost, state size, and perplexity.
K0XaXJFxdF.claimed_gains: At known-mask density 0.1 and length 2048, the block runs 1.2× faster than Gated DeltaNet-2; mixer MACs fall from 0.865M to 0.469M per token and layer, while WikiText-103 perplexity changes from 26.705 to 26.709.
K0XaXJFxdF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating tracking from recall is well motivated and that controlled synthetic and matched language-model tests show minimal perplexity change.
K0XaXJFxdF.main_concern: Reviewers most often question FLINT's language-model contribution and practical efficiency because gains follow EGAM and arithmetic savings lack direct hardware measurement.

aqsOlxs5FH.one_liner: Closed-form automorphisms on generalized symplectic bounded domains support geometry-aware representation learning.
aqsOlxs5FH.problem: Existing Siegel-disk networks leave broader symplectic-group geometries and their learnable representations insufficiently explored.
aqsOlxs5FH.method: The paper constructs upper half-space and precompact models for symplectic groups over involutive algebras and derives closed-form automorphisms and inverses for neural networks on bounded domains.
aqsOlxs5FH.key_idea: Construct precompact models for symplectic groups over involutive algebras and implement neural mappings through closed-form automorphisms.
aqsOlxs5FH.evidence: The mappings are evaluated on radar clutter classification, action recognition, graph reconstruction, and node classification.
aqsOlxs5FH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the mathematical development is principled and that models outperform Siegel and SPD baselines on most evaluated tasks.
aqsOlxs5FH.main_concern: Reviewers most often question which mathematical constructions exceed classical bounded-domain results and ask for clearer intuition.

vb7DK4t9I8.one_liner: Trajectory routing selects masked subnetworks with gated low-rank expansion for task-agnostic continual offline RL.
vb7DK4t9I8.problem: Continual offline RL must retain and transfer knowledge across differing dynamics without requiring task identities at inference.
vb7DK4t9I8.method: RMDT allocates learnable binary-mask subnetworks with capacity regularization and gated low-rank expansion, while a classifier and Gaussian prototype router infers tasks from multi-step trajectories.
vb7DK4t9I8.key_idea: Route trajectories to task prototypes while allocating reusable parameter masks and on-demand low-rank capacity without test-time task labels.
vb7DK4t9I8.evidence: Reviews report task-agnostic comparisons on ten-task and twenty-task benchmarks, with routing analyses and prototype, replay, and capacity ablations.
vb7DK4t9I8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that task-agnostic deployment is relevant and that the combined routing and parameter-management design gives consistent improvements.
vb7DK4t9I8.main_concern: Reviewers most often question methodological novelty and attribution because masking resembles prior work and key matched baselines are missing.

MQjtWfeS5T.one_liner: Models two-channel spoken dialogue in continuous VAE latent space via an interleaved text-speech stream and autoregressive flow matching.
MQjtWfeS5T.problem: Existing spoken dialogue language models rely on discrete semantic tokens that limit fine-grained acoustic modeling and do not generalize across diverse speech generation tasks.
MQjtWfeS5T.method: CSDLM serializes time-aligned two-channel dialogue into an interleaved text and continuous VAE-latent stream modeled by an autoregressive Transformer (initialized from Qwen3.5-2B) with flow-matching speech heads and voice-prompt CFG.
MQjtWfeS5T.key_idea: Unifies two-channel spoken dialogue and TTS in a single model by autoregressively predicting interleaved text and continuous VAE speech latents with flow matching.
MQjtWfeS5T.evidence: Evaluated on dialogue continuation, script-to-dialogue generation, contextual TTS, and streaming TTS using automatic metrics (WER, speaker similarity, coherence).
MQjtWfeS5T.claimed_gains: Improves semantic dialogue coherence by almost 2x compared to dGSLM while matching lexical and timbre fidelity in streaming.
MQjtWfeS5T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying two-channel dialogue and diverse speech generation tasks in a single continuous-latent checkpoint is clean and versatile.
MQjtWfeS5T.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the comparison against dGSLM confounds continuous latents with text interleaving, pretrained LLM initialization, and training data, and note missing human listening tests and novelty overlap with CoVoMix/Delayed Streams.

pBwc39lFMY.one_liner: Derives exact high-dimensional ODE dynamics for LoRA continual learning and proposes state-dependent hidden-unit masking to reduce forgetting.
pBwc39lFMY.problem: The mechanisms by which LoRA rank, initialization, and task similarity govern catastrophic forgetting and plasticity in continual learning are poorly understood.
pBwc39lFMY.method: The authors derive a closed system of ODEs for macroscopic order parameters in a two-task online teacher-student model under LoRA fine-tuning, and propose State-Dependent Gradient Masking (SDGM) to freeze hidden units carrying strong Task 1 representations.
pBwc39lFMY.key_idea: Solves exact online-learning ODEs for two-task LoRA adaptation and freezes hidden units with the largest first-task representations via state-dependent masking.
pBwc39lFMY.evidence: Analytical ODE solutions matched against finite-dimensional teacher-student simulations, ReLU/inverse-selection checks, and a binary MNIST classification experiment.
pBwc39lFMY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the ODE dynamical theory of continual LoRA matches numerical simulations well and yields clear insights into rank and task similarity.
pBwc39lFMY.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that validation is restricted to a two-layer, two-task teacher-student setup and binary MNIST, lacking deeper models, multi-task sequences, and a random-masking baseline for SDGM.

DmwT6JI4Ek.one_liner: Adaptively reweights expert model logits at each token using implicit log-likelihood rewards to maximize the worst-case alignment objective.
DmwT6JI4Ek.problem: Training-free multi-objective decoding methods use fixed aggregation weights across all prompts and tokens, failing to resolve context-dependent conflicts among alignment objectives.
DmwT6JI4Ek.method: TAMD computes implicit reward signals from the expert models' own token log-likelihoods during decoding and dynamically shifts aggregation weights toward the current bottleneck (worst-performing) objective at each token position.
DmwT6JI4Ek.key_idea: Dynamically reweights multiple expert models' logits per token toward the lowest-scoring objective estimated from cumulative implicit log-likelihood rewards.
DmwT6JI4Ek.evidence: Evaluated on safety-helpfulness and multi-objective alignment tasks using 1B, 3B, and 8B models scored by reward models.
DmwT6JI4Ek.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that token-level adaptive weighting for training-free max-min alignment is well-motivated, practical, and improves reward-model metrics with low overhead.
DmwT6JI4Ek.main_concern: Reviewers question whether low token likelihoods reliably reflect preference violations across differently calibrated experts, note a gap between Theorem 4.1 and Algorithm 1, and point to small 8B gains and scaling cost with >3 objectives.

bBTVxBNXJX.one_liner: Trains an LSTM on token-resolved MoE routing traces to attribute refusal to specific experts and silence them at inference time.
bBTVxBNXJX.problem: Static expert-activation frequencies poorly localize the conditional routing components responsible for safety refusal in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs.
bBTVxBNXJX.method: Large Language Lobotomy (L^3) records token-resolved routing trajectories for harmful prompts and benign twins, trains a local-expert LSTM (LE-LSTM) to predict refusal, attributes importance via gradient-times-input, and iteratively silences top-ranked experts without weight updates.
bBTVxBNXJX.key_idea: Uses sequential routing-trajectory modeling (LE-LSTM) and gradient attribution to construct a single reusable ranking of refusal-mediating MoE experts for silencing.
bBTVxBNXJX.evidence: Evaluated across eight open-weight MoE LLMs on jailbreak ASR and five downstream utility benchmarks, with token-order shuffling and random-silencing controls.
bBTVxBNXJX.claimed_gains: Raises average ASR across eight open-weight MoE LLMs from 8.3% to 78.0% (up to 86.3%) while reducing accuracy on five downstream benchmarks by 3.4% on average.
bBTVxBNXJX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling ordered token-level routing trajectories yields stronger safety-expert localization than static activation summaries across eight MoE models.
bBTVxBNXJX.main_concern: Reviewers note that cumulative ASR and utility are not measured at the same fixed silencing configuration, the LSTM confounds prompt harmfulness with refusal, and figures/writing in Section 5 are dense.

VwJQinKGlB.one_liner: Synthesizes premotor cortex speech neural activity by composing reusable linguistic-level kernels or a TCN to augment low-resource BCI decoding.
VwJQinKGlB.problem: Speech brain-computer interfaces suffer from limited labeled neural recording data, hindering phoneme decoding accuracy.
VwJQinKGlB.method: The authors propose an interpretable linear model that sums reusable neural kernels across phonemes, biphones, syllables, and words, alongside a nonlinear temporal convolutional network (TCN), to generate synthetic neural trajectories for data augmentation.
VwJQinKGlB.key_idea: Synthesizes sentence-level premotor neural activity by linearly composing hierarchical linguistic-unit kernels (phonemes to words) or nonlinear TCNs for BCI data augmentation.
VwJQinKGlB.evidence: Evaluated across four neural speech datasets on temporal/spectral fidelity, cross-decoding with real-trained decoders, and low-data phoneme error rate (PER) augmentation.
VwJQinKGlB.claimed_gains: Reduces phoneme error rate by up to 30 percentage points (TCN) and 24 percentage points (linear model) over resampled-data augmentation, matching full-data decoding with up to 48% less real data.
VwJQinKGlB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the compositional linear primitive model is a well-motivated, interpretable contribution and that synthetic augmentation strongly improves low-data speech decoding.
VwJQinKGlB.main_concern: Reviewers flag conflicting descriptions of checkpoint selection (test vs validation PER), note that tuning residual noise on validation PER confounds neural fidelity with decoding ease, and request an update-matched control.

oyt490RUa3.one_liner: Decomposes continual RL deployment drops at a single checkpoint by comparing forced task-aware experts against learned routing.
oyt490RUa3.problem: Old-task performance drops in modular continual RL conflate weight-level forgetting with failure to retrieve an intact module.
oyt490RUa3.method: The authors propose a same-checkpoint diagnostic protocol and instantiate it in CM-Dreamer, a modular DreamerV3 agent with LoRA experts. It compares forced task-assigned expert execution against learned label-free routing and fixed mixtures to separate acquisition, retention loss, and retrieval gap.
oyt490RUa3.key_idea: Evaluates forced task-assigned experts versus learned routing on the same checkpoint to isolate retrieval failures from retention loss.
oyt490RUa3.evidence: Experiments on CM-Dreamer across a three-task Meta-World stream (cw3) and additional streams with observation masking and delayed-correction ablations.
oyt490RUa3.claimed_gains: On a three-task Meta-World stream (cw3), the same final checkpoint scores 0.66 under the task-aware reference versus 0.32 under learned deployment, and another checkpoint with 97% assigned-expert router weight still shows a 1.00 retrieval gap.
oyt490RUa3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating retention loss from execution-time retrieval failure at a single checkpoint is a useful diagnostic contribution.
oyt490RUa3.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over prior expert-selection comparisons like OWL and Expert Gate, and that most tested checkpoints only master one task within a single architecture.

d453wM2zWV.one_liner: Pretrains a JEPA time-series backbone, fine-tunes masked contextual reconstruction, and scores anomalies via a joint 2D latent-input distribution.
d453wM2zWV.problem: Time-series anomaly detection methods typically operate solely in either input reconstruction space or latent representation space rather than combining their complementary evidence.
d453wM2zWV.method: JELI pretrains a JEPA Transformer backbone for latent prediction, fine-tunes it for contextual reconstruction with an attention-masking bottleneck, and combines latent and input anomaly scores via a joint-distribution 2D CDF.
d453wM2zWV.key_idea: Combines a JEPA-pretrained latent predictor with masked contextual reconstruction and fuses both anomaly scores through a joint 2D distribution.
d453wM2zWV.evidence: Evaluated on univariate and multivariate TSB-AD benchmarks (TSB-AD-U and TSB-AD-M) without point adjustment.
d453wM2zWV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that JELI is clean, avoids point-adjustment pitfalls, and achieves strong empirical results on TSB-AD benchmarks.
d453wM2zWV.main_concern: Methodological novelty over existing JEPA and dual-space detectors is limited, and ablations do not establish clear gains from joint scoring over independent tails.

aaV7eyvu40.one_liner: Calibrates segmentation seeds with isotonic regression and grows nested regions via geodesic propagation under conformal risk control.
aaV7eyvu40.problem: Pixel-wise Conformal Risk Control (CRC) thresholding produces fragmented image segmentation masks under strict instance-level miss-risk constraints.
aaV7eyvu40.method: GeoCRC uses isotonic regression to identify reliable seed regions and traversal costs, grows a nested family of regions via multi-source geodesic propagation parameterized by radius, and calibrates the radius with an instance-level miss loss.
aaV7eyvu40.key_idea: Constructs nested segmentation masks via multi-source geodesic propagation from calibrated seeds so conformal risk control bounds connected-component miss risk.
aaV7eyvu40.evidence: Derives distribution-free marginal risk guarantees from CRC and evaluates spatial fragmentation and false-positive noise across segmentation benchmarks.
aaV7eyvu40.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting connected-component miss risk to reduce segmentation fragmentation is practically important and well structured.
aaV7eyvu40.main_concern: Baselines omit spatially regularized conformal methods, making it unclear how much gain comes from geodesic propagation versus spatial smoothing.

gfFIJ2GxLO.one_liner: Constructs a bilingual VLM benchmark from real deployed robot-harness calls preserving processed views and output contracts.
gfFIJ2GxLO.problem: Standalone VLM benchmarks abstract away the processed views, request taxonomies, and output contracts through which real robot harnesses query VLMs.
gfFIJ2GxLO.method: The authors log routine operation calls from a deployed manipulation robot to build a category-balanced, Chinese-English benchmark across eight request families, evaluating VLMs with contract-acceptance and semantic metrics.
gfFIJ2GxLO.key_idea: Derives VLM evaluation instances, processed visual crops, and output-contract metrics directly from logged API calls of a deployed robot harness.
gfFIJ2GxLO.evidence: Evaluated representative VLMs across eight request categories using human-verified dual-model reference answers and physical-robot checks.
gfFIJ2GxLO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that grounding VLM evaluation in real robot-harness interfaces and separating contract acceptance from semantic errors yields practical insights.
gfFIJ2GxLO.main_concern: Data comes from successful episodes of a single company's setup (mainly washing-machine scenes), limiting generalizability and correlation to task success.

cuTStbc3yE.one_liner: Estimates spatial recoverability gates for color, layout, structure, and detail to progressively reconstruct hidden screens from wall glows.
cuTStbc3yE.problem: Diffuse wall reflections attenuate color, layout, structure, and detail unevenly across space, making uniform image-to-image mapping unreliable for indirect screen reconstruction.
cuTStbc3yE.method: OARL learns a calibrated shared evidence field predicting spatial recoverability gates for color, layout, structure, and detail (CHRRL), then modulates a sequential color-to-layout-to-structure-to-detail residual reconstruction backbone (OSAR).
cuTStbc3yE.key_idea: Predicts per-location recoverability gates across four visual cues to modulate a sequential color-layout-structure-detail reconstruction backbone.
cuTStbc3yE.evidence: Evaluated on a newly captured 12,400-pair real wall-glow dataset across five screen-content categories with component ablations and robustness tests.
cuTStbc3yE.claimed_gains: Achieves the best reported values in all 15 category-metric comparisons across five screen-content categories.
cuTStbc3yE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that passive indirect screen reconstruction from wall glows is a compelling setting supported by a valuable real paired dataset.
cuTStbc3yE.main_concern: The train-test split protocol is unclear (risking template memorization), and figure/equation inconsistencies obscure how components improve over progressive baselines.

57B7QuQIk6.one_liner: Selects small stimulus sets covering one subject's fMRI response space to train data-efficient image-to-fMRI encoders for new subjects.
57B7QuQIk6.problem: Training image-to-fMRI encoders typically requires hundreds of costly participant-specific fMRI scans, limiting population-scale and longitudinal neuroscience studies.
57B7QuQIk6.method: The authors evaluate subset-selection objectives (effective dimensionality, k-means, k-center, coverage) in image representation space and in a reference subject's brain-response space to choose tens of stimuli for scanning new subjects.
57B7QuQIk6.key_idea: Selects small fMRI stimulus sets that maximize coverage of a reference subject's brain-response space to improve encoder training on new subjects.
57B7QuQIk6.evidence: Evaluated low-data encoder training and cross-dataset transfer from NSD to other fMRI datasets including LAION-fMRI.
57B7QuQIk6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that stimulus selection for low-data fMRI encoding is an important problem with compelling cross-subject and cross-dataset transfer results.
57B7QuQIk6.main_concern: Standard heuristic selection objectives lack first-principles motivation or full-dataset upper-bound comparisons, and the writing is overly verbose.

2QadHfqilx.one_liner: Conditions channel modulation routing and multiscale fusion on normalized attention entropy for referring image segmentation.
2QadHfqilx.problem: Transformer attention outputs aggregate value vectors without explicitly exposing how concentrated or diffuse the underlying attention distribution is.
2QadHfqilx.method: Attention Entropy Routing (AER) computes normalized multiscale attention entropy, routes among language-generated channel modulation vectors using local visual features and aligned entropy, and conditions multiscale fusion on pooled entropy.
2QadHfqilx.key_idea: Uses normalized multiscale attention entropy alongside visual features to route language-conditioned channel modulations and guide multiscale fusion.
2QadHfqilx.evidence: Evaluated on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, and hazy remote-sensing benchmarks (RefSegRS, RRSIS-D) with frozen-encoder and spatial-permutation controls.
2QadHfqilx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using attention entropy to condition referring segmentation is well motivated and supported by matched-head and permutation controls.
2QadHfqilx.main_concern: Added projections and multi-stage features confound entropy gains, experiments use a single training seed, and alternative concentration statistics are untested.

0TcsziqDbP.one_liner: Combines structured spatial-temporal QA grounding of a VLM with city-specific dynamics encoders and Nash-balanced multi-city optimization.
0TcsziqDbP.problem: VLMs lack quantitative spatial-temporal urban dynamics knowledge, while joint multi-city forecasting suffers from heterogeneous distributions and conflicting optimization objectives.
0TcsziqDbP.method: UrbanBind adapts a VLM via structured QA grounding, pairs it with native-grid spatial-temporal encoders and cross-city attention, and uses Nash-balanced optimization to reconcile conflicting city-wise gradient updates.
0TcsziqDbP.key_idea: Grounds a VLM with spatial-temporal QA tasks alongside explicit numerical dynamics encoders and Nash-balanced multi-city gradient optimization.
0TcsziqDbP.evidence: Evaluated MAE and RMSE across three urban datasets, plus held-out-city, image-perturbation, and representation-probing experiments.
0TcsziqDbP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining VLM QA grounding with native-grid numerical encoders and Nash-balanced optimization is well motivated for multi-city forecasting.
0TcsziqDbP.main_concern: Ablations and code inspection suggest gains come mainly from the numerical encoder rather than VLM understanding, and claimed task flexibility is unverified.

Ey35ZOLnZK.one_liner: Compresses per-agent eligibility traces into state-wise expected traces for memory-efficient, replay-free policy evaluation in mean-field games.
Ey35ZOLnZK.problem: Replay-free policy evaluation in finite-horizon mean-field games requires O(NT) memory to store population histories across N agents and horizon T.
Ey35ZOLnZK.method: The authors first compress agent histories into Private Population Dutch Traces to remove T dependence, then aggregate agent traces into state-wise expected traces (DoubleSWEET) propagated via empirical state transitions.
Ey35ZOLnZK.key_idea: Compresses N per-agent eligibility traces into state-wise expected traces via empirical transitions to eliminate both horizon and population-size memory scaling.
Ey35ZOLnZK.evidence: Proves trace compression consistency and convergence guarantees for linear value functions, and evaluates numerically on Garnet-style mean-field games.
Ey35ZOLnZK.claimed_gains: Eliminates memory dependence on horizon T and agent count N from O(NT).
Ey35ZOLnZK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that DoubleSWEET is clearly presented and provides sound theoretical trace-compression consistency for mean-field policy evaluation.
Ey35ZOLnZK.main_concern: Numerical evaluation is limited to Garnet-style finite-state settings where increasing N barely reduces error over subsampled agents, questioning practical impact.

vtLNhOwXRx.one_liner: Propagates explicit normalized physical states augmented with recomputed latent features for constraint-aware and transferable TD-MPC.
vtLNhOwXRx.problem: Latent TD-MPC world models lose physical state semantics in imagined rollouts, preventing deployment-time state constraints and zero-shot task transfer without costly reconstruction.
vtLNhOwXRx.method: S-TD-MPC directly predicts normalized physical state transitions augmented by latent features recomputed at each imagined step, uses MPC-based Bellman targets, and selectively reanalyzes stale targets via target bounds.
vtLNhOwXRx.key_idea: Predicts explicit normalized physical states augmented with step-wise recomputed latent features, aligned with MPC-based Bellman targets and bounded reanalysis.
vtLNhOwXRx.evidence: Evaluated on seven continuous control tasks from two dynamical systems, testing zero-shot transfer, state constraints, and analytic rewards.
vtLNhOwXRx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicit physical-state propagation enables practical deployment-time constraints and task transfer while retaining TD-MPC control performance.
vtLNhOwXRx.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate whether the recomputed latent feature actually improves dynamics prediction over a pure state-space model.

AiujcJgQhD.one_liner: Jointly learns layer-wise quadratic activation coefficients and weights via data-dependent initialization and distillation for private inference.
AiujcJgQhD.problem: Replacing nonlinear Transformer activations with fixed quadratic polynomials for private inference degrades accuracy, especially in bias-free gated FFNs.
AiujcJgQhD.method: CoQuad identifies a projection-invariant coefficient ratio in bias-free gated FFNs, initializes quadratic approximations via DirectFit, and jointly adapts both polynomial coefficients and network weights using teacher-guided distillation (Co-Optimize).
AiujcJgQhD.key_idea: Jointly distilling network weights and layer-wise quadratic coefficients—initialized via DirectFit—preserves accuracy in both standard and bias-free gated FFNs for private inference.
AiujcJgQhD.evidence: Evaluates ViT-B/16 on ImageNet-1K and Llama SwiGLU on ARC-Easy, plus latency/communication estimates against MPCFormer and SHAFT.
AiujcJgQhD.claimed_gains: ViT-B/16 reaches 79.83% ImageNet-1K Top-1 (1.42 points over MPCFormer); Llama reaches 72.6% ARC-Easy vs. 36.5% for MPCFormer; GeLU evaluation is estimated 47-59x faster with 62x less communication than SHAFT.
AiujcJgQhD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the architectural analysis of coefficient absorption vs. gated-FFN invariants is insightful and that the ViT and Llama accuracy results are promising.
AiujcJgQhD.main_concern: Reviewers note that Llama comparisons confound initialization with coefficient trainability, and raise auditability and baseline concerns regarding secure-efficiency speedups.

QsD8PLNCMA.one_liner: Assigns quantization scales by Transformer functional role rather than matrix layout, with optional Fisher-allocated secondary ternary planes.
QsD8PLNCMA.problem: Sub-4-bit weight quantization degrades factual knowledge and task accuracy, while ternary weights typically require training from scratch or long fine-tuning.
QsD8PLNCMA.method: RoleQ places one scale per output unit for vectors reading from the residual stream and one per input unit for vectors writing to it, paired with a RoleQ-T conversion pipeline, scale distillation, and optional Fisher-weighted secondary ternary planes.
QsD8PLNCMA.key_idea: Determines per-input versus per-output quantization scale placement solely from a Transformer unit's read/write role relative to the residual stream without axis search.
QsD8PLNCMA.evidence: Experiments across two model families from 0.6B to 14B parameters compare against Qronos, PT²-LLM, and QTEA on perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, and MMLU.
QsD8PLNCMA.claimed_gains: Reduces ternary perplexity by up to half relative to uniform scale placement, and RoleQ-T reaches 1.59 bits per weight in a few GPU-hours.
QsD8PLNCMA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the role-aligned scale-placement rule simple and interpretable, supported by controlled experiments.
QsD8PLNCMA.main_concern: Reviewers question whether headline gains rely on scale distillation applied unevenly across baselines, and note missing inference speedup measurements and limited formal analysis.

QtbtZqJ1IF.one_liner: Identifies a shared one-dimensional visually grounded truth representation in intermediate VLM layers across negation and object substitution.
QtbtZqJ1IF.problem: How vision-language models compute proposition truth under semantic edits rather than relying on surface cues like negation remains unclear.
QtbtZqJ1IF.method: Using answer-balanced natural-image quartets pairing negation and object substitution, the authors use attention-swap interventions, truth-axis projections, localized visual-evidence removal, and response-code reversal to isolate intermediate truth representations.
QtbtZqJ1IF.key_idea: Demonstrates that intermediate VLM layers map distinct linguistic and visual edits onto a shared one-dimensional truth axis causally tied to visual evidence rather than output symbols.
QtbtZqJ1IF.evidence: Experiments across three VLMs and two natural-image benchmarks (RePOPE and AMBER) using causal patching and cross-dataset linear probes.
QtbtZqJ1IF.claimed_gains: A one-dimensional truth-axis projection retains over 80% of the full attention-swap effect, and frozen RePOPE-to-AMBER probes reach 91-93% accuracy.
QtbtZqJ1IF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean quartet experimental design and convergent causal checks via patching, visual removal, and codebook reversal.
QtbtZqJ1IF.main_concern: Reviewers note that the grounded-truth claim is tested only on binary object-existence questions, lacks comparison to purely linguistic truth directions, and relies heavily on one small model.

7Wdco6vHsu.one_liner: Constrains medical concept bottleneck inference using LLM-built clinical evidence graphs with typed finding, anatomy, and nuisance roles.
7Wdco6vHsu.problem: Unconstrained concept bottleneck models can exploit source-domain correlations and nuisance shortcuts in medical images under distribution shift.
7Wdco6vHsu.method: GC-NCE uses four LLM agents to build clinical evidence graphs with typed concept roles (support, inhibition, anatomy, nuisance) from medical literature, refines observability, and performs constrained probabilistic inference with validation-gated nuisance correction.
7Wdco6vHsu.key_idea: Restricts diagnostic concept weighting to typed clinical roles in an LLM-constructed evidence graph with validation-gated nuisance correction.
7Wdco6vHsu.evidence: Evaluations across ten domain-shift benchmarks in chest X-ray and skin lesion classification.
7Wdco6vHsu.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest mean out-of-distribution AUROC across ten benchmarks in chest X-ray (78.5%) and skin lesion (84.5%) modalities.
7Wdco6vHsu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that enforcing typed clinical roles on diagnostic inference is a principled alternative to unconstrained linear concept heads.
7Wdco6vHsu.main_concern: Headline comparisons confound diagnostic architecture with checkpoint selection criteria (worst-group vs. overall validation), and graph-construction retrieval details are underspecified.

VQWcK9V84q.one_liner: Aggregates discounted token-level teacher feedback into group-relative sequence credit for stable on-policy distillation.
VQWcK9V84q.problem: Standard token-level on-policy distillation assigns credit locally, ignoring how earlier tokens affect later feedback and collapsing under mismatched thinking patterns.
VQWcK9V84q.method: GR-OPD decouples feedback computation from credit assignment by discounting and summing token-level teacher feedback along trajectories, normalizing within same-prompt rollout groups while retaining a controlled fraction of the group mean.
VQWcK9V84q.key_idea: Aggregates discounted token-level teacher log-ratios into group-normalized sequence-level credit with controlled collective teacher pressure.
VQWcK9V84q.evidence: Theoretical unbiasedness analysis and experiments across five Qwen3 teacher-student pairs and six math reasoning benchmarks.
VQWcK9V84q.claimed_gains: GR-OPD outperforms vanilla OPD in macro Avg@K in all five settings, including gains of 10.9 and 11.5 percentage points in two matched thinking-pattern settings.
VQWcK9V84q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that GR-OPD achieves substantial gains and prevents training collapse under mismatched thinking patterns where vanilla OPD fails.
VQWcK9V84q.main_concern: Experiments are restricted to Qwen3 models against a single possibly under-tuned vanilla OPD baseline, and ablations do not fully isolate individual estimator components.

tcFnxpwnpY.one_liner: Learns lightweight skew-symmetric trajectory perturbation matrices via GRPO to correct and transfer across frozen flow driving planners.
tcFnxpwnpY.problem: RL fine-tuning of generative end-to-end driving planners is expensive and can disrupt pretrained driving behaviors.
tcFnxpwnpY.method: A-Flow fuses camera history into Temporal BEV Mapping, optimizes a skew-symmetric perturbation matrix via GRPO with the base planner frozen, and retrieves and selects corrected candidates in unseen scenes using Field-Guided Correction Transfer.
tcFnxpwnpY.key_idea: Applies GRPO-learned skew-symmetric perturbation matrices at the terminal step of a frozen flow planner and retrieves them via BEV features.
tcFnxpwnpY.evidence: Evaluations on NAVSIM v1, zero-shot HUGSIM transfer, and a ReCogDrive-based flow planner.
tcFnxpwnpY.claimed_gains: A-Flow achieves 90.7 PDMS in NAVSIM v1 and an HD-Score of 37.49 in zero-shot HUGSIM.
tcFnxpwnpY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that learning reusable terminal corrections for frozen flow planners yields strong benchmark gains across scenes and backbones.
tcFnxpwnpY.main_concern: Experiments lack a multi-sample-and-select baseline from the base planner, fail to isolate retrieval and kinematic post-processing contributions, and incur higher inference latency.

RjcB57gCVq.one_liner: Forecasts time series by lifting out historical event effects and kicking in future ones via a shared response function.
RjcB57gCVq.problem: Exogenous events distort historical time series dynamics, and existing event-aware forecasters treat historical attribution and future event generation separately.
RjcB57gCVq.method: Loki learns a shared Event Response Function (ERF) parameterized by event type and relative temporal position. It removes estimated event-induced deviations from historical observations before forecasting and applies the same ERF to inject responses for known future events.
RjcB57gCVq.key_idea: A shared Event Response Function removes historical event deviations before forecasting and injects future event responses using a unified parameterization.
RjcB57gCVq.evidence: Evaluated on five forecasting benchmarks across multiple forecasting backbones, plus ablations and semi-synthetic event-recovery tests.
RjcB57gCVq.claimed_gains: Achieves the best standardized MAE on all five datasets, reducing error by approximately 2.2%–11.7% over the strongest non-Loki baseline.
RjcB57gCVq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using a shared ERF to decouple historical event attribution from underlying dynamics and future injection is clear, coherent, and improves MAE across five benchmarks.
RjcB57gCVq.main_concern: Reviewers note that closely related event-decomposition baselines are missing from empirical comparisons and that differing baseline information access and limited originality weaken the claims.

zytRJpwQMV.one_liner: Learns a forecast-shaped latent space of neural network weights to extrapolate training trajectories and skip optimization steps.
zytRJpwQMV.problem: Weight-space forecasting methods predict future parameters directly in high-dimensional weight space, limiting trajectory predictability and training speedup.
zytRJpwQMV.method: LFNT trains a weight autoencoder (Stage I), aligns the latent space using a forecasting supervision objective (Stage II), and trains a forecaster on the resulting latent trajectories (Stage III). This enables jumping ahead in optimization across CNN, ResNet, and small GPT-2 models.
zytRJpwQMV.key_idea: Shapes a learned weight autoencoder latent space with forecasting supervision before training a latent trajectory forecaster to jump ahead in optimization.
zytRJpwQMV.evidence: Evaluated on vision and language tasks across CNNs, ResNets, and small GPT-2 models, including transfer to unseen datasets and depths and ablations against WNN/NiNo.
zytRJpwQMV.claimed_gains: Latent-space forecasting provides training speedups of up to 59% over weight-space forecasting baselines.
zytRJpwQMV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that latent-space weight trajectory forecasting outperforms WNN and NiNo baselines and that forecast-shaping ablations support the latent-space design.
zytRJpwQMV.main_concern: Reviewers question practical significance because autoencoder/forecaster training and zoo costs are excluded from speedup and evaluated models are very small.

7KNFSknpNH.one_liner: Admits, blends, and certifies affordable LLM judges with finite-sample risk control to automate selective evaluation.
7KNFSknpNH.problem: Individual LLM judges can disagree with human ratings due to surface biases, while stronger models are costly and naive ensembles lack error-rate guarantees.
7KNFSknpNH.method: ABC (Admit, Blend, Certify) first runs a cross-fitted residual association test to admit judges correlated with human ratings beyond surface features like length and style. It then blends admitted judges via penalized logistic regression and certifies an acceptance threshold guaranteeing population error below a target rate.
7KNFSknpNH.key_idea: Filters LLM judges via residual association beyond surface features, blends them with penalized logistic regression, and certifies a finite-sample risk-controlled acceptance rule.
7KNFSknpNH.evidence: Theoretical finite-sample risk-control guarantees (Theorems 1-2) and experiments on human-rated benchmarks against single-judge, majority-voting, and cascade baselines.
7KNFSknpNH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Admit-Blend-Certify framework is clean and provides a meaningful finite-sample risk-control guarantee independent of admission/blending accuracy.
7KNFSknpNH.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing comparisons to recent multi-expert conformal/selective-evaluation baselines and unestablished necessity of the admission step or human-label cost tradeoffs.

cGoDRaQLlP.one_liner: Fuses molecular, cellular, biological-fact, and few-shot response inputs in an LLM trained with REINFORCE for drug response prediction.
cGoDRaQLlP.problem: Predicting drug responses for unseen drugs and cell lines requires integrating heterogeneous molecular, cellular, and few-shot experimental evidence.
cGoDRaQLlP.method: Projectors map molecular and cellular features alongside biological facts and support responses into an LLM trained via response-free alignment, teacher-guided reasoning warmup, and alternating numerical prediction and REINFORCE updates using a probability-weighted numerical token interface.
cGoDRaQLlP.key_idea: Alternates numerical response prediction with REINFORCE over evidence-grounded reasoning traces via a probability-weighted numerical token readout.
cGoDRaQLlP.evidence: Evaluated against eight baselines under drug-blind and cell-blind splits with zero and five support measurements.
cGoDRaQLlP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the unified integration of heterogeneous biological inputs and the entity-held-out zero- and few-shot evaluation.
cGoDRaQLlP.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing multi-seed standard deviations, small gains over simple baselines (MLP, XGBoost), and unclear isolation of reasoning vs. RL components.

xFngHDf6O7.one_liner: Coupling a discrete-time neural operator with a proxy optimizer approximates PDE-constrained control decisions without iterative test-time optimization.
xFngHDf6O7.problem: Repeatedly solving high-dimensional discretized PDEs during optimization makes conventional PDE-constrained optimal control too expensive for near-real-time decisions.
xFngHDf6O7.method: The framework combines a time-discrete neural operator that predicts PDE trajectories with an optimization surrogate that predicts control decisions. The dual networks model the coupling between system dynamics and optimal strategies.
xFngHDf6O7.key_idea: A learned dynamics operator and a proxy optimizer amortize PDE simulation and control optimization into a fast neural approximation.
xFngHDf6O7.evidence: Evaluations include 1D reaction-diffusion voltage dynamics, 2D heat equations, and 1D viscous Burgers' equations against classical and learning-based solvers.
xFngHDf6O7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that avoiding iterative inference-time optimization yields substantial acceleration while retaining competitive solution quality.
xFngHDf6O7.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the methodological novelty unclear beyond combining DeepONet-style dynamics prediction with proxy optimization.

nVgcGyo4zD.one_liner: Generating crystals through a global latent and parallel slot decoder removes atom-wise correspondence from flow-based transport.
nVgcGyo4zD.problem: Permutation-equivariant particle flows become harder to train reliably as crystal sets grow larger and denser, limiting all-atom generation for metal-organic frameworks.
nVgcGyo4zD.method: GLASS encodes structures into a permutation-invariant global latent and learns their distribution with flow matching. A learned-slot decoder constructs every atom in parallel instead of transporting individual particles.
nVgcGyo4zD.key_idea: Slot-based parallel decoding separates set generation from atom-wise correspondence by mapping one global latent directly to the complete atomic structure.
nVgcGyo4zD.evidence: Experiments cover MP20 and a QMOF subset, including MOF generation with up to 150 atoms per unit cell without building-block, topology, or composition conditioning.
nVgcGyo4zD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the correspondence hypothesis is well motivated and that the slot decoder, ablations, and dataset experiments are informative.
nVgcGyo4zD.main_concern: Reviewers consistently warn that high structural validity comes with limited novelty, especially the low valid-and-novel rate on QMOF150.

baJBmmOf2n.one_liner: Learning sketching-matrix distributions with a VAE produces data-aware low-rank Transformer compression and decoder-only transfer.
baJBmmOf2n.problem: Data-oblivious random projections ignore downstream data when selecting sketches for post-training low-rank model compression.
baJBmmOf2n.method: The method trains a variational autoencoder to learn a distribution over sketching matrices with a task-oriented loss. Fine-tuning only the VAE decoder adapts the compressor to depth upscaling and domain changes.
baJBmmOf2n.key_idea: A VAE learns the probability distribution over projection operators so sketches reflect downstream data rather than remaining data-oblivious.
baJBmmOf2n.evidence: The study compares against data-oblivious sketching and low-rank baselines and examines depth upscaling and domain adaptation through decoder fine-tuning.
baJBmmOf2n.claimed_gains: For compression ratios of up to 30%, the compressed model outperforms even the uncompressed baseline.
baJBmmOf2n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers who provide strengths praise the learned projection distribution, decoder-only transfer, and principled task loss.
baJBmmOf2n.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the evaluation because WikiText-2 training overlaps evaluation and recent compression baselines are missing.

uZYu8wN77X.one_liner: Applies post-hoc multicalibration in representation space to bound documented and undocumented biases in pairwise LLM-as-a-judge evaluations.
uZYu8wN77X.problem: LLM judges exhibit systematic biases such as position, verbosity, and model-family preference, as well as undocumented group biases, that distort human-preference predictions.
uZYu8wN77X.method: CaLLM is a post-hoc multicalibration framework that calibrates an LLM judge's pairwise preference scores across groups captured by an input representation and optional explicit bias groups. The authors prove bounds on group-wise bias and derive conditions under which multicalibration improves judge accuracy rather than trading it off.
uZYu8wN77X.key_idea: Post-hoc multicalibrates LLM judge scores over representation-defined and explicit bias groups to simultaneously bound group miscalibration and improve preference accuracy.
uZYu8wN77X.evidence: Supported by theoretical bias and accuracy-improvement guarantees and empirical evaluations across multiple datasets, bias types, judges, and independent embedders.
uZYu8wN77X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multicalibration framing for unifying multiple LLM-judge biases well motivated, with promising empirical gains in calibration and accuracy.
uZYu8wN77X.main_concern: Reviewers note that experiments lack controlled comparisons against standard supervised predictors (e.g., GBDT) trained on the exact same representations and human labels to isolate the benefit of multicalibration.

iUXlQrm5C5.one_liner: Transfers cross-modal knowledge in dual-partial federated learning via verified modality-label evidence prototypes and OOD-gated Top-K graph aggregation.
iUXlQrm5C5.problem: In multimodal federated learning with both missing modalities and missing labels, missing supervision prevents verifying whether cross-modal transfers are accurate.
iUXlQrm5C5.method: DualP-EGFL builds signed modality-label evidence prototypes from verified client observations and admits cross-modal graph edges only after checking structural support and verified target utility. Unknown targets receive transferred evidence only when pair-specific OOD gating and conservative Top-K path aggregation confirm sufficient support, leaving unsupported targets low-evidence.
iUXlQrm5C5.key_idea: Restricts cross-modal federated transfer to verified modality-label evidence graph paths filtered by structural support, target utility, pair-specific OOD gating, and conservative Top-K aggregation.
iUXlQrm5C5.evidence: Includes theoretical analysis and federated experiments on multimodal benchmarks including 100-client MM-IMDb and MELD against recent MFL baselines.
iUXlQrm5C5.claimed_gains: Improves supported-hidden Macro-AUPRC by up to 7.65 percentage points over recent MFL baselines, with the largest gain on 100-client MM-IMDb.
iUXlQrm5C5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly missing modalities and labels is a practically relevant problem and appreciate reframing it around verified evidence transfer.
iUXlQrm5C5.main_concern: Reviewers highlight a severe reliability-coverage breakdown (100% false-support rate at 99.99% coverage on 100-client MM-IMDb versus 3.76% coverage on MELD), single-seed evaluation, and missing hyperparameter sensitivity analysis.

aWYYU09BfJ.one_liner: Localizes visual prompt injections via attention probes and replaces selected visual tokens with boundary-feature means to recover user tasks.
aWYYU09BfJ.problem: Existing visual prompt injection defenses can suppress attacker outputs while still failing to complete the user's original task on application screenshots.
aWYYU09BfJ.method: The authors introduce AppInjectBench, pairing clean, benign-text, and injected screenshots across 11 real applications. They propose PRISM, which extracts visual-token attention under a fixed query, predicts injection regions with a lightweight spatial locator, replaces those visual features with the mean of unselected boundary features, and runs a fresh prefill on the frozen VLM.
aWYYU09BfJ.key_idea: Uses fixed-query visual attention maps to train a 9K-parameter spatial locator and repairs injected visual tokens by replacing them with the mean of surrounding boundary features.
aWYYU09BfJ.evidence: Evaluated on model-specific 1,000-source AppInjectBench test sets for Qwen2-VL-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B, plus cross-dataset transfer tests from ARGUS.
aWYYU09BfJ.claimed_gains: Recovers 96.7% of injected cases with Qwen2-VL-7B and 94.0% with Qwen2.5-VL-7B while causing new errors on at most 0.3% of benign inputs.
aWYYU09BfJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the distinction between attack suppression and user task recovery, the realistic 11-application paired benchmark, and PRISM's lightweight design.
aWYYU09BfJ.main_concern: Reviewers highlight severe cross-domain over-masking when trained without clean negative supervision (45.6% benign harm when transferring from ARGUS to AppInjectBench) and missing ablations on feature-repair strategies.

Iqm7249gqD.one_liner: Generates metal-organic framework building-block poses by predicting representative anchor-atom coordinates with Bayesian Flow Networks and rigid alignment.
Iqm7249gqD.problem: Predicting building-block orientations in angular space ignores how block size, shape, and rotation axis cause anisotropic Cartesian atomic displacements.
Iqm7249gqD.method: AnchorPose represents each MOF building block by a small set of representative anchor atoms, combines local block geometry with spatial state, and generates anchor coordinates using Bayesian Flow Networks.
