Rigid alignment against the known local block geometry then recovers complete building-block poses while preserving intra-block structure.
Iqm7249gqD.key_idea: Replaces rotation-space pose generation with Bayesian Flow Network generation of sparse representative anchor-atom coordinates followed by rigid alignment to recover building-block poses.
Iqm7249gqD.evidence: Evaluated on the MOF structure prediction benchmark against existing baselines (such as AtomMOF-L and quaternion/Bingham rotation states) with ablation studies.
Iqm7249gqD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that motivating anchor coordinates through geometry-dependent anisotropic displacement errors is intuitive and yields strong structure match rates.
Iqm7249gqD.main_concern: Reviewers note modest single-seed ablation margins, lack of justification for why four sparse anchors beat quaternion representations (which outperform anchors in Table 12), and independent conformation fitting ignoring inter-block interactions.

S2cQcRF30w.one_liner: Extracts a 20,783-record co-crystal synthesis database from literature to power method-specific condition prediction and tool-augmented LLM decision support.
S2cQcRF30w.problem: While ML methods assist co-crystal pair screening, downstream prediction and decision support for experimental synthesis conditions remain largely unresolved.
S2cQcRF30w.method: CoSyn hierarchically extracts method-specific synthesis parameters from literature to build CoSyn-DB (20,783 records across 12 synthesis methods), trains method-specific starting-condition recommenders for API-coformer pairs, and wraps them in a tool-augmented LLM agentic orchestration system.
S2cQcRF30w.key_idea: Combines hierarchical literature extraction into a structured 12-method synthesis database with method-specific condition predictors orchestrated by a tool-augmented LLM.
S2cQcRF30w.evidence: Evaluated via manually annotated extraction sets, a 30-question domain benchmark (1-5 scale), and prospective wet-lab validation on four held-out API-coformer pairs.
S2cQcRF30w.claimed_gains: Achieves phase-pure co-crystals for three of four held-out pairs and scores 3.58 on the domain benchmark versus 1.88 for an LLM without tools and 3.29 for a fixed non-agentic workflow.
S2cQcRF30w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CoSyn-DB (20,783 structured synthesis records) is a valuable resource for an underexplored downstream materials task and commend the multi-stage validation.
S2cQcRF30w.main_concern: Reviewers find limited methodological novelty in the agentic orchestration (where LLM predictors match Random Forest and multi-agent matches single-agent) and note the small 30-question benchmark and underspecified scale constraints.

d4GoKA8Vyz.one_liner: Pairs a 47.57M-parameter sparse-expert world action backbone with frozen-backbone cross-task and cross-embodiment adapters for manipulation.
d4GoKA8Vyz.problem: World action models struggle to stay lightweight while transferring learned dynamics across manipulation tasks and new robot embodiments without forgetting.
d4GoKA8Vyz.method: LiteC-WAM combines a lightweight shared backbone (perception module, sparse Top-2 dynamics experts, and a flow-matching action head refined by world-model feedback) with language-guided cross-task adapters and low-rank observation adapters plus robot-specific action encoders and decoders for continual expansion.
d4GoKA8Vyz.key_idea: Freezes a lightweight Top-2 sparse-expert dynamics and flow-matching backbone while attaching modular cross-task and low-rank cross-embodiment adapters.
d4GoKA8Vyz.evidence: Evaluated on 5 LIBERO tasks (plus a 20-task paired feedback check), 15 RLBench manipulation tasks, and physical robot deployments (ARX5 and SO-ARM101).
d4GoKA8Vyz.claimed_gains: With 47.57M parameters, achieves 96.0% success on 5 LIBERO tasks (vs. 72.4% Diffusion Policy, 75.1% Octo-Base, 82.75% SmolVLA-240M, and comparable to 3.3B-7B models) and 86.67% across 15 RLBench tasks.
d4GoKA8Vyz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the compact architecture balancing efficiency and capability, closed-loop feedback evidence, and physical robot deployment.
d4GoKA8Vyz.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the very small evaluation sample sizes (50 LIBERO rollouts, 120 RLBench rollouts) and inconsistent architecture/feedback configurations across robot embodiments that obscure what drives performance.

TKvsokkhHZ.one_liner: Extracts local supervision segments from failed and successful agent rollouts using progress frontiers matched against the shortest successful rollout.
TKvsokkhHZ.problem: Self-evolving language agents trained only on outcome feedback lack step-level supervision showing where failed trajectories broke down and discard useful partial progress.
TKvsokkhHZ.method: Policy-Relative Frontier Learning uses the shortest successful rollout as a reference to locate each failed rollout's furthest shared progress state (its relative frontier). It then selects trajectory segments from each rollout's frontier to the next frontier in the group (or completion) from both failed and successful rollouts for iterative fine-tuning.
TKvsokkhHZ.key_idea: Aligns failed rollouts to the shortest successful trajectory to define relative progress frontiers and harvests local segment-level supervision from both failed and successful donor rollouts.
TKvsokkhHZ.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld and WebShop using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with component ablations.
TKvsokkhHZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, PRM-free training-data construction idea that leverages partial progress from failed trajectories.
TKvsokkhHZ.main_concern: Reviewers note reliance on recorded simulator states and strict ordered-path matching against a single reference (limiting scalability and fairness), as well as evaluation restricted to Qwen2.5-7B on ALFWorld and WebShop.

TBdekWCqY8.one_liner: Routes each student rollout to the highest-priority deficient specialist teacher and projects out log-policy updates opposing higher-priority specialists.
TBdekWCqY8.problem: Multi-reward post-training methods scalarize rewards or merge specialists without enforcing priority ordering, letting lower-priority objectives like conciseness degrade correctness.
TBdekWCqY8.method: Lexicographic Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation (LMOPD) integrates reward-specialized teachers under an explicit priority order. For each student rollout, it selects the specialist for the first objective whose gate detects a deficiency and locally projects its centered log-policy correction to remove components opposing higher-priority specialists.
TBdekWCqY8.key_idea: Combines lexicographic deficiency-gated rollout routing to specialist teachers with local projection of centered log-policy corrections orthogonal to opposing higher-priority teachers.
TBdekWCqY8.evidence: Evaluated on proprietary 30B-A3B MoE models in two- and four-expert settings across three math benchmarks with matched four-expert ablations.
TBdekWCqY8.claimed_gains: With two experts, retains 100% of accuracy and reasoning-quality gains while acquiring 46.9% of conciseness gain; with four experts, retains 90.6% of accuracy and 71.2% of reasoning-correctness gains versus at most 57.1% and 51.0% for other unified methods.
TBdekWCqY8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that enforcing explicit asymmetric objective priorities via deficiency-gated routing addresses a meaningful limitation of scalarized post-training.
TBdekWCqY8.main_concern: Reviewers flag missing referenced appendices/algorithms needed for verification, non-reproducible proprietary models and math training data, single-seed four-expert results, and untested priority orders.

9ARjCE6v4O.one_liner: Corrects federated local drift and non-stationary participation bias using one persistent model-sized client memory with FedAvg communication.
9ARjCE6v4O.problem: Federated optimization suffers coupled local drift and unequal, time-varying client participation bias that existing variance-reduction fixes resolve only with extra communication or server memory.
9ARjCE6v4O.method: TRUSS maintains a single persistent model-sized memory vector per client and applies its difference from the current server model as a local-step correction. Active clients exchange only one model-sized vector per direction per round, while the server stores only the global model.
9ARjCE6v4O.key_idea: Use the difference between each client's single persistent model-sized state and the current server model to correct both local drift and arbitrary participation bias.
9ARjCE6v4O.evidence: Proves non-convex convergence without bounded gradient heterogeneity or known inclusion probabilities, and validates on non-iid federated simulation benchmarks.
9ARjCE6v4O.claimed_gains: Establishes an O((NKR)^{-1/2} + R^{-1}) stationarity bound achieving linear speedup in clients N and local steps K while matching FedAvg per-round communication.
9ARjCE6v4O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that TRUSS has a simple, communication- and memory-efficient design with clean convergence guarantees under time-varying participation.
9ARjCE6v4O.main_concern: Writing clarity is weak in places, comparisons omit key baselines such as FedSUM-CR and gradient-tracking discussions, and experiments fix N=10, K=50 without testing speedup scaling.

8PYNWZs7MK.one_liner: Benchmarks clinical-agent procedural inertia on SkillInertiaBench and enforces an independent pre-action skill-validity gate via PatientGate.
8PYNWZs7MK.problem: Clinical LLM agents following reusable skills often persist with a procedure even after new patient evidence invalidates it during execution.
8PYNWZs7MK.method: The authors build SkillInertiaBench (576 clinician-reviewed cases across six procedure families) pairing routine cases with pre-execution, mid-execution revealed, and state-change invalidations. They propose PatientGate, where an independent reviewer rechecks the active skill against current patient state before every action and a gate enforces its verdict.
8PYNWZs7MK.key_idea: Insert an independent pre-action reviewer and hard execution gate that re-verifies active skill validity against updated patient state before each clinical action.
8PYNWZs7MK.evidence: Evaluated across two model families on SkillInertiaBench with prompt-based controls and enforcement ablations.
8PYNWZs7MK.claimed_gains: Standard skills raise routine completion from 67.7% to 80.6% but cut later-contradiction completion from 62.2% to 44.8% and raise harmful persistence from 31.2% to 49.8%; PatientGate raises later-contradiction completion to 69.8% and lowers harmful persistence to 25.3% at 79.9% routine completion.
8PYNWZs7MK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that procedural inertia after skill invalidation is a meaningful clinical-safety problem and that the enforcement ablations support the intervention.
8PYNWZs7MK.main_concern: PatientGate relies on structured manual annotations and lacks specification-matched guard baselines, while benchmark variants confound invalidation content with timing and under-specify clinician curation.

SU3CXiFyPm.one_liner: Uses finite-step flow reversal to encode frozen VLA action chunks into structured noise for high-frequency tactile-conditioned decoding.
SU3CXiFyPm.problem: Flow-based vision-language-action policies update too slowly from vision alone to react to rapid contact dynamics in contact-rich robotic manipulation.
SU3CXiFyPm.method: TacFRS keeps a pretrained flow-based VLA frozen and applies finite-step flow reversal to map its action chunks into observation-conditioned structured noise. A fast tactile-conditioned decoder then revises actions between VLA updates using fresh touch and proprioception, trained with tactile-gated supervision blending base actions and expert demonstrations.
SU3CXiFyPm.key_idea: Invert frozen VLA action chunks via finite-step flow reversal into structured noise, then rapidly re-decode them with fresh tactile and proprioceptive inputs under tactile-gated supervision.
SU3CXiFyPm.evidence: Evaluated across four real-world single-arm and bimanual manipulation tasks on two VLA backbones (20 trials per setting noted in reviews) with ablations.
SU3CXiFyPm.claimed_gains: Improves every evaluated task for both backbones, increasing average success from 28.75% to 41.25% (abstract truncated before second backbone figure).
SU3CXiFyPm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that keeping the pretrained VLA frozen while plugging in a lightweight high-frequency tactile revision module is practical and consistently improves real-robot success.
SU3CXiFyPm.main_concern: Experiments fail to cleanly isolate the contributions of tactile sensing and flow-reversal structured noise, as the direct-correction baseline scores 0% and high-gate targets are dominated by extra supervised demonstrations.

yGvNUsTAqF.one_liner: Trains a terrain-aware autoregressive diffusion planner on 75M expert transitions to generate future humanoid motion imaginations tracked by a unified policy.
yGvNUsTAqF.problem: Distilling multiple terrain-specific humanoid policies into one controller transfers individual primitives poorly to novel and composite terrains.
yGvNUsTAqF.method: DreamPolicy constructs a modular multi-terrain benchmark with over a dozen primitive terrains and 75M transitions of expert rollouts, then trains a terrain-aware autoregressive diffusion planner to output physically plausible future state trajectories (humanoid motion imaginations). A unified HMI-conditioned policy tracks these planned trajectories without terrain-specific reward design.
yGvNUsTAqF.key_idea: Decouples terrain-aware locomotion into an autoregressive diffusion planner predicting future state trajectories and a unified tracking policy that composes behaviors across terrains.
yGvNUsTAqF.evidence: Evaluated in simulation (Isaac Gym/Isaac Lab) on composite and unseen terrains and zero-shot sim-to-real on a Unitree G1 humanoid across gaps, balancing beams, slopes, and stairs.
yGvNUsTAqF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the 75M-transition modular multi-terrain benchmark and meaningful Unitree G1 real-robot gains on gap traversal (16/20 vs. 8/20) and balancing beams.
yGvNUsTAqF.main_concern: Reviewers question the 'zero-shot' unseen-terrain claim (online RL training terrains are unlisted), note missing comparisons to existing diffusion-planner-tracker methods (e.g., CLoSD, PARC) and deterministic predictors, and flag confounded ablations.

RSlfcClR45.one_liner: Encodes pseudo-RGB log-mel spectrograms with FLUX.2's frozen image VAE and adapts its pretrained Diffusion Transformer via conditional flow matching for TTS.
RSlfcClR45.problem: Whether representations and generative priors from pretrained text-to-image diffusion models transfer effectively to transcript-faithful, speaker-preserving speech synthesis remains unclear.
RSlfcClR45.method: ImageTTS converts log-mel spectrograms into pseudo-RGB images encoded by FLUX.2's frozen image VAE and adapts only the pretrained Diffusion Transformer using conditional latent flow matching for zero-shot and instruction-guided TTS, isolating VAE representation transfer from DiT initialization transfer.
RSlfcClR45.key_idea: Repurposes a frozen text-to-image VAE and pretrained Diffusion Transformer via conditional latent flow matching on pseudo-RGB mel spectrograms to separate representation and prior transfer.
RSlfcClR45.evidence: Evaluated VAE reconstruction quality, controlled pretrained-vs-random DiT ablations at 100K–150K updates, and 100K-hour scaled models on Seed-TTS test-en and CapSpeech.
RSlfcClR45.claimed_gains: The frozen FLUX.2 VAE retains 0.99 STOI and 0.95 speaker similarity; pretrained DiT initialization cuts WER from 4.2% to 2.7% at 100k matched updates; scaling to 100K hours reaches 1.12% WER on Seed-TTS test-en and 0.66 Style-ACC on CapSpeech.
RSlfcClR45.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the cleanly controlled pretrained-versus-random DiT initialization experiments isolating convergence and linguistic accuracy benefits.
RSlfcClR45.main_concern: Reviewers point out omitted closely related prior work (Auffusion) that already transferred pretrained image VAEs and diffusion models to pseudo-RGB mel spectrograms, and note image-specific vs. generic Transformer pretraining is not isolated.

Gbqu33OFyN.one_liner: Applies two-stage label-free test-time RL (one-shot format alignment plus majority-voting distribution alignment) as a train-before-test protocol for LLM evaluation.
Gbqu33OFyN.problem: Direct LLM benchmark evaluation confounds underlying model capability with prior task familiarity, while SFT-based train-before-test requires task-specific labeled training data.
Gbqu33OFyN.method: The authors propose two-stage test-time RL alignment (TTRA): first, single-sample RL aligns the model to the task format, and second, label-free test-time RL with majority-voting reward aligns it to the benchmark distribution without task-specific training sets.
Gbqu33OFyN.key_idea: Aligns models before benchmark testing using one-shot format RL followed by label-free majority-voting test-time RL to equalize task preparation without training labels.
Gbqu33OFyN.evidence: Evaluated across multiple LLM families (base and fine-tuned variants) on domain-specific benchmarks without training data and reasoning benchmarks (including HumanEval).
Gbqu33OFyN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that disentangling task familiarity from underlying capability in LLM benchmarks is an important evaluation question and find the convergence between base and fine-tuned models after TTRA striking.
Gbqu33OFyN.main_concern: All three reviewers caution that because TTRA updates model weights on benchmark questions via RL, improved scores cannot be cleanly attributed to correcting task familiarity rather than additional learning or benchmark adaptation.

zgl72xaYh7.one_liner: Enforces a non-conservative optimal transport dual consistency condition via coupled Newton updates in an O(NM) Sinkhorn-type solver.
zgl72xaYh7.problem: Classical optimal transport assumes mass conservation, whereas edge-dependent mass dissipation breaks the rank-one factorization that makes standard Sinkhorn efficient.
zgl72xaYh7.method: NC-Sinkhorn solves discrete non-conservative optimal transport with edge-dependent preservation maps and hard marginal constraints by enforcing a dual consistency condition through a coupled Newton step at O(NM) per-iteration cost. For structured preservation maps such as separable cost-aligned maps c = 1 - m, it reduces updates to an O(N + M) closed form.
zgl72xaYh7.key_idea: Enforces a dual consistency condition induced by edge-dependent mass loss using a coupled Newton projection step that preserves O(NM) per-iteration complexity.
zgl72xaYh7.evidence: Convergence proofs for exact column projections and safeguarded finite-Newton variants, an O(delta^-2) feasibility bound for a sequential variant, benchmarks up to N=5,000, and portfolio rebalancing and MoE routing applications.
zgl72xaYh7.claimed_gains: Achieves over 600x speedup versus LP solvers on benchmarks up to N=5,000.
zgl72xaYh7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the edge-dependent mass dissipation setting is well motivated and the O(NM) coupled Newton extension is practically efficient with broad experiments.
zgl72xaYh7.main_concern: Reviewers flag a discrepancy in the dual objective derivation and note that the convergence and complexity proofs do not directly cover the deployed finite-Newton algorithm or guarantee row feasibility at termination.

Gs0npN1ivF.one_liner: Benchmarks multi-step agent safety under user-specific consent graphs and adds a cross-task authorization memory (CAGMem).
Gs0npN1ivF.problem: Existing agent-safety benchmarks assume uniform platform rules while personalized-safety suites only judge final replies, missing intermediate privacy-sensitive steps that depend on per-user consent.
Gs0npN1ivF.method: PASCA represents each task as a multi-path graph whose edges are State-Purpose-Content-Action (SPCA) steps paired with per-user consent labels and a limited query budget. The paper also introduces CAGMem, an authorization memory storing Allow/Deny outcomes on coarse (role, data, purpose) triples for cross-task reuse.
Gs0npN1ivF.key_idea: Models tasks as multi-path graphs of recurring State-Purpose-Content-Action edges with per-user consent labels and caches coarse (role, data, purpose) authorization outcomes in CAGMem.
Gs0npN1ivF.evidence: Benchmark of 500 tasks across 100 user profiles with recurring SPCA steps and feasibility-aware metrics, compared conceptually against existing agent-safety suites.
Gs0npN1ivF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of combining per-step agent trajectories with user-specific consent and query budgets is well framed and practically relevant.
Gs0npN1ivF.main_concern: Reviewers question benchmark validity and diversity, citing unclear provenance of the 100 user profiles, only 15 templates with fixed 4-step topology, and incomplete audit reporting.

Fl3qMidQ7H.one_liner: Couples input-adaptive multi-expert wavelet decomposition with orthogonal-projection sparse attention and spectral cross-scale interaction for facial rPPG estimation.
Fl3qMidQ7H.problem: Remote photoplethysmography methods struggle to separate subtle pulse signals from motion and illumination interference across temporal scales when using mixed representations or fixed wavelet bases.
Fl3qMidQ7H.method: PhysWave adaptively combines multiple learnable wavelet experts at each decomposition level to split local video dynamics across temporal scales. It then models intra-component dependencies using sparse attention with a shared orthogonally initialized projection and learnable gating, and uses temporal spectra to guide cross-component feature exchange.
Fl3qMidQ7H.key_idea: Combines input-conditioned mixtures of learnable wavelet experts with gated orthogonal-projection sparse attention and spectrum-guided cross-scale feature interaction.
Fl3qMidQ7H.evidence: Intra-dataset, cross-dataset, and ablation experiments on five public rPPG benchmarks including UBFC-rPPG, PURE, BUAA, MMPD, and MR-NIRP-Car.
Fl3qMidQ7H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree PhysWave achieves strong empirical performance across diverse acquisition and transfer conditions, including illumination, motion, and driving datasets.
Fl3qMidQ7H.main_concern: Reviewers note missing ablation controls to isolate input-adaptive routing, ambiguous subject-disjoint split details with a reporting discrepancy, and insufficient positioning against prior wavelet and spectral attention work.

RTVMtjYD8j.one_liner: Explores Mixture-of-Experts routing space during RL via entropy-adapted candidate-pool perturbations and rollout-path replay.
RTVMtjYD8j.problem: RL post-training for MoE models relies mainly on token-level sampling for exploration, while direct routing perturbation activates unsuitable experts and degrades rollout quality.
RTVMtjYD8j.method: ESRL preserves high-confidence experts as anchors, restricts stochastic routing perturbations to a plausible candidate pool, and adapts perturbation strength using router entropy. To avoid routing mismatch during updates, it records the perturbed expert paths from rollouts and replays them during policy optimization.
RTVMtjYD8j.key_idea: Keeps top-confidence experts as anchors, applies router-entropy-scaled stochastic selection within a candidate pool, and replays recorded rollout expert paths during policy updates.
RTVMtjYD8j.evidence: Experiments across multiple MoE architectures, mathematical, science, and code benchmarks, baseline comparisons, and component ablations.
RTVMtjYD8j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree expert routing is an interesting exploration dimension beyond token sampling and that the multi-architecture experiments and ablations show promising gains.
RTVMtjYD8j.main_concern: Reviewers note limited technical novelty beyond combining routing noise with R3, missing post-training noise-disabled routing-load checks, and missing comparison with MoE-ERL.

PC7fX1lIEZ.one_liner: Automates aerial manipulation VLA demonstration generation in GPU simulation using payload-aware control, reusable RL policies, and expert task rules.
PC7fX1lIEZ.problem: Collecting demonstrations and evaluating Vision-Language-Action policies on physical aerial manipulators is costly, unsafe, and hard to scale due to coupled flight-manipulation dynamics.
PC7fX1lIEZ.method: AeroManip-VLA provides a GPU-accelerated parallel simulation benchmark with low-level payload-aware flight and manipulation control. It combines reusable RL policies with expert task rules and automated event labeling to generate grasping, placing, and long-horizon navigation-manipulation demonstrations without human teleoperation.
PC7fX1lIEZ.key_idea: Pairs a GPU-parallel aerial simulator with payload-aware flight control and hybrid RL plus rule-based experts to generate demonstrations automatically.
PC7fX1lIEZ.evidence: Payload-aware controller analysis, an 80K+ generated demonstration dataset across skills and task suites, and learned-policy evaluations on short-horizon Pick/Place tasks.
PC7fX1lIEZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper addresses a clear gap with a dedicated aerial VLA benchmark, a large-scale automated data pipeline, and a well-tested payload-aware controller.
PC7fX1lIEZ.main_concern: Reviewers note that quantitative learned-policy results cover only short-horizon tasks with no scaling curve or breakdown of data composition across RL, BC, and task types.

6NOzuabYdr.one_liner: Releases FILM, a 512-channel flexible-electrode intracortical dataset across 178 sessions and 277 days for calibration-free longitudinal motor decoding.
6NOzuabYdr.problem: Long-term decoding stability of high-channel-count flexible intracortical electrodes across days without recalibration remains insufficiently characterized.
6NOzuabYdr.method: FILM pairs spiking-band power (SBP) and threshold-crossing rate (TCR) features from 512-channel flexible intracortical arrays with synchronized 2D cursor kinematics from two nonhuman primates performing Center-Out and Random Target tasks across 178 sessions spanning up to 277 days. The authors also define a benchmark for long-term calibration-free cross-day decoder generalization.
6NOzuabYdr.key_idea: Provides 512-channel longitudinal flexible-electrode neural features (SBP and TCR) with synchronized 2D cursor kinematics across up to 277 days to benchmark frozen cross-day motor decoders.
6NOzuabYdr.evidence: 178 recording sessions across three subject-task subsets in two nonhuman primates, compared against a published Utah-array longitudinal dataset and evaluated with Wiener Filter and GRU baselines.
6NOzuabYdr.claimed_gains: Evaluated FILM recordings contain a median of 167 task-related channels versus 16 in a published longitudinal Utah-array dataset, with slower tuning drift and higher frozen cross-day decoding performance.
6NOzuabYdr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree FILM is a valuable, well-presented longitudinal neural recording resource combining high-channel-count flexible arrays, multi-area coverage, and standard NWB formatting.
6NOzuabYdr.main_concern: Reviewers question the incremental scientific contribution over existing longer-span datasets like LINK, noting limited decoder baselines, no spike sorting, and under-analyzed feature and anatomical comparisons.

DkJFXl2Rtg.one_liner: Identifies causal effects under unobserved confounding by regressing outcomes on treatments while adjusting for cross-environment conditional-expectation contrasts.
DkJFXl2Rtg.problem: Instrumental variable regression requires exogenous variation in the treatment distribution, failing when the treatment distribution is unchanged across environments.
DkJFXl2Rtg.method: Outstrumental Variable Regression (OVR) computes the conditional expectation of outcome Y given treatment X in each environment, forms a contrast vector of differences relative to a reference environment, and regresses Y on X while adjusting for the contrast and environment. Identification holds under an inclusion restriction (the contrast determines conditional confounding bias) and positivity.
DkJFXl2Rtg.key_idea: Constructs cross-environment differences in E[Y|X] as a contrast vector and adjusts for it in regression to remove unobserved confounding when outcome mechanisms vary.
DkJFXl2Rtg.evidence: Identification theorems, finite-sample consistency proofs under regularity conditions, and experiments on synthetic data and a real-world short-video recommendation dataset.
DkJFXl2Rtg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree using cross-environment variation in outcome mechanisms as a complement to instrumental variables is an original and clearly presented idea.
DkJFXl2Rtg.main_concern: Reviewers question the practical validity of the untestable inclusion restriction and invariant linear slope assumption, and note that the real-world recommendation experiment alters treatment policies rather than outcome mechanisms.

8HyrzEICxi.one_liner: Models overlapping historical word responses with a causal source-time FIR model (CAST-FIR) to separate temporal mixing from pre-onset neural prediction.
8HyrzEICxi.problem: LLM-based neural encoding studies interpret pre-onset lag-r correlation as brain next-word prediction, but overlapping responses to correlated historical words can create spurious pre-onset predictability.
8HyrzEICxi.method: The authors formalize temporal source mixing via a constrained-availability source-time finite impulse response model (CAST-FIR) and derive Target Isolation, a source-adjustment procedure that subtracts fitted historical-source contributions before measuring target-word encoding.
8HyrzEICxi.key_idea: Fits causal one-sided source-time FIR kernels (CAST-FIR) to historical words and subtracts their overlapping responses (Target Isolation) before evaluating target-aligned neural encoding.
8HyrzEICxi.evidence: A strictly causal simulation, a passive acoustic benchmark, and neural encoding analyses on English ECoG and Chinese SEEG datasets.
8HyrzEICxi.claimed_gains: Target Isolation contracts the r > 0.075 cross-onset temporal-generalization area by 98.1% in English ECoG and 100.0% in Chinese SEEG, with fitted kernels peaking at 75 ms and 225 ms after source onset.
8HyrzEICxi.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers agree the question of pre-onset encoding artifacts matters for neuroscience and appreciate the controlled synthetic experiments and reproducibility.
8HyrzEICxi.main_concern: Reviewers warn that CAST-FIR's one-sided causal kernel biases Target Isolation toward the null by absorbing true anticipatory activity into history kernels, and cite sparse related-work coverage.
